What happens after a city hosts the world? Miami is about to find out.

In 2026 the city hosted seven FIFA World Cup matches, including a quarterfinal and the bronze final. The city’s broader calendar also featured the College Football Playoff national championship game, the World Baseball Classic and the Formula 1 Miami Grand Prix.

open image in gallery In 2026 the city hosted seven FIFA World Cup matches, including a quarterfinal and the bronze final ( Getty Images )

The question now is whether this global exposure in 2026 will translate into sustained tourism demand in 2027.

As dean of one of the nation’s leading hospitality schools, I research trends affecting tourism, travel behavior and the hospitality industry in one of the country’s most international visitor markets. My work keeps me closely connected to industry leaders and destination partners across South Florida. Based on the latest economic indicators and South Florida’s calendar of major events, 2027 is shaping up to be a pivotal year for the area’s visitor economy.

Right now the data points to fewer domestic budget travelers but more – and higher-spending – international ones.

The fall of Spirit

Start with the biggest shock: the closure of Spirit Airlines in May 2026. The ultra-low-cost carrier headquartered in South Florida was the dominant airline at Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport for years. But in spring 2026, jet fuel prices roughly doubled amid the fuel crisis triggered by conflict in the Middle East, and when a hoped-for federal rescue fell through.

Only months earlier the airline had planned 100 peak daily departures from Fort Lauderdale in 2026. That capacity is now gone.

The consequences of this for 2027 fall unevenly. Ultra-low-cost carriers make their living on price-sensitive leisure travelers, such as the families and spontaneous weekenders who fill Florida hotel rooms in the shoulder seasons of April to May and September to November.

With Spirit’s seats gone and fuel costs pushing fares up across the airline industry, the cheapest tier of air travel to Florida has thinned considerably. Some of those trips will likely migrate to remaining carriers at higher fares. Others simply will not happen.

Then there are Florida residents, who accounted for about 9.1 million visits to Greater Miami in 2025, including 4.8 million overnight visitors and 4.3 million day-trippers. This segment is best insulated from the airline price shock, which will help 2027 visitation.

open image in gallery Then there are Florida residents, who accounted for about 9.1 million visits to Greater Miami in 2025 ( Getty Images )

International travel

Even before the latest concerns about fuel prices and Spirit Airlines’ closure, Greater Miami’s international market was inconsistent. In 2025 the area’s international visitation declined 2.8% to about 6.26 million total international travelers.

Overnight visitors from Colombia, Brazil and Canada decreased, for a loss of roughly 75,000 visitors compared to 2024. Growth from the U.K., Italy and Argentina nearly offset that loss, adding about 73,000 visitors combined, but those gains were not enough to reverse the overall decline in international visitation.

This matters because international visitors tend to punch above their weight economically. In Greater Miami they accounted for roughly US$7.2 billion in spending in 2025, about 5% more than the prior year, even as total international visitation dipped 2.8%. This suggests people are staying longer and spending more.

Early 2026 showed signs of a rebound from that dip. U.S. inbound international travel fell 5.5% in 2025, and early 2026 has been uneven nationally. But Florida’s gateways remain a bright spot: In the first quarter of 2026, Miami, Orlando and Tampa together processed about 1.59 million international arrivals; 1.13 million of those arrivals were to Miami International Airport alone. Meanwhile, JFK and Newark airports welcomed slightly more overseas arrivals at 1.15 million, but this is down 7% from the first quarter of 2025 for those destinations.

Carrying the momentum forward

Early media research suggests that the World Cup may help carry Greater Miami’s tourism momentum into 2027. The Miami Host Committee reported that the FIFA Fan Festival Miami drew more than 600,000 fans over 24 days at Bayfront Park, alongside more than 70 match broadcasts, 1,000 performers, dozens of food and beverage vendors and family-friendly activities.

If they had a good time, the more than 64,000 fans who attended these matches may plan a return trip to Miami. Still, 2027 has no World Cup, no CFP championship, no World Baseball Classic.

But the calendar is not empty – it’s simply different. Miami Beach is hosting the Professional Convention Management Association Convening Leaders in January 2027, effectively giving thousands of the world’s meeting planners a chance to experience Miami’s beaches, nightlife and cultural amenities.

The convention pipeline behind this event is unusually strong: Adobe’s Creativity Conference, the iConnections Global Alts investor gathering, Unleash America and a Nike national tournament are already contracted for the 2027 fiscal year. And Amazon, WordPress and Boston Consulting Group events are currently in advanced negotiation.

Plus, recurring anchor events such as the Miami Open, Formula 1 Grand Prix, Art Basel and the South Beach Wine and Food Festival will continue.

The Grand Hyatt Miami Beach, the Miami Beach Convention Center’s long-awaited 800-room headquarters hotel, is scheduled to open in November 2027. This structural addition will outlast any single event.

In short, 2027’s demand skews away from one-off spectacle and toward business events, group travel and repeat leisure.

The price is right

Pricing is the wild card, and the freshest data shows why hotel performance depends not only on how many rooms are booked but on how much travelers are willing to pay for them.

Through May 2026, Miami-Dade led all top 25 U.S. hotel markets in occupancy at nearly 80%, while posting the nation’s highest average daily rate at $293.67, up 11.2% in a year.

Preliminary data on hotel stays for the week ending June 27, 2026, shows Miami’s average daily rate is up 51.1% year over year, and revenue per available room is up 51.6%. Occupancy was relatively flat at 73.5%, underscoring that the World Cup effect was driven more by pricing power than by fuller hotels.

The 2027 forecast

The question now is whether any of that pricing power persists once the event calendar normalizes, especially if airfares stay high and price-sensitive visitors stay home.

My reading of the data is that headline visitor counts in 2027 may be roughly flat, perhaps even down modestly in the domestic budget segment. Meanwhile, I think visitor spending will prove more resilient, because the mix shifts toward international, group and drive-market travelers who stay longer or cost less to reach.

Several early indicators will demonstrate whether this forecast is correct. I will be looking at how quickly airlines backfill Fort Lauderdale’s lost seats, along with how quickly the prices of jet fuel and airfare normalizes. It will also be important to watch whether the first quarter surges from Canada and Mexico persist through this winter and whether Latin American demand, still Florida’s international backbone, recovers from its 2025 dip.

About the author Michael ChengDean and Professor of Hospitality Management, Florida International University. This article was first published by The Conversation and is republished under a Creative Commons licence. Read the original article.

A stronger dollar can make Florida more expensive for overseas visitors, while concerns about visa delays and U.S. border procedures can affect whether travelers choose Florida or competing destinations elsewhere.

But research on destination loyalty consistently shows that repeat visitation follows satisfaction with the total experience rather than any single attraction. Millions of first-time World Cup visitors have formed that impression in 2026.

Miami business owners can’t set fuel prices or exchange rates, but they can determine whether the people who came for the world’s biggest sporting event find a reason to come back on their own in 2027.

News.title: Car insurance is highest in these 5 states - but drivers are about to get a win
News.content:
There are five states where car insurance premiums will cost drivers a median of $2,676 a year or more, a new study has found.

Louisiana is home to the highest annual median rate in the nation at $3,342, according to an analysis published Monday by insurance marketplace The Zebra.

Residents of Louisiana will spend 5.1 percent of their yearly income on car insurance, more than twice the national average of 2.69 percent.

Nationally, the median annual car insurance rate was $2,079 - up from $1,933 in 2025, according to The Zebra.

While the national median rate ticked up in 2026, the analysis had some good news for consumers. Insurance rates are coming down, or rising only slightly, in many states because insurance companies are paying out less on claims than they bring in from premiums.

open image in gallery Car insurance rates have shot up over the past five years due to a variety of factors, including inflation, tech advancements and lawsuits ( AFP/Getty )

“This has now led to a hyper-competitive environment amongst insurance companies,” The Zebra CCO said in a statement. “They are spending a ton on marketing and dropping rates to stay competitive.”

Florida, the second most expensive state for car insurance, saw its median premium drop more than any other state in America: $353.50.

After Louisiana and Florida, Colorado ($2,905), Maryland ($2,800) and New Jersey ($2,676) had the highest median rates.

Meanwhile, Vermont ($1,398), Wyoming ($1,344) and North Carolina ($1,304) had the lowest median annual car insurance rates.

Car insurance rates have climbed drastically over the past five years. The average rate to insurance a car for a year was $1,483, according to a 2021 analysis from The Zebra. That number rose nearly $800 by 2026.

Several factors have contributed to the rise, according to a June panel discussion about car insurance at nonpartisan think tank Brookings Center on Regulation and Markets.

open image in gallery Louisiana, a state prone to flooding and hurricanes, has the highest median insurance rates in the nation ( Getty )

Experts said part of the blame falls on the complexity of modern cars. Vehicles are more “technologically sophisticated” nowadays, which means replacing items damaged in car accident is more expensive.

Inflation has played a role in higher replacement costs over the past five years, too - parts are nearly 30 percent higher.

“Inflation has exacerbated these impacts, with auto replacement costs up 28 percent from 2021 to 2025,” noted the Insurance Information Institute, whose CCO was on the Brookings panel.

Other causes of higher raters included “rampant” lawsuits against insurance companies, the institute said, and insurers raising rates to catch up to lost revenue when states froze rates during the pandemic.

News.title: US on track to have historically low number of homicides in 2026
News.content:

Homicide rates across 30 major American cities have seen an 18% decrease this year compared to the same period in 2025, translating to approximately 215 fewer killings, according to a new report from the independent Council on Criminal Justice.

Should this positive trend continue, the nation could see its annual homicide rate fall to the lowest levels in over a century once final figures are compiled at year-end.

The report, released on Thursday, tracked 13 distinct crime categories, revealing declines in nine of them. These included significant drops in carjackings, residential burglaries and aggravated assaults. However, the study noted slight increases in shoplifting, domestic violence incidents, sexual assaults and drug offenses during the same 2025-2026 period.

Experts suggest these broadly positive shifts are surpassing expectations, pushing crime rates below baseline levels observed before 2020 and the Covid-19 pandemic, which had triggered historic surges in violence. While both Democrats and Republicans nationwide have sought to claim credit for these improvements in a competitive midterm election year, the report indicates that these trends are consistent across cities with diverse political leadership.

Adam Gelb, president and CEO of the Council on Criminal Justice, a nonpartisan think tank focused on criminal justice policy and research, stated that this suggests the most significant contributing factors are operating nationwide rather than being tied to specific local public safety initiatives.

open image in gallery Beyond the overall reduction in violent crime, the report also highlighted a 23% drop in the lethality of crimes committed, measured by the proportion of serious violent crimes that result in fatalities ( Getty Images )

"Murder and other crime rates are falling across the map in cities with different political leadership, different housing and economic conditions, different policing and prosecution and violence reduction strategies and different levels of federal enforcement activity," Gelb said.

Beyond the overall reduction in violent crime, the report also highlighted a 23% drop in the lethality of crimes committed, measured by the proportion of serious violent crimes that result in fatalities. Non-violent crimes also largely declined, with residential burglaries falling 13% year-over-year and a substantial 50% decrease compared to pre-pandemic levels in 2019. Shoplifting, however, bucked this trend with a 5% increase, and while drug offenses saw a small rise, they remained below pre-pandemic figures.

Despite the widespread improvements, roughly a third of the 30 sampled cities experienced an increase in deadly violence from the first half of 2025 to the same period in 2026. This included Norfolk, Virginia, which saw a 64% rise in homicides, and San Francisco, with a 55% increase. A smaller number of cities, specifically Norfolk, Austin, Pittsburgh, and Minneapolis, recorded more homicides in 2026 than in the corresponding period in 2019.

John Roman, director of the Center on Public Safety and Justice at the National Opinion Research Center from the University of Chicago, said various factors can influence why certain locations see crime increases or decreases. Roman noted that conservative politicians affiliated with President Donald Trump might attribute success to intensified immigration crackdowns and National Guard deployments in cities like Los Angeles and Memphis. In contrast, liberal politicians might point to President Joe Biden's public safety legislation, which strengthened background checks on firearm sales.

Ultimately, Roman argued, the most compelling explanations transcend specific administrations. These include a decrease in drug usage, leading to fewer purchases from illegal markets often linked to violence, and an influx of federal funding for localities post-pandemic, which was invested in social programming. These programs, Roman added, frequently funded positions like teachers and social workers who primarily engage with "young people who are the highest risk of violence and victimization."

While both Gelb and Roman agreed there isn't a single cause for the decline, Gelb emphasized the importance of studying these outcomes for future insights and celebrating the current success.

"This is one of the most significant public safety developments in decades. It means lives are being saved, families are spared trauma and communities are regaining stability," Gelb said.

Tens of thousands of people have been forced to evacuate as another extreme heatwave moves across Sicily, Spain, France and other parts of southern Europe, igniting wildfires as temperatures exceed 44C.

Footage shows vast infernos sweeping through the island as dramatic fires scorched the Sicilian hills around Bivona in the central Agrigento province, while the capital of Palermo suffered blackouts.

In southwest France, more than 20,000 people have been evacuated near Bordeaux, officials said, as some 700 firefighters were called out to tackle the blaze near the popular coastal town of Lege Cap-Ferret.

It comes as Wales is the first UK region to officially declare a drought amid record dry conditions, intense heatwaves, wildfires and dwindling rivers. Across Europe, extreme heat supercharged by climate change has been sucking European soils dry, as warmer air pulls moisture from soil and rivers.

Greece was also sweltering under what was forecast to be the last of a four-day heatwave. Temperatures topped 42C, while several regions in southern and central Greece, including the wider Athens area, were on the highest alert level for wildfire danger. Cyprus, meanwhile, issued a warning for high temperatures expected to reach 43C.

Near Bordeaux, two firefighters were killed earlier this week while battling a blaze near the city’s airport.

“Overnight, the fire spread more quickly than we had imagined,” acknowledged Philippe de Gonneville, the mayor of Lège-Cap Ferret. Authorities said 12,000 have already been evacuated, while around 8,800 are being moved.

open image in gallery Vast flames engulfed France’s southeastern forests near Contignac ( AFP/Getty )

In neighbouring Spain, authorities were still working to put out fires which have raged for several days. Spain's railway infrastructure operator Adif said train traffic between Mejorada del Campo and Alcalá de Henares, near Madrid, had been suspended due to a wildfire close to the tracks.

Across central Spain, firefighters, emergency personnel and military units remained deployed as authorities monitored multiple active fires, including blazes in Guadalajara, Toledo, Ciudad Real and Albacete.

Spain’s meteorological agency warned of “extraordinary danger” with temperatures of up to 44C on Thursday in some regions. Popular Spanish tourist spots, including the areas around Malaga, Valencia and Alicante, could see temperatures reach as high as 42C.

The disruption affected services on the high-speed rail line linking Madrid and Barcelona, one of the country's busiest transport corridors.

More than 100,000 hectares have burned nationwide so far this year.

open image in gallery In Avila, Spain, wildfires spread across the Burgohondo mountains ( Reuters )

Meanwhile in Italy, a 59-year-old firefighter died after falling ill while battling a large wildfire near San Cataldo in Sicily.

The central areas of Cammarata, Santo Stefana Quisquina and Bivona suffered some of the worst impact of the islands huge wildfires, with health clinics evacuated, phone lines down, roads closed and farmland destroyed as residents helped authorities battle the flames.

More than 100 people were forced to evacuate from homes and clinics on the island, according to local media, as dozens of wildfires strained emergency services battling against fires that threatened rural areas, residential districts, and major public roads.

open image in gallery Le Porge, southwestern France, where a fast-moving blaze has burned 900 hectares north of Arcachon Bay ( AFP/Getty )

Temperatures in inland Sicily exceeded 40C on Wednesday for the second day running, reaching 43 C according to forecaster Ventusky.

On Thursday, the mercury dropped into the mid-30C across most of the island, with some central-northern areas reaching the high 30C. On Friday, the warmest temperatures will move southwards, before the entire island cools down to the low 30C on the weekend.

Farmer Marco Barbaccia told how a wind-fuelled wildfire destroyed olive groves, wiping out this year's crop and damaging trees needed for future harvests.

"We were unable to save anything. We lost both this year's harvest and the trees themselves, which means losing future production of Sicilian extra-virgin olive oil as well," Mr Barbaccia said.

Italian newspaper La Repubblica reported that families had barricaded themselves in their homes to keep the smoke out.

"The heat was so intense that railings and doorknobs became red-hot,” the paper wrote. “Smoke engulfed several neighbourhoods, and by 4am temperatures in the city exceeded 40C."

Elsewhere in Europe, firefighters struggled on Tuesday to contain Spain's largest wildfire of the year, while two firefighters were killed battling a fire in southwestern France, as an extreme heatwave continued to fuel dangerous conditions across Europe, bringing drought and forecasts of severe hailstorms.

open image in gallery A wildfire in Sagana in the territory of Monreale, Sicily ( AFP/Getty )

In mainland Italy, temperatures have remained in the high 20C and low 30C, while on the island of Sardinia, they neared 40C on Wednesday. Sardinia will remain in the low-to-mid 30C for the rest of the week, with temperatures in mainland Italy around average for this time of year for the rest of the week.

The fires in Sicily, which were fueled by strong sirocco winds – those blowing northward from the Sahara into southern Europe – reached the western-central town of Santo Stefano Quisquina in the Agrigento province overnight into Wednesday.

The province of Palermo, Sicily’s capital, also battled dozens of fires damaging rural homes and businesses, forcing the temporary closure of the SS186 state road, and disrupting traffic on the Palermo-Catania motorway.

A health clinic, oxygen depot, fuel station and fireworks factory are all under surveillance by firefighters and other authorities, according to local media. Some 22 patients were evacuated from the Ignazio Attardi clinic as a precaution.

In Bivona, a wildfire emergency has caused damage to the water pipes, with emergency systems kicking into response, mayor Milko Cina said. The TIM telephone line was also put out of service in the area.

He added that the situation is “improving” after authorities had to “evacuate all the houses along the state road between Bivona and Santo Stefano”.

Residents of the area helped put out fires since the early hours of Wednesday, Mr Cina said.

open image in gallery A forest fire near Bordeaux ( Reuters )

“Heartfelt thanks in particular to the many farmers who, with their excavators, shovels, tractors and their water-filled barrels, are still on site helping the population,” Mr Cina said. Farms and livestock farms have been damaged by the fires.

But he added that the situation is “improving” after authorities had to “evacuate all the houses along the state road between Bivona and Santo Stefano”

Although wildfires are not new to the region, scientists say they are becoming more frequent and intense as a result of stronger and longer heatwaves and droughts, due to the climate crisis.

News.title: Poker champ robbed of Vegas tournament winnings by thieves who stacked dishes on back to keep him still
News.content:

Read our Privacy notice

A professional poker player was tackled, hog-tied and robbed at a Las Vegas rental property shortly after withdrawing tens of thousands of dollars in tournament prize money, according to a Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department report.

The victim, Jared Griener, was staying at an Airbnb near Vegas Drive and Buffalo Drive on July 12 when two unidentified men forced their way in. According to police documents, the intruders restrained Griener and demanded he reveal the location of his backpack, which contained approximately $45,000 in cash and $1,000 sunglasses.

During the robbery, the suspects placed dishes on Griener's back and warned him that the items would shatter if he attempted to move, as reported by NBC affiliate KSNV.

Griener told police he waited until the house fell silent for several minutes before loosening his restraints enough to escape. Ring camera footage obtained by the outlet showed him knocking on a neighboring door for help, barefoot and still partially bound with duct tape. A second neighbor eventually called 911.

He later provided further details to the Las Vegas Review-Journal regarding how the break-in occurred.

open image in gallery Professional poker player Jared Griener was robbed of $60,000 in cash and personal items at a Las Vegas rental property on July 12, according to police ( Getty )

According to Griener, he returned to the rental on July 12 after cashing out roughly $60,000 from his World Series of Poker account. The California native, who has built up more than $3.3 million in career tournament earnings, said two men were already waiting inside when he unlocked the front door and tackled him as soon as he stepped through.

He noted there was no sign of forced entry, leaving him convinced the men knew his schedule and came specifically for him. The intruders grabbed his phone and threatened his life while demanding his backpack.

“I begged them to take whatever they wanted and leave and to please let me live,” Griener later shared in a social media post describing the encounter.

When Griener told them the bag was in his car, they took his keys to retrieve the money, headphones and other belongings, but left the vehicle and his phone behind.

Before fleeing, the men used duct tape found in the house to bind his wrists behind his back and tie his ankles to his hands. Once the intruders left, Griener managed to break free and seek assistance outside.

“I was so afraid that they were still at the house, so I just sprinted outside and banged on the neighbor’s door who looked like they were home,” he told the Las Vegas Review-Journal. “They didn’t answer.”

Griener said he sustained minor soreness during the tackle but did not need hospital treatment, though paramedics had to help him cut away the remaining tape when they arrived.

The Las Vegas Metropolitan Police Department confirmed officers searched the home for fingerprints and that an active robbery investigation was underway. No arrests have been made.

An Airbnb spokesperson told the Las Vegas Review-Journal that the company fully refunded Griener’s stay and was cooperating with law enforcement.

The Independent has contacted Airbnb for comment.

Anthony Joshua side-stepped talk of Tyson Fury before his fight with Kristian Prenga, but knows he cannot “conquer the universe” without victory in Jeddah on Saturday night.

Former two-time world heavyweight champion Joshua will return to the ring in Saudi Arabia a day after long-standing rival Fury takes on Mariusz Wach in Thailand on Friday.

Both Fury’s bout with Wach and Joshua’s contest with little-known Albanian Prenga are viewed as tune-up fights before an all-British blockbuster battle later in 2026, which is expected to be hosted at Wembley.

open image in gallery Anthony Joshua is back in action on Saturday (John Walton/PA) ( PA Wire )

However, Joshua refused to overlook his 35-year-old opponent during Thursday’s press conference, he said: “Look, respect my opponent here.

“We don’t want to talk about Tyson Fury. Respectfully, I have done all the media that I can about what the future holds but you know our focus is him and his team.

“We have been working since January, working hard, keeping my head down, aligned all my stars and I am fully focused.

“I understand there is a big picture. The goal is to conquer the universe, right? But first we must conquer earth. My target is here.”

This is Joshua’s first fight since he stopped YouTuber-turned-boxer Jake Paul in Miami last December before days later the British heavyweight was involved in a car crash in Nigeria which killed close friends Latif ‘Latz’ Ayodele and Sina Ghami.

At that point Joshua’s career hinged in the balance with speculation the 36-year-old may never box again, but after a period of grief, he returned to the gym and an agreement was finally reached to fight Fury, but only after a warm-up with Prenga was pencilled in beforehand.

open image in gallery Tyson Fury lurks in the backdrop to Joshua’s fight (Peter Byrne/PA) ( PA Wire )

“When you speak to me about what may lay ahead or I sit down in an office with Eddie (Hearn) and he presents to me what may lay ahead, it is a great opportunity for me to understand where this checkpoint takes me and what it leads me on to,” Joshua said.

“The reality of the matter is there is no universe, there is no future unless I get past this checkpoint on Saturday night.”

Prenga has produced 20 knockouts but campaigned well below the level of Joshua and this will be the biggest occasion of his career.

“I work all my life for this, I waited all my life for this and I hope I am going to show the world on Saturday who I am,” Prenga said.

“I respect Anthony Joshua very much, I grew up watching all his fights and I have seen his weakness, I have seen what he does best and I will show exactly what I have paid attention to.”

Asked how it will finish, Prenga said: “I’m just going to say it short, knock-out.”

Stunt performer Devyn Dalton has offered insight into her acclaimed performance doubling for Matt Damon in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey.

The 34-year-old’s involvement in the film was recently praised by Damon, who described Dalton as having “the greatest arms I’ve ever seen.”

The 4-foot-5-inch actor faces off against 7-foot-tall stunt performers playing giants in one of the film’s most memorable sequences. The scene also features on a promotional poster for the blockbuster retelling of Homer’s epic Greek poem.

Speaking to the New York Post, Dalton described the use of “forced perspective” in her scenes as “movie magic.”

Dalton has been performing in stunt roles since 2011’s Rise of the Planet of the Apes, and maintains a strict regime of yoga, weight training, boxing and weapon work because she never knows when she might get asked to join a production.

open image in gallery Devyn Dalton is a 34-year-old stunt performer who made her debut in 2011’s ‘Rise of the Planet of the Apes’ ( Instagram/@devyn.dalton )

open image in gallery Dalton after undergoing her transformation into Odysseus for Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ ( Instagram/@devyn.dalton )

“Physically, I’m always ready to go because you get the phone call and have to be ready,” said Dalton. “Sometimes you only get a week’s notice.”

She added that her role in The Odyssey had come after years of building relationships in Hollywood, explaining: “Opportunities like this come from building trust and [having] a strong reputation in the industry. It doesn’t just happen overnight. It takes so long and I spent my entire career [preparing] for this.”

Dalton also thanked Damon for giving her credit for her role in bringing Odysseus to the screen, saying: “I’m so overwhelmed that he gave a shoutout into how it works. It’s about time more information comes out about this.”

open image in gallery Dalton appears on this poster for Nolan’s epic version of ‘The Odyssey’ ( Universal Pictures )

She added that stunt work is often perceived to be a male profession, and asked: “They often say ‘stuntman’, but what about stuntwomen? It’s been a really long journey paving the way... There’s been a lot of women who have opened the doors, but it’s an ongoing battle always. I hope to continue to pave the way for that.”

Speaking on the Happy Sad Confused podcast earlier this week, Damon explained how stunt doubles were used for the scenes involving the Laestrygonians, a race of giant cannibals.

“There were these stuntmen who were all seven feet and then they got stunt men who were under five feet,” said Damon. “My double was a woman, a female stunt performer who had the greatest arms I’ve ever seen.”

He continued: “There are those shots where you see these giants looming over me. It was almost 100 per cent my arms in the movie, but you got to give it up where it’s due.”

News.title: Ebola death toll passes 1,000 as outbreak shows no signs of slowing
News.content:
More than 1,000 people have now died in the outbreak of Ebola in the Congo, as medics struggle to curb the fastest-growing epidemic of the virus.

Dozens of deaths are being recorded each day and modelling has forecast that, in a worst case scenario, it could become the worst Ebola outbreak in history.

The outbreak, centred on the north east of Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), passed the four-figure death milestone little more than two months after it was first declared.

By contrast, the worst outbreak of the haemorrhagic fever on record, which struck West Africa from 2014 to 2016, took eight months from the first case to reach 1,000 deaths. It went on to kill 11,000 people.

The latest figures from the DRC’s national public health institute show 2,536 confirmed Ebola cases and 1,033 deaths, with at least 738 patients in isolation or hospitalised.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

Sports.title: Arsenal preparing £70MILLION transfer bid for Bruno Guimaraes after star, 28, told Newcastle he wants to join Gunners

The Gunners want to sign a new midfielder this summer and the Brazilian is their prime target.



Newcastle are adamant that they do not want to sell their skipper this summer, but Arsenal are set to test their resolve with an offer of £70m.

Talks through intermediaries had previously suggested the Premier League champions were willing to cough up around £60m.



Guimaraes has informed the Magpies of his desire to move to the Emirates and talks are expected to accelerate this week.

Arsenal missed out on the signing of Morgan Rogers, though, who joined Chelsea for £117m.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford hit with another brutal snub as Barcelona sign Champions League star after £70m Anthony Gordon transfer
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED outcast Marcus Rashford’s hopes of sealing a quickfire return to Barcelona are all but over.

The Spanish heavyweights brutally snubbed the chance to trigger a £26million option to sign the England forward, 28, permanently following a stunning loan spell last season.



Barcelona splashed the cash to land Rashford’s Three Lions team-mate Anthony Gordon instead.

But he was still desperate for the five-time Champions League winners to come back in for him following the World Cup.



Those dreams appear to have shattered after Barcelona have now completed the signing of Karim Adeyemi from Borussia Dortmund.

The German’s arrival at the Nou Camp means chief Hansi Flick is well stocked on the flanks.

Rashford turned down lucrative offers and saw his £40m release clause expire as he held out for a possible move back to Barcelona.

He notched 14 goals and as many assists during a temporary stint which saw him bag the LaLiga title and Supercopa de Espana last season.

But United have still been planning to sell Rashford before jetting off to Ireland for their pre-season training camp next month.

And there is uncertainty over whether the Red Devils would be prepared to sanction another loan exit.

Old Trafford chief Michael Carrick has refused to rule out giving Rashford another chance to reignite his United career if a suitable offer is not tabled.

The former Aston Villa loanee has made 426 appearances for his boyhood club, bagging 138 goals along the way.

Adeyemi, 24, admitted he was shocked when Barcelona came calling for his signature.

He said: “I couldn’t believe it to be honest because I know what I can do and the last season was not the best.

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson takes huge dig at Man Utd as England World Cup star reveals why he joined Man City in £116m transfer
Sports.content:
ELLIOT ANDERSON believes he is joining the ‘Kings of Manchester’ after opting for a move to City – despite interest from United.

The Red Devils were tracking the England ace in recent months as Michael Carrick looked to revamp his midfield.



However it became clear the former Nottingham Forest man favoured a move to the Etihad and a £116million fee was agreed.

The deal was done during the World Cup but Anderson headed to the North West to officially signed his five year contract – worth around £300,000 per week.



Asked why he chose City, Anderson said: “They’re winners, they’re relentless. And that’s the sort of team I want to be a part of – champions and people who win trophies.

“Over the last 10, 12 years, they’ve dominated, so that’s why I wanted to join.



“They are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing – so strong in every position.

“As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make the move happen.”

Anderson has signed a deal which keeps him at the Etihad until 2031 with the option of a further 12 months at the end of it.

He will get an early chance to see what he turned his back on when his new team-mates travel to Old Trafford on September 13.

Sports.title: Premier League owner reveals club’s entire transfer plans on Twitter in unprecedented move after ‘false rumours’
Sports.content:
HULL CITY owner Acun Ilicali has bizarrely taken to social media to clarify the club’s transfer business.

The Tigers are back in the Premier League for the first time in nine years and want to add to their squad this summer.



Hull have made three signings so far, bringing in defender Matt Targett, goalkeeper Jack Butland and midfielder Oscar Zambrano.

But Ilicali is “disturbed” and unhappy by media reports that Hull have been rejected for other targets.



The Hull owner therefore took the unique approach yesterday (THU) of posting a cryptic shortlist on social media of the club’s transfer targets.

Butland, Targett and Zambrano were all listed with a green tick by them, but underneath were 11 unnamed players.

Ilicali used flag emojis and percentages as clues for fans, with several matching of them players that Hull are after.

Target No4 was listed as a Japan flag with 99 per cent by it and is likely a nod to midfielder Hidemasa Morita being set to join as a free agent.

There was also a Greek flag that indicated a huge deal is “90%” done – and that is surely for Olympiacos’ highly-rated goalkeeper Konstantis Tzolakis, who SunSport understands is set to move to the MKM Stadium for £17m once his club find a new No1.

Posting on X, formerly known as Twitter, Ilicali wrote: “We are reading dozens of false transfer rumors in many places.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“We are disturbed by the claims that we have been rejected and by the use of our club’s name to gain attention.

“We have been working intensively for two months. I believe we will build a team that we will all be proud of.

“To prevent false speculation and to give you more information, I am leaving you with our latest transfer situation, which includes some clues.”

Sports.title: Topless Vinicius Jr’s girlfriend shows off tanlines while covering up in bed after World Cup star undergoes chin surgery
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN influencer Virginia Fonseca has given fans another glimpse into her reunion with partner Vinicius Jr after sharing a cosy late-night update from bed.

The social media star, who boasts more than 56 million Instagram followers, posted a video to her Instagram Story tucked beneath a blue blanket while showing off the tan lines she picked up during her recent holiday with the Real Madrid superstar.



Virginia appeared makeup-free as she relaxed for the evening and wished her followers goodnight after spending time in Brazil.

She wrote alongside the clip: “Amo voce e ate daqui a pouco se Deus quiser,” which translates as: “I love you, and see you soon, God willing.”



That caption was accompanied by the words: “I’m already here, all ready to go to sleep. So, good night to you all. Sleep with God’s blessing. I love you all. Thank you for everything, always, and I’ll see you again very soon, God willing. Kiss.”

Earlier stories showed Virginia enjoying time in São Gonçalo – Vinicius Jr’s hometown in Rio de Janeiro – including snaps of the pair partying together.

The posts came after the couple appeared to rekindle their romance following a brief split before the World Cup.

Virginia had previously revealed they had gone their separate ways, but the pair have since been pictured together again, embracing as she officially opened a new gym.

Their reunion also comes after Vinicius underwent cosmetic surgery immediately following the World Cup, where Brazil‘s campaign ended in the last 16 following a 2-1 defeat to Norway.

The 26-year-old forward was pictured with dermatologist Dr Alessandro Alarcao after the procedure, with his chin appearing noticeably more defined than before.



While the exact cost of the treatment has not been disclosed, similar cosmetic procedures in the UK can range anywhere from around £3,000 to more than £14,000 depending on the type of surgery performed.

Vinicius joined Real Madrid from Flamengo in 2018 after progressing through the Brazilian club’s academy.

Since arriving in Spain, he has made 375 appearances for Los Blancos, scoring 128 goals and establishing himself as one of world football’s biggest stars.



He will now begin a new chapter under Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid, with the pair hoping to put behind them the controversy surrounding last season’s Champions League clash against Benfica.

During that tie, Benfica midfielder Gianluca Prestianni was accused of abusing Vinicius after the Brazilian scored a stunning winner in Lisbon, although the player was later handed a six-match ban for homophobic conduct after investigations concluded he allegedly used the Spanish slur “maricón” rather than the initially reported racist term.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho defended his own players while insisting Vinicius had played a part in the confrontation.

He said: “These talents are able to do these beautiful things, but unfortunately was not just happy to score that astonishing goal. When you score a goal like that, you celebrate in a respectful way.”

Now, with both back at Real Madrid, Mourinho and Vinicius will look to leave the controversy behind as they prepare for the new campaign, with the Portuguese coach aiming to recreate the success he enjoyed when he famously toppled Pep Guardiola’s Barcelona during the 2011/12 LaLiga season.

Sports.title: Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges
Sports.content:
Man Utd given green light for Aurelien Tchouameni transfer as Real Madrid stance emerges

Manchester United are interested in signing Aurelien Tchouameni from Real Madrid, lodging an enquiry as they bid to revamp their midfield in the summer transfer window

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni is a target for Manchester United (Image: Stephen Nadler/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Real Madrid are open to selling Aurelien Tchouameni in a major boost to Manchester United's chances of signing him. Tchouameni, 26, has just got back from helping France reach the semi-finals of the World Cup, playing an integral role in Didier Deschamps' side.

‌



But throughout the tournament, his future at club level was a hot topic. United have a long-standing interest in Tchouameni, who Real boss Jose Mourinho initially planned to keep after returning to the Bernabeu this summer.

‌



However, the Sun report that Real are now prepared to let the midfielder go at the right price. The La Liga giants have been linked with a big-money move for Manchester City star Rodri and might need to drum up funds.

‌



United's interest is said to have ramped up since the World Cup ended, with Tchouameni out of contract in 2028. It was reported in Spain earlier this month that Real and the Frenchman had agreed a new five-year deal, although there's been no confirmation.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

United have already signed two midfielders this summer, paying a combined £85m for Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos. But with Manuel Ugarte expected to miss most of the season because of a serious knee injury, the Red Devils want to add a third.

‌



Their search for a specialist defensive midfielder has led them to Tchouameni, whose experience of starting the 2022 World Cup final and winning the Champions League in 2024 appeals to United. The former Monaco star also suits United's preferred age range for signings - between 22 and 26.

How much should Manchester United pay for Aurelien Tchouameni? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Aurelien Tchouameni's contract with Real Madrid expires in 2028 (Image: Marcel Bonte/Soccrates/Getty Images)

‌



Real's pursuit of Rodri could therefore prove to be a double boost for United, as local rivals City would be losing one of their best players. However, Los Blancos could wait until Rodri's contract expires next summer and sign him on a free.

As for Tchouameni, ex-Real midfielder and French compatriot Claude Makelele has warned Bernabeu chiefs not to sell him. Makelele told DAZN: "He was the only player who performed consistently from start to finish.

"Mourinho isn't a fool; he's a good manager, one of the best managers. He knows he's going to need a strong squad to be able to win La Liga."

Sports.title: Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance
Sports.content:
Arsenal to launch £70m Bruno Guimaraes bid - but transfer for Newcastle star hangs in balance

Bruno Guimaraes has emerged as a top target for Arsenal this summer in their search for quality reinforcements and they are ready to pay out £70million to sign him

View 2 Images Arsenal want to sign Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle (Image: Getty )

Arsenal are poised to table a £70million bid for Bruno Guimaraes - but will not overpay for the midfielder if Newcastle try to resist a sale.

‌



The Gunners are in the market for quality additions to bolster the squad that won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final last season. And a move for Guimaraes, who boasts extensive top-flight pedigree, appeals in their search for an elite midfielder.

‌



Guimaraes, 28, is known to be keen on the move, which would give him a realistic opportunity to win major trophies.

‌



Newcastle, though, have no appetite to cash in on their talismanic captain — and it remains to be seen if a financial package in the region of £70m would realistically be enough for them to soften that stance.

BBC Sport report that Arsenal are ready to launch an official bid of that amount after stepping up their interest in Guimaraes. However, it's noted that they will not stray from their valuation of the Brazilian.

Whether or not they would consider bidding higher for a player who turns 29 later this year remains to be seen. And if that is the case, then they could opt to move on to other targets.

‌



That stance saw them miss out on a deal for Morgan Rogers, a long-term target who was viewed as the ceiling-raiser signing Arsenal were looking for in their search for a new left-sided attacker.

View 2 Images Bruno Guimaraes wants to join Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

The Gunners valued Rogers at £80m; a figure far lower than Aston Villa's valuation of the England star. That gulf in valuations opened the door for Chelsea to swoop in with a £117m offer. Arsenal declined to match it, with Rogers going on to join one of their big domestic rivals.

Sports.title: Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook
Sports.content:
Argentina's shameful behaviour should not let the World Cup's biggest offenders off the hook

Lionel Messi and his beaten Argentina team-mates deserved all the flak that came their way following the World Cup final but that should not give Gianni Infantino and FIFA a reprieve

View 3 Images Lionel Messi has come under fire for his behaviour in the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

According to a polling company that might have better things to do, Lionel Messi’s popularity amongst British people has gone down since he tried to get the saintly Marc Cucurella sent off during the World Cup final. It is unclear whether this news is keeping Messi awake at night but you suspect not.

‌



Messi’s lamentable attempt to land Cucurella in trouble was part of a tapestry of unedifying Argentinian antics and was unbecoming of a great player. But it was hardly the crime of the century.

‌



Since when did we become so puritanical? Would Cucurella have done it if the situation of the game had been reversed? Of course he would.

‌



You might hold Messi to a higher moral standard but players trying to get opponents into bother is a staple of the modern game. It did not help Messi’s cause that he was the captain of a squad that turned its back on Spain’s coronation after it had also descended into violent disarray at the final whistle.

Argentina flop's sister makes Falklands Islands claim after World Cup shame READ MORE :

The offending individuals will deserve whatever punishment comes their way and deserved all the criticism that has already come their way. But let’s not pretend we were shocked by the Argentinian reaction to the loss to Spain.

And let’s not allow their behaviour to deflect criticism and scrutiny from where it most needs to be directed most. It needs to be directed most at Gianni Infantino and FIFA.

‌



View 3 Images Bryson DeChambeau threatened to get Donald Trump involved in his rules row at The Open (Image: Richard Heathcote, Getty Images)

When it comes to petulant reactions, there was a belter at Royal Birkdale last Friday after Bryson DeChambeau received a two-shot penalty for what was a debatable rules infringement. It was a slightly controversial decision but one DeChambeau should have taken on the chin.

Instead, he ranted and raved at officials … and, apparently, threatened to call Donald Trump and get him involved. As it happened, the President of the United States never stepped in but you know where the idea came from.

‌



Thankfully, at least one football association is taking a stance. The Norwegians, headed by its federation president Lise Klaveness, are set to make an official complaint to FIFA’s ethics committee over Trump’s involvement in the Folarin Balogun case, which saw the American striker have his red card ban suspended.

View 3 Images Messi has been accused of trying to get Marc Cucurella sent off (Image: AFP or licensors)

Hopefully, more will follow suit. And hopefully, more will tell the relevant committee that the hydration breaks were aberrations that cannot be repeated. Hopefully, more will kick up a serious fuss over ticket prices and already demand changes for the 2030 World Cup.

‌



Never mind the tantrums shown by several Argentinians after the last whistle - and it has to be said that we seem to be more upset by them than the Spanish are - the final itself was a grotesquely gaudy and elongated occasion. Wayne Rooney had it spot on when he said the best thing about the half-time show was when it finished.

Sure, Argentina’s behaviour needs to be punished. And sure, Messi did not cover himself in glory. But the people who really need to be looked at now the World Cup is over are Infantino and FIFA.

Sports.title: Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers
Sports.content:
Man Utd XI from last Rosenborg friendly with six axed and two more potential transfers

A lot has changed since Manchester United last met Rosenborg

View 2 Images Less than half of the starters from Manchester United's previous trip to Rosenborg still play for the club (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are due to take on Rosenborg this week, some two years on from their last meeting. Those two years have been incredibly eventful, though, with the Premier League club undergoing a huge upheaval - and not just with the playing staff.

‌



Erik ten Hag was still United's manager when that match in Trondheim took place. He had just led the Red Devils to FA Cup glory but pre-season got off to a tough start when Noah Holm scored the winner in Trondheim.

‌



Ten Hag was gone just months later with Ruben Amorim taking his place. However, the Portuguese coach only lasted 14 months in the hotseat before his January 2026 exit, meaning Michael Carrick is in charge for the latest trip to Norway.

‌



Changes in the dugout have also been accompanied by an overhaul of the playing staff. Six of the 11 players who started the last Rosenborg game have since left or retired, while two more could yet leave Old Trafford before the current window is up.

Bruno Fernandes commits future to Manchester United despite new contract wait READ MORE :

Man Utd release new 2026/27 away kit with striking blue design READ MORE :

Radek Vitek started in goal that day and is the sole survivor of the back five still on the books at Old Trafford. The Czech started behind centre-back Jonny Evans - now retired and part of Carrick's coaching staff - and three other defenders now playing elsewhere.

‌



Aaron Wan-Bissaka and Will Fish both left the following month and could end up facing one another in the Championship before too long. Wan-Bissaka's West Ham are newly relegated to the second tier while Fish's Cardiff won promotion last season.

The defence was rounded out by academy graduate Sam Murray, who left for Carlisle in 2025 and is now looking for a new club again. As for Vitek, a promise of first team football could tempt him away.

View 2 Images Aaron Wan-Bissaka left United just a month after the friendly in Norway (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"At the moment, I am still here, but we will see. I hope so," he said after featuring against Wrexham in United's first friendly of the summer. "I hope there will be some interest. I think you will know when things are more concrete."

Further forward, Casemiro gave United two more years but left in the summer of 2026. The Brazilian is now at Inter Miami, with a strong end to last season not enough to keep him around.

He played in midfield with Mason Mount and Hannibal Mejbri that day. While Mount is still a United player, impressing against Wrexham, Hannibal is long gone.

‌



The Tunisian international sealed a permanent move to Burnley in August 2024 and remains at Turf Moor to this day. He helped the Clarets win promotion to the Premier League but they dropped straight back down last term.

Pre-season regularly gives clubs the opportunity to blood younger talent, particularly while waiting for international players to return from major tournaments. Ethan Williams and Ethan Wheatley are both still at United, having started that Rosenborg game, as are some of the youngsters who came off the bench in Trondheim.

Completing the front three was Marcus Rashford, who had surprisingly been overlooked by Gareth Southgate for England's Euro 2024 squad. The forward spent the 2025/26 season on loan at Barcelona but his future is up in the air again after the Catalan club opted against triggering a buy option, and manager Carrick will have a decision to make on the academy graduate.

Sports.title: Christos Tzolis: How Arsenal's new £34m signing went from Norwich flop to Champions League star
Sports.content:
It says everything about the evolution of Christos Tzolis that Arsenal's newest signing accrued more goal contributions last year than he made league appearances across an ill-fated spell at Norwich City.

The reason Tzolis will play for the newly minted Premier League champions is because, at 24, he is now every inch the clinical, cold-blooded attacker that Europe's elite believed he would become back when he was a teenager. Barcelona were among his illustrious courters back then as heavyweights flocked to observe a prodigious talent. But it was Norwich, rather than Barcelona, who clinched the youngster's sought-after signature.

The Tzolis hype train was already in full flow when the formalities of his £8.8million transfer from PAOK was confirmed back in the summer of 2021. At 21, Tzolis was already a full Greece international; for a Norwich side who were back in the big-time after romping to the Championship title under Daniel Farke, the winger's capture had all the hallmarks of a transfer coup.

And yet, things deteriorated rapidly. After scoring twice in a 6-0 win over Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup on his debut, Tzolis soon fell out of favour. By early November, Tzolis had seen the manager who signed him sacked by the club, just hours after recording Norwich's first league win of the season.

‌



Dean Smith's appointment as Farke's successor proved to be the catalyst for the change of shape which effectively killed Tzolis' Norwich career.

Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race READ MORE :

Arsenal respond to Morgan Rogers transfer snub as £34m signing flies in for medical READ MORE :

“It was the hardest year of my career,” Arsenal's newest attacker conceded to Het Nieuwsblad back in 2024. “The first time I didn’t play with the first team, but with the second [reserves], I was very disappointed. That was the lowest point of my career.

“My agent and my family had to convince me not to give up. And life off the pitch wasn’t easy back then.”

In total, Tzolis made just 27 appearances for Norwich before leaving the club permanently in the summer of 2024. The first of two loan spells designed to resurrect his career, with FC Twente, fell flat due to a knee injury. It was in the second tier of German football with Fortuna Dusseldorf that the youngster finally rediscovered his killer instinct, plundering more than 20 goals.

‌



From there, he never looked back. Unsurprisingly, Dusseldorf triggered their option to sign him permanently for just £3m. But it was Tzolis' next move which put the teen prodigy back on the path to superstardom.

Club Brugge swooped in to offer Dusseldorf the chance to effectively double their money instantly. They accepted and, in Belgium, Tzolis has flourished, accumulating more than 20 goals in successive seasons. Not only did he score 22 times last term, he registered a staggering 29 assists to break out as one of the biggest stars in the Belgian Pro League.

View 3 Images Christos Tzolis has transformed into a different player with Club Brugge (Image: JASPER JACOBS, BELGA MAG/AFP via Getty Images)

Tzolis returns to these shores not only hardened by the challenges of his stint in Norfolk, but brimming with confidence. Deadly with his right-foot, he has thrived in a left-sided attacking role and is viewed as the successor to the revered Leandro Trossard, who completed a move to Besiktas last week.

‌



Speaking to The Telegraph, Norwich's sporting director at the time Tzolis was signed, Stewart Webber, cites the physicality of the Premier League as one of the reasons behind the young attacker's failure to live up to expectations. “He was very young, coming into the hardest league in the world where the physicality is off the charts,” said Webber.

“It didn’t work out because we [Norwich] were a struggling team in an unforgiving division. Attacking players don’t get 100 touches of the ball when they are playing for Norwich. If he’d been at an Arsenal he would have probably been successful straight away.”

Tzolis returns to the Premier League a different beast. Naturally, he has grown physically and looks more robust than the twinkle-eyed teenager who was swatted aside both figuratively and literally at Norwich. The numbers he has put up consistently elsewhere in Europe, albeit at a level which is not elite, are eye-catching. His previous experience, although chastening, should give him some form of advantage when it comes to adapting to the rigours of Premier League life this time around.

“I’m a direct player, I go for goals or assists,” Tzolis told Arsenal’s website. “That’s my point of view as an attacker, as a winger. I’m always hungry to score or to give the final pass to my teammates. And I can say I work hard for the team, also in the defensive part.”

‌



View 3 Images Christos Tzolis struggled previously in the Premier League for Norwich City (Image: Ryan Pierse)

Arsenal went into the summer with designs on levelling up their attack, particularly on the left side. A deal for Morgan Rogers is now off the table, and Tzolis will not be the only acquisition in that area. Whereas at Tzolis organically became the main man at Brugge, his role at Arsenal will be significantly different.

There is, of course, the risk that Tzolis' exceptional record in Belgium does not translate to the Premier League. Even with the additional experience and nous under his belt.

In a transfer market where the Premier League's heavyweights have focused on domestic signings for inflated transfer fees this summer, the signing of Tzolis is somewhat of an outlier.

‌



But considering the transfer fee, the prospective upsides to the deal and the fact Arsenal are still after a ceiling-raiser signing for the left wing berth, you can see why signing Tzolis is a risk they feel is worth taking.

Sports.title: 'Kings of Manchester' - Elliot Anderson taunts Man Utd as City unveil £116m signing
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson hasn't even kicked a ball in anger on behalf of the blue side of Manchester.

But the England superstar has guaranteed that most of the fury will belong to those on the red half, having pinned his colours well and truly to the Manchester City mast. Anderson snubbed Manchester United in favour of becoming City's most expensive signing in a £116m deal. And he's wasted no time in making it clear why he chose one neighbour over the other.

“I think they're winners. They're relentless - and that's the sort of team I want to be a part of," said Anderson. "Champions and people who win trophies. Over the last 10, 12 years, they've dominated, so that's why I wanted to join.

"For as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the kings of Manchester."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Manchester United pull out of Alex Scott transfer race after learning asking price READ MORE :

Rodri to Real Madrid transfer truth as Man City contract stipulation revealed READ MORE :

Anderson’s comments will rile his new neighbours and echo the time when City taunted United with a giant ‘Welcome To Manchester’ poster depicting the face of Carlos Tevez, having lured the Argentine from Old Trafford in 2009.

United might have spent months attempting to land Anderson themselves, but the player insists Sir Jim Ratcliffe & Co were wasting their time.

Former United boss Sir Alex Ferguson once labelled City the ‘noisy neighbours’. But City have gone on to dominate the landscape of English football in the last decade.

‌



View 2 Images Carlos Tevez was welcomed to Man City in quite the fashion (Image: PA Archive/Press Association Images)

Anderson said: "Manchester City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen. As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity.

"From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. The success they have had, and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It’s a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that."

Anderson's rise to the top has been rapid and phenomenal. In the space of four seasons he has gone from being on-loan with Bristol Rovers to helping England reach a World Cup semi final, via becoming the most expensive footballer in Britain.

‌



But taking the next step at club level is something Anderson is relishing, because he knows he has joined a machine made to be successful.

He said: "It's happened quite quick, but I think I always believed that I could get to this point - and this is where I want to be. Now that I'm here, I'll keep pushing and try to take this club forward.

"It's a club built to win trophies and compete at the very top of the game. That is exciting for any footballer. I'm so happy to have been given this opportunity, and I am determined to repay the faith City have shown in me."

‌



Anderson, 23, grew up marvelling at the influence Kevin De Bruyne once had on City and English football. And he admits now finding himself on the same team De Bruyne used to grace with such distinction, feels like a dream come true.

He said: "I think Kevin De Bruyne is someone who I've hugely looked up to over the past seven or eight years.

"I've always grown up through the academy at Newcastle. I've always wanted to play like him. I've watched him all the time, and to be sat here in the team that he was doing it for is so special."

Pep Guardiola might now be gone, but Anderson is relishing working under Enzo Maresca. Not to mention the chance to prove he is worth the nickname the 'Geordie Maradona', given to him by Rovers fans during his time in Bristol.

‌



He added: "They started that and it sort of stuck everywhere I've been. It's a really good one.

"It makes me happy when I hear it on the pitch and yeah, it gives me real confidence.

"I think I bring a bit of everything. I bring quality, I bring physicality, energy. I'd like to think I'd get them (City fans) excited, get them off their feet and bring energy to the team."
