Sports.title: Chelsea paid Aston Villa £117m for Morgan Rogers. Is he the right fit?
Sports.content:
It quickly became apparent this summer that Aston Villa would not be holding on to Morgan Rogers. Having helped the club finish fourth in the Premier League and win the Europa League, the 23-year-old was in demand.

Arsenal looked like his likeliest next destination, with the champions eager to strengthen the left side of their attack. The charm offensive came from many angles, with Martin Ødegaard, Mikel Arteta and the club’s England players trying to sell the idea to Rogers. But, with Arsenal reluctant to meet Villa’s asking price, Chelsea intervened and made Rogers the most expensive British player ever, surpassing the £116m that Manchester City paid Nottingham Forest for Elliot Anderson earlier this summer.

Xabi Alonso is new to Chelsea, so it is difficult to know exactly where Rogers will play. The versatile forward, who started out at West Brom before moving to Manchester City, Middlesbrough and then Villa, will probably be used in a variety of roles – often starting from the left but having opportunities to take up various attacking positions.

Alonso predominantly used a 3-4-3 formation at Bayer Leverkusen and a 4-2-3-1 at Real Madrid. If Chelsea play with three at the back, Rogers will be the left-sided No 10 in the team; if they use a four-man defence, he will start slightly wider but with the freedom to come inside – or he might even occupy the central role from time to time.

If Alonso goes with the style he used at Leverkusen, Rogers might not be the best fit. During Alonso’s two full seasons in the Bundesliga, the team averaged 62.1% (2023-24) and 59.6% (2024-25) possession. During their title-winning campaign in 2023-24, they went unbeaten all season while dominating the ball and moving up the pitch slowly.

They were set up to patiently build with lots of passes, win back possession quickly if they lost it and keep the ball as close to the opposition’s goal as possible. They made 367 high turnovers, which was 54 more than any other side. This system works best with attacking players who are tidy and intricate in tight spaces. However, Rogers is at his most effective when he can use his pace and gallop into space.

His dribble completion rate last season was just 34.2%, which was nothing to shout about. And his completion rate for passes under pressure was just 73.4% – again not exceptional. Of the 161 forwards and midfielders who attempted at least 300 passes under pressure last season, Rogers ranked 143rd. The statistics suggest he is not particularly effective in close-quarters engagements.

With space to attack, Rogers is a threat. He made 223 progressive carries last season, the 10th highest among Premier League forwards, wingers and attacking midfielders. Only Cody Gakpo (41) and Matheus Cunha (35) had more carries that ended in shots than Rogers (30). He also created 16 chances for teammates after a carry: only 11 players created more. Rogers’ combined 46 chances created and shots taken following carries put him behind just Jérémy Doku (58), Gakpo (57) and Bukayo Saka (56). Alonso’s passing style may not bring the best from Rogers.

There are reasons for optimism though. Rogers is frequently on the move and that makes him difficult to track. Only four players made more off-ball runs in the league last season; his 160 off-ball runs ending in the box was the eighth highest in the division.

View image in fullscreen A mural of Jude Bellingham and Rogers in Birmingham. Photograph: Christopher Thomond/The Guardian

He also has the potential to form a good relationship with João Pedro. The Brazilian will probably be the focal point of the team and he is not a conventional No 9. He likes to drop deep, link with teammates and be a creator almost as much as a finisher. With Pedro dropping back, there will be room for Rogers to exploit beyond him: he made 258 runs in behind last season, the 12th highest in the league.

Rogers’ strong relationship with Ollie Watkins bodes well for Chelsea. He created 20 open-play chances for Watkins last season, which was the second most from one player to another in the league. Wherever he has played, Rogers has developed an understanding with his teammates. He already has a close friendship with Cole Palmer after their time together in the Manchester City academy.

Rogers’ other great attribute is his ball-striking ability. Since he made his Premier League debut in February 2024, Rogers has scored 21 non-penalty goals from 14.7 non-penalty expected goals. His overperformance of +6.3 is the 10th highest in the league.

Rogers has a great strike on him and it could be a gamechanger for Chelsea, particularly when they play teams employing a low block. His five league goals from outside the box since his Villa debut is bettered by just six players. Few players are as accurate when shooting from distance. It was his shot against Norway that led to Jude Bellingham’s winning goal in the World Cup quarter-final.

Chelsea have paid an incredible amount of money for Rogers and there are reasons to wonder if the move will work tactically. But Rogers has a habit of making an impact regardless of the context. He’s not a right winger but he still made his presence known for England against Argentina in the World Cup semi-final, setting up Anthony Gordon’s opener from the right.

Is he a £117m player? Perhaps not. Will he succeed playing the same way he played at Villa? Perhaps not. But it’s hard to imagine him not making a significant impact at Stamford Bridge.

This is an article by Opta Analyst

Sports.title: Maldini confirms crisis-hit Italy have held talks with Guardiola and Ancelotti
Sports.content:
The Italian football federation (FIGC) has talked to Pep Guardiola, the former Manchester City coach, and Carlo Ancelotti, the Brazil manager, about taking over the crisis-hit national team.

It hopes to announce the new Italy coach within the week, with the Azzurri still reeling after failing for a third straight time to qualify for the World Cup.

Paolo Maldini, the former Italy and Milan defender, was named as the federation’s new technical director at the start of the month and was present at a meeting with the Serie A clubs on Thursday, along with the new FIGC president, Giovanni Malagò, and the special advisor Leonardo.

“Honestly, today we can’t give news about what’s happening. You’ve identified one of our targets,” Maldini said when asked about Guardiola in a news conference after the meeting. “We can’t hide that we also talked with Carlo Ancelotti before talking with Pep. Honestly, it seemed right to start with the best in the world, to see their general availability.”

Guardiola left City at the end of last season, bringing to a close a trophy-laden, 10-year spell in which he established the club as a force in Europe and changed the face of English football. The 55-year-old has won numerous major titles across his coaching career including at Barcelona and Bayern Munich.

Maldini and Leonardo spent three days in Barcelona recently to speak with Guardiola about taking the Italy job. “The best thing would be to announce the new coach this week, but even more to wait for the person we really want,” Maldini said. “So there’s urgency, but not so much inside us.”

Ancelotti signed a contract extension with Brazil in May through to the 2030 World Cup. But the five-time world champions had one of their worst ever performances on football’s biggest stage as they were eliminated in the last 16 thanks to a 2-1 loss against Norway.

The 67-year-old has won league titles in Italy, England, France, Spain and Germany. He is also the only coach to have won the Champions League five times.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Italy, four-time world champions, missed out on a third straight World Cup after a playoff loss to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March, prompting the resignations of the FIGC president, Gabriele Gravina, and the head coach, Gennaro Gattuso. Gattuso had taken over from the fired Luciano Spalletti the previous June with the team already flailing following a defeat against Norway in their opening qualifier.

The former Italy coaches Roberto Mancini – who led the Azzurri to victory in the European Championship in 2021 – and Antonio Conte are also among the favourites to take charge of the national team. Andrea Pirlo, who helped Italy to win the World Cup in 2006 as a player, is also reportedly in contention.

Sports.title: Darwin Nunez offered escape from Saudi nightmare by MLS club
Sports.content:
Al Hilal striker Darwin Nunez is in talks over a move to MLS side Atlanta United, talkSPORT understands.

Nunez, who left Liverpool last summer for Saudi Arabia, is expected to leave after being frozen out of games last season.

2 Nunez hasn't played for Al Hilal since February and is expected to leave Credit: Getty

Both the Uruguayan and Al Hilal have discussed a mutual termination of his deal - which does not expire until 2028 - but as it stands, he remains under contract at the club.

Nunez played 14 times in the Saudi Pro League last season, scoring six goals and providing four assists.

However, in February, he was axed from their registered league squad following a failed move to Turkish giants Fenerbahce.

His transfer to Turkey fell through, but Al Hilal had already signed Karim Benzema from Al Ittihad to replace him.

Benzema took his spot in the squad, leaving Nunez without a place and unable to feature in any league fixtures.

He was able to play in the AFC Champions League, where he scored two goals following his snub and stared in the direction of the club's ownership, muttering something to himself after celebrating.

Since that game on February 16, Nunez hasn't played a single game for Al Hilal, making his last five appearances for Uruguay.

He featured in all of his nation's games at the World Cup, as they failed to win a game and were knocked out early.

His recent misery seems to potentially be coming to an end though, as Atlanta have opened talks to sign him this summer.

The MLS side are also interested in Swiss striker Breel Embolo, who currently plays for Monaco and is valued at £12.8million.

2 Nunez could finally be able to end his misery with a move to the MLS Credit: Getty

Striker conundrum

Should Nunez leave Al Hilal, the Saudi side will have Benzema as their main front man for the next campaign.

At least that's what he's expecting to be for the club...

talkSPORT understands that the 2022 Ballon d'Or winner is expecting a prominent role in the team next term.

But the club and Benzema are in talks ahead of the new season, with Al Hilal attentive to the striker market.

He would not accept a scenario, suggested by some Saudi reports, where he is only registered for Asian Champions League games.

That is the position that Nunez was put in last term, which left him sidelined from the Al Hilal set-up.

Sports.title: USMNT player Sebastian Berhalter closes in on transfer to Championship club
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough continue to be active during this summer's transfer window.

Having penned a deal for former Tottenham Hotspur starlet Will Lankshear, the EFL Championship outfit are now on the brink of bringing in one of the United States Men's National Team's biggest names in Sebastian Berhalter.



3 Berhalter made his World Cup debut in the USA's 4-1 win over Paraguay Credit: Getty

According to a report from The Athletic, the 25-year-old midfielder is finalizing the switch from MLS side Vancouver Whitecaps to Boro for a fee of roughly $2 million (£1.5 million).

Middlesbrough reportedly beat out 6-10 other clubs who were thought to have 'seriously pursued' Berhalter's signature this summer.

He was omitted from the Whitecaps' squad in their 4-3 defeat to Cincinnati on Wednesday night as the deal advanced.



With Berhalter set to be out of contract this winter, the Whitecaps seized the opportunity to recuperate some funds and avoid letting him walk away on a free transfer.

Berhalter has spent his entire senior career playing in MLS, having suited up for the Columbus Crew and Austin FC in the early parts of his career.



But his tenure with the Whitecaps has been by far his most successful. He's registered 20 goals and 26 assists in 167 appearances for the Canadian outfit.

Boro bringing in one of MLS' brightest talents

In the 2025 MLS campaign, the box-to-box midfielder had five goals and 13 assists in all competitions, and was named in the MLS Best XI, helping the Whitecaps to the Canadian Championship title.



He was also instrumental in the Whitecaps reaching the MLS Cup final last season, though they ultimately lost out to Lionel Messi and Inter Miami.

Vancouver also reached the CONCACAF Champions Cup final last season, but lost 5-0 to Mexican side Cruz Azul.

Having earned All-Star recognition in 2026, Berhalter was rewarded by being named as part of Mauricio Pochettino's 26-man USMNT squad for the 2026 World Cup, making his debut off the bench in the second half of their 4-1 thumping of Paraguay.

3 Berhalter registered a goal and an assist at the 2026 World Cup Credit: Getty



3 Berhalter has been a revelation for the Whitecaps since joining the team in 2022 Credit: Getty

He even got on the scoresheet during the Group Stages of the competition, netting the Stars and Stripes' equalizer against Turkey, although the USMNT would fall to a late goal in stoppage time to lose 3-2.

He wound up featuring in all five (one start) of the States' games of this summer's tournament on home soil, adding an assist.

Berhalter now follows in the steps of his father Gregg - the former USMNT head coach - footsteps by moving across the pond to England with his father playing for Premier League side Crystal Palace at the time he was born in 2001.



Middlesbrough are currently on a promotion push, having come narrowly close in the 2025-26 campaign, finishing in fifth place to cement a playoff spot.

Although they would lose to Southampton 2-1 on aggregate after extra time in the semi-finals, they advanced to the final after the Saints were expelled from the competition due to SpyGate.

However, Hull City ultimately proved to be too much for Boro on the day in front of the 80,000-plus fans at Wembley Stadum as Oli McBurnie netted the winning goal in stoppage time to bring their Premier League aspirations for the 2026/27 season to an end.

Stay up to date on all things MLS across our talkSPORT platforms - subscribe to our YouTube channel for the latest news, opinion, exclusive interviews and our daily unfiltered, unscripted show 'The S* Word, from 8am ET.

Sports.title: How can Chelsea afford Morgan Rogers? Alejandro Garnacho ‘PSR deal’ theory dismissed
Sports.content:
Chelsea broke the British transfer record to sign Morgan Rogers, and questions have been raised over they can afford it.

England star Rogers joined the Blues from Aston Villa on Tuesday for a massive £117million fee.



2 Rogers has joined Chelsea in a blockbuster, British record deal

Alejandro Garnacho has since moved in the other direction on loan, with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

Football finance expert Stefan Borson doesn't believe the two clubs struck any kind of deal relating to the Premier League's Profit and Sustainability (PSR) rules, however.

'I wouldn't read too much into it'

Asked whether he thought there was an 'arrangement of convenience' between Chelsea and Villa, Borson told talkSPORT on Tuesday: "I don't think so actually at this point, particularly on Garnacho.



"First thing is, it is a loan, and we know that Villa have taken a number of players on loan with conditions and have not bought those players ultimately.

"So they've ended up paying relatively small loan fees, including players with Chelsea themselves."



Jadon Sancho and Axel Disasi have both spent time on loan at Villa from Chelsea in recent seasons, but neither player made their move permanent.

"So I wouldn't read too much into it that it's a certain deal," Borson continued.



"I think the other factor is that there's no profit on Garnacho either way. I mean, there be a couple of million here or there, but it's certainly not significant player trading profit.

"It gets them out of a difficult deal, I guess. I mean, I think they've done well to get their money back largely if the player does end up going to Villa [permanently]."

'A red herring'

"But generally," Borson added. "It doesn't really work from settling the issue that they have with UEFA. I think it's a bit of a red herring there."

2 Garnacho is the latest player to join Villa on loan from Chelsea Credit: Getty



Both Chelsea and Villa were among four English clubs fined for breaching UEFA's squad-cost rules for 2025.

Villa and Chelsea entered into three and four-year settlement agreements with UEFA in light of the aforementioned rule breaches.

Newcastle and Nottingham Forest were the other sides punished.

Villa have also been linked with a move for Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson, but a deal for the striker could prove difficult, as Borson explained.

"And of course, if they did a permanent deal with, say, Jackson," Borson said.



"And they can't do a loan deal now because they've got one player on loan [from Chelsea, Garnacho]. So they'd have to do a permanent deal with Jackson.

"And the rules have changed this summer such that if you trade a player within 45 days, it's deemed to be a player exchange. And that will cause both Villa and Chelsea issues in respect of their UEFA settlement."

Sports.title: Arsenal set to sign history-making EFL star after missing out on Jeremy Monga
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to sign history-making EFL star after missing out on Jeremy Monga

Arsenal are reportedly set to complete the signing of 16-year-old sensation Axel Donczew from Cardiff City.

The Gunners have moved for another history-making teenager after missing out on Jeremy Monga, who joined Manchester City.

3 Arsenal are set to sign another young star after missing out on Monga to City Credit: Manchester City

Monga is the second youngest ever player in Premier League history and the youngest ever Championship goalscorer, and he signed for Man City from Leicester earlier this summer.

That deal was completed despite Arsenal having an agreement in place, with City swooping in to complete a hijack and sign the starlet.

Mikel Arteta missed out on his target in the end - but the club have now made an approach for a second youngster.

According to The Athletic, the Gunners are on the brink of signing Donczew, who is Cardiff's youngest ever player.

The midfielder made his Bluebirds debut in October 2025, appearing as a substitute in an EFL Trophy tie against Newport County.

His first appearance, at 16 years and 117 days old, saw him break the record set by ex-Arsenal star Aaron Ramsey, who made his Cardiff bow aged 16 years and 123 days old in 2007.

He then went on to feature in another game in the cup competition, playing 23 minutes against AFC Wimbledon in December.

Donczew also has caps for Wales on the international stage, playing for his country at under-15 level through to the under-19s.

Across his 11 national appearances, he has scored two goals.

The teenager is also eligible to play for Poland, so he has multiple options when it comes to future senior representation.

3 Arteta has done some business already this summer, with more big names linked Credit: Getty

Arsenal's signings so far this summer

Donczew looks set to be the next arrival for Arsenal in this transfer window, with the Gunners already welcoming two new faces.

Christos Tzolis' signing was confirmed on Thursday, as the ex-Norwich winger made a £34million move from Club Brugge.

That came after former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier joined the club following the expiration of his contract at Elland Road.

In fact, the Gunners have made three signings already this summer, if you include the permanent arrival of Piero Hincapie.

Hincapie spent last season on loan at the Emirates, but signed a full-time contract at the club for £34.5m in June.

More incomings are expected though, as Arteta looks to bolster his squad for their Premier League title defence this term.

3 Guimaraes is one of Arsenal's targets as they look to secure multiple new signings Credit: Getty

Arsenal have been linked with John Stones, who is now a free agent after leaving Man City at the end of his contract.

And they are also continuing to pursue Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes, having already seen an approach rejected.

The Gunners made an offer of £65m for Guimaraes, but they were knocked back, despite agreeing personal terms.

They are expected to return with an improved bid for the Brazilian, who is understood to want to leave St. James' Park.

That new offer for the Toon captain is set to be over £70m.

Sports.title: Arsenal urged to give Declan Rice extended break or risk early retirement
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been warned they'll pay the price long term if they don't give Declan Rice an extended summer break.

The 27-year-old endured a relentless campaign that saw him play an exhausting 69 games, totalling 4,925 minutes across all competitions for club and country.

3 Rice struggled to match his club form with Arsenal during the World Cup, with an ongoing hamstring injury and illness affecting his game Credit: Getty

Rice missed just two Premier League for the Gunners, and featured in every World Cup game for the Three Lions.

He became a champion of England, starring in Mikel Arteta's side with four goal contributions during their title-winning season.

Additionally, he helped propel England to their best ever finish at the World Cup since 1966, securing a third place finish with a 6-4 victory over France in the bronze medal match.

However, after featuring in nearly every fixture available, it's clear that congested scheduling is mounting physical demands on Rice.

He was managing a hamstring issue in North America, having already suffered from a dead calf and minor knee injuries earlier in the season.

Immediately after England's final game of the tournament, Rice said: "That's what you do [play through injury] when you get to come to a World Cup. It's an honour, you do anything you can to put on this shirt.

"You never know when it's going to come to an end, you never take it for granted.

"The body's been through a lot this season. I think you can see I'm mentally done, physically done. I need a break now."

And Peterborough United chairman Darragh MacAnthony insists Arsenal must not rush Rice back from his break.

MacAnthony told talkSPORT: "I'd be saying to him, you go away for like a month, go get a holiday with your family, and then we're going to do a month of light training, and you're not going to touch a football for a couple of months.

3 Arsenal are working hard on their title defence with new signings, including Christos Tzolis Credit: Getty

"Because that kid, he's not a kid, he's 27 now, he will be burnt out by 30. You know, the body, it's amazing what football can do to the body, and we've seen over the years.

"Do you remember Fabinho at Liverpool? He was phenomenal one season, and over one summer he aged ten years."

Saka concern

Rice is not the only Arsenal star facing physical strain after a relentless 12 months.

Arsenal have also confirmed William Saliba will be sidelined for an extended period with a back injury.

Meanwhile, Bukayo Saka arrived at the World Cup with a persistent Achilles issue.

Even England manager Thomas Tuchel felt the winger needed careful management, opting not to allow the 24-year-old to train every day.

3 Tuchel was being extremely careful with Saka, who only started three games at the tournament

MacAnthony added: "Sometimes it's the wear and tear on the engine, right? And you worry about that for say Rice, you worry about Saka with his hamstrings now, his Achilles that he's got those issues with.

"So they're going to have to handle it really, really well."

Sports.title: Premier League releases its own team of the tournament after controversial FIFA picks
Sports.content:
Premier League releases its own team of the tournament after controversial FIFA picks

The Premier League has unveiled its very own World Cup team of the tournament, albeit with one key caveat.

It came hot on the heels of FIFA revealing it's World Cup 'Dream XI', which was voted on by fans across the globe.



6 A number of Spanish Premier League stars shone on the world's biggest stage Credit: Getty

The 'Dream XI' produced some rather peculiar picks, with Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha selected ahead of Spain's Unai Simon, who won the Golden Glove having kept seven clean sheets.

Spanish centre-back Pau Cubarsi, who was named the Young Player of the Tournament, was also snubbed from the 'Dream XI'.

There was also no room for either Simon or Cubarsi in the Premier League's team of the tournament, but that wasn't down to their qualities.



Instead, it's because they don't play in the English top-flight, which was the primary criteria for inclusion.

Announcing the team, which was listed in a 4-3-3 formation, the Premier League confirmed it was chosen by fans from all over the world from a shortlist of 101 players.



So, which Premier League stars made the cut?

Which goalkeeper made the team?

We start between the sticks and it's England goalkeeper Jordan Pickford who got the nod.

Pickford, who plays for Everton, made 19 saves for the Three Lions across the tournament as they finished third.



The 32-year-old beat the likes of Argentina's Emiliano Martinez (Aston Villa), Dutch gloveman Bart Verbruggen (Brighton) and Brazil's Alisson (Liverpool) in the voting.

Which defenders made the team?

At the back, Spain's Pedro Porro (Tottenham) and Argentina centre-back Lisandro Martinez (Manchester United) retained their spots in the line-up from the 'Dream XI'.

6 Despite playing a part in Spurs coming 17th, Porro ensured Spain wouldn't have similar misery Credit: Getty

That meant one other centre-back position as well as left-back was up for grabs.



Partnering Martinez in central defence was his Argentina teammate Cristian Romero (Tottenham).

Romero was a virtual ever-present for the La Albiceleste, missing just one of their eight matches throughout the tournament.

Completing the back four was England's Djed Spence (Tottenham), who is a natural right-back, but slotted in comfortably at left-back.

With the additions of Romero and Spence, that means 75 per cent of defence featured in the Premier League's team of the tournament was made up of Tottenham stars.



However, the duo may not be in north London for much longer, with Romero holding talks with Inter Milan while Spurs are understood to be open to offers for Spence.

6 Spence won over fans thanks to his perfectly-timed tackles Credit: Getty

Which midfielders made the team?

Spain's Rodri (Manchester City) was the only midfielder from the 'Dream XI' to be included in the Premier League's team of the tournament.

That should not come as much of a surprise since he was awarded the Golden Ball, which is given to the best player at the World Cup.



Joining Rodri in the midfield was England's Elliot Anderson (Manchester City) and Argentina ace Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea).

Anderson started every match for the Three Lions prior to their third-place play-off and finished top of the charts among his teammates for tackles (21) and interceptions (8).

It was also a tournament to remember for Anderson off the field, as he completed a £116m switch from Nottingham Forest to Manchester City.

Fernandez's World Cup ended on a sour note when he was sent off against Spain in the final, although he failed to address his red card in his post-match statement shared on social media.



6 Fernandez picked up two yellow cards in the space of 11 minutes during the final Credit: Getty

The midfielder also may not be a Premier League player for much longer having pined for a move to Real Madrid in recent months.

Which forwards made the team?

There's no prizes for guessing who was voted to lead the line in the Premier League's team of the tournament.

Erling Haaland (Manchester City) was the people's choice having scored seven goals in five games for Norway.



On the right, Bukayo Saka (Arsenal) received the nod despite starting three games for England.

Saka ended the tournament with three goals to his name, all of which were scored against France in the third place play-off.

His treble saw him become just the fourth England player to score a hat-trick in the gloal tournament.

6 Only Kylian Mbappe [ten] and Lionel Messi [eight] scored more goals than Haaland's seven in North America



And incredibly, only Harry Kane [14], Gary Lineker [ten] and Jude Bellingham [eight] have scored than Saka's six World Cup goals for England.

Senegal's Ismaila Sarr (Crystal Palace) completes the Premier League's team of the tournament on the left wing.

Sarr netted four times in as many games, which helped him become Senegal's leading goalscorer at the World Cup.

Sports.title: EFL club left gutted as Chelsea snap up star in under-the-radar transfer
Sports.content:
EFL club left gutted as Chelsea snap up star in under-the-radar transfer

Wigan Athletic have expressed their disappointment at seeing young star Harrison Bettoni depart for Chelsea.

The 18-year-old attacking midfielder has joined the Blues from the League One club on a four-year deal, with the two sides agreeing a 'significant' amount of compensation.

2 Bettoni burst onto the scene at Wigan last season Credit: Getty

Having signed for Wigan at under-13 level, Bettoni rose through the ranks to break into the first team.

He made his senior debut last season, scoring four goals in 26 appearances overall.

He notched up the only goal of the game as Wigan shocked Championship Preston North End in the FA Cup third round.

Wigan disappointed but proud

Announcing Bettoni's exit, Wigan managing director Sarah Guilfoyle said: "As a club, we made every possible effort to retain Harrison.

"We offered Harrison multiple strong and competitive long-term offers to remain at Wigan Athletic, reflecting both the high regard we have for his ability and the importance we saw him having in our future.

"Ultimately, every player reaches a point where they must make a decision they believe is right for their career. Harrison has chosen to pursue a new opportunity, and while we are disappointed not to see him continue his journey with us, we respect his decision.

"We've worked closely with Chelsea to agree a compensation package that reflects the time, care, and investment our academy has put into Harrison's development from a young age. Producing talented young players is something our academy takes immense pride in, and it's important that work is recognised.

"We thank Harrison for everything he has contributed during his time with us and wish him every success in the next chapter of his career."

Bettoni becomes Chelsea's fifth signing of the summer so far.

Earlier this week, the Blues completed a British-record £117m move to sign Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa.

Meanwhile, Alejandro Garnacho has moved the other way on loan but with an obligation to buy if certain conditions are met.

2 Rogers has just become the most expensive British player of all time, beating the record set earlier this summer when Manchester City paid £116m for Elliot Anderson Credit: Getty

The other new arrivals at Stamford Bridge are right-back Marco Palestra, striker Emmanuel Emegha and Geovany Quenda, who have come in from Atalanta, Strasbourg and Sporting Lisbon respectively.

The start of the Alonso era

Chelsea are preparing for the 2026/27 season with a new manager at the helm, Xabi Alonso.

They begin their Premier League campaign with a West London derby away to Fulham on August 24, before their home opener against Brighton on August 30.

Wigan, meanwhile, are building up to a third straight season in the third tier.

The Latics finished 15th last term, re-appointing Gary Caldwell as their boss in February.

They travel to newly promoted Cambridge United as the League One campaign kicks off on August 15.

Sports.title: Will Lionel Messi retire? Argentina captain tipped for new role with Real Madrid academy star
Sports.content:
Will Lionel Messi retire? Argentina captain tipped for new role with Real Madrid academy star

Lionel Messi has been tipped to retire from professional football before the 2030 World Cup.

The Argentina forward will turn 43 during the next finals in four years time.



4 Messi has been tipped to assume a new role with Argentina before the 2030 World Cup Credit: Getty

Fans had expected Messi to walk away from international football after winning the World Cup in 2022.

However, he remained part of the national team ahead of this summer's tournament, reaching the third final of his career.

Having scored eight goals and provided four assists, he was unable to guide Argentina to glory as they were beaten by Spain in the final.



The showpiece clash could now prove to be his final international appearance.

Meanwhile, Messi's current Inter Miami deal runs until the end of 2028, by which point he will be 41.



Although he could continue playing at club level until his contract expires, another World Cup appearance is less concrete.

Messi's international future

South American football journalist Tim Vickery remains unsure whether Messi will still be playing come the 2030 finals.



Speaking to Max Scott and Charlie Baker on talkSPORT, he was asked if the loss to Spain would be his last Argentina outing.

Vickery responded by admitting: "I don't know, because defeat for them is so painful that you'll need a little bit of time to assimilate.

"The next World Cup looks a long, long way off, especially after the evidence of the game.

4 Vickery believes Messi could nurture Paz over the next four years to become his successor for Argentina Credit: Alamy



"When you're playing against a team like Spain, it's really hard to carry someone who doesn't run.

"You can do it against some other teams, but against Spain, they're just too good without the ball. It's really, really tough.

"Before the game I was thinking, 'could he?' Could he still be around in four years? When Argentina's next game is in Buenos Aires in the World Cup, will he?

"Then after the game I'm thinking he's looking at the stands thinking 'no', but I wonder if he can play a role in the transition."



New role for Messi

Whilst Messi may not feature at the next World Cup, Vickery believes he could remain with the national team to nurture his successor.

He continued: "He's under contract for Inter Miami for another two-and-a-half years. There's a Copa America in 2028.

4 Nico Paz made just two appearances for Argentina at this summer's World Cup but could replace Messi on the pitch Credit: Alamy

"Nico Paz, who hardly got a look in this World Cup, partly because he can't really play with Messi because he wants the ball to feet just like Messi does.



"You can't have too many of them in your team, but Nico Paz I think is going to be the one for the future.

"I just think it's possible that Messi could stay in the squad as the kind of wise old owl, as a kind of Master Yoda.

"You could call him Messi Yoda, with Nico Paz as a kind of Luke Skywalker figure. I wonder if that will be the dynamic over the next couple of years."

Como's Nico Paz made just two appearances for Argentina during the World Cup, totalling 71 minutes of action.



The 21-year-old currently has one goal to his name in 11 senior caps since making his debut in October 2024.

4 The Como starlet has been tipped to become Messi's long-term heir for Argentina Credit: Getty

Of those, only five have seen him on the pitch at the same time as Messi.

However, the Real Madrid academy graduate is seen as the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner's long-term heir for Argentina.



Paz scored once in eight appearances for the Spanish giants before moving to Como two years ago.

He has since featured for the Serie A side 75 times, scoring 19 goals and adding 17 assists.

Argentina will host their first match at the 2030 World Cup on home soil as part of the tournament's centenary celebrations.

As a result, the Albiceleste have already automatically qualified for the finals alongside Spain, Morocco, Portugal, Paraguay and Uruguay.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to test Newcastle's resolve with £70m bid for Bruno Guimaraes after star told the club he wants to LEAVE to join Premier League champions
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to test Newcastle's resolve with £70m bid for Bruno Guimaraes after star told the club he wants to LEAVE to join Premier League champions

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Arsenal are ready to make a £70million offer for Newcastle United captain Bruno Guimaraes.

The Brazil international has told Newcastle he wishes to speak to the Premier League champions if they can agree a fee.

Newcastle have maintained he is not for sale and have been frustrated by proposals coming from his agents so far rather than official bids.

The Magpies, though, are aware of the 28-year-old's preference to join Arsenal this summer but would need a greater sum to convince them to sell.

There is understood to be other Premier League interest in Guimaraes.

Arsenal have effectively been told 'to put up or shut up' in their pursuit of the midfielder, who played 41 times for Newcastle last season, scoring nine goals.

Arsenal are finally set to table an offer of £70million for Newcastle captain Bruno Guimaraes

All discussions so far have come from the Brazilian midfielder's agent and Newcastle are becoming increasingly agitated by what they view as a 'tactical process' with the player becoming distracted by the speculation over his future which is being played out in public.

Arsenal have been led to believe a deal for the 28-year-old can be achieved for around £75million but Newcastle would need more than that to be persuaded. They have had no formal offers from the Premier League champions and would point to the increasing market rate for midfielders.

The onus is firmly on sporting director Andrea Berta coming to the table with a proper offer.

Guimaraes has two years to run on his contract but Newcastle have an option to extend by 12 months, offering them some protection.

Mikel Arteta is keen to strengthen his midfield ahead of the club's title defence and they have identified Guimaraes, who has been on duty at the World Cup, as their main target. After five seasons on Tyneside, he wants a new challenge.

Newcastle will be keen to avoid a drawn-out saga, like Alexander Isak last summer, and the onus is now on Arsenal to make an official offer.

Sports.title: Madeleine McCann's younger brother Sean says representing Scotland at Commonwealth Games will be 'pinnacle' of his journey ahead of opening ceremony
Sports.content:
The younger brother of Madeleine McCann, 21, has spoken of his excitement at competing in the Commonwealth Games in his home country of Scotland.

Sean McCann has been selected to compete for the Scots in the pool at the home Games, with swimming beginning Friday in Glasgow.

Madeleine disappeared from her family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal, at the age of three, back in 2007, and has been missing ever since. Sean was just two years old at the time.

Sean, 19 years on, is now making his senior international bow as a swimmer, and will compete alongside Olympic champion Duncan Scott for his national team.

'I'm very excited, it's my first senior games so I'm just looking forward to representing Scotland and doing my absolute best,' he told Loughborough Sport.

'It's the pinnacle really of representing Scotland at the Commonwealth Games, especially at a home Games.

Madeleine McCann's younger brother, Sean, has spoken about his excitement at swimming for Scotland at the Commonwealth Games

Madeleine disappeared from her family's holiday apartment in Praia da Luz, Portugal, at the age of three in 2007

'I've got lots of family up in Glasgow so that makes it even more special. I was there in 2014, watching as a kid, so to make it now, 12 years later, is really a full circle moment.'

McCann is a distance freestyler and is expected to compete in the 400m, 800m and 1,500m freestyle at the slimmed-down Games.

It is yet to be known whether parents Kate and Gerry McCann will attend the event to watch their son compete.

Sean has been competing in the pool since the age of eight, and his career took him to the international stage at youth level in 2023 as he competed at the Commonwealth Youth Games in Trinidad and Tobago.

The distance swimmer, who originally hails from Leicester but qualifies to represent Scotland through his father Gerry, is a student at Loughborough University, studying Chemical Engineering.

Sean is looking to follow in the footsteps of the likes of Adam Peaty by qualifying for the next Olympic Games in 2028. There is confidence that his upcoming appearance has him on the right path to competing for Team GB in LA in two years.

'I started competitive sport when I was eight, joining Charnwood Triathlon Club,' he once wrote on the Joe Humphries Memorial Trust website.

'It was here that I discovered my passion for swimming, and I joined Loughborough Town Swimming Club to increase the number of swim sessions I did per week.

It is not known if parents Kate and Gerry will be in attendance to watch their son compete

'At the age of ten I was selected to swim at City of Leicester (Leicestershire's performance swimming club), and I have since gone on to win multiple county titles as well as becoming regional and National champion in my age group.

'In order to have achieved this, I have had to remain extremely dedicated, getting up at 4am multiple mornings each week to train, since the age of 11.

'I am aiming to compete at the 2026 Commonwealth Games and also the 2028 Olympics in LA.'

Sports.title: Chelsea close in on £55m agreement for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix as Arsenal announce £34m signing of Christos Tzolis: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea close in on £55m Maxence Lacroix

Chelsea are closing on agreement over a deal for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix worth around £55m.

As Daily Mail Sport reported on Monday, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea are closing on agreement over a deal for Crystal Palace defender Maxence Lacroix

Crystal Palace locked in Matsima talks

Crystal Palace are continuing talks to sign centre-back Chrislain Matsima from Augsburg.

As negotiations carry on with Chelsea over the structure of a fee on the sale of Maxence Lacroix, Palace are looking to bolster their defensive options.

They have discussed Chelsea's Axel Disasi as an alternative too. The Frenchman had interest from Roma also.

They have already added versatile Oscar Mingueza on a free after he left Celta Vigo.

Gunners get their man

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34million.

The fee is a record for the Belgian Pro League.

Arsenal have completed the signing of winger Christos Tzolis from Club Brugge for £34million

The 24-year-old, formerly of Norwich City, scored 17 goals and added 23 assists in 36 league appearances last season.

Magpies swoop for £30m star

Newcastle United have agreed a £35.5million deal for Monaco midfielder Aladji Bamba.

The 20-year-old travelled to Tyneside for a medical on Thursday morning ahead of completing his surprise move.

The France U20 international has only had one season in Monaco's first team and has made only 12 competitive starts in all competitions but is rated as an outstanding prospect.

The clubs have agreed an initial £30m guaranteed payment plus £5.5m in add-ons. There is also a 15 percent sell-on clause in the agreement.

Bamba, who plays as a defensive midfielder, made five Champions League appearances and 18 in Ligue Un last season.

Newcastle sold Sandro Tonali to Tottenham last month and have been in the market for a second young midfielder after signing 18-year-old Sean Steur from Ajax. Another target, Freiburg's Johan Manzambi, opted to join Aston Villa instead last week after they had agreed a £49m fee. They also enquired about Tottenham’s £50m-rated Lucas Bergvall but insist stopped short of a formal offer.

Newcastle United have agreed a deal to sign Monaco defensive midfielder Aladji Bamba (left)

It underlines a change in strategy for Newcastle of signing players to develop which carries a degree of risk. It also gives added importance to keeping experienced players such as Bruno Guimaraes though he remains eager to leave for Arsenal.

Newcastle remain the market for another goalkeeper after moving on from Manchester City's James Trafford, who is destined for Leeds.

They did hold a meeting over Brighton's Carl Rushworth who has been the subject of offers from Coventry City and was also on Leeds' radar.

🚨 Newcastle have agreed a £30m deal with AS Monaco for Aladji Bamba



✈️ The 20-yr-old midfielder is due on Tyneside this morning — Craig Hope (@CraigHope_DM) July 23, 2026

Saints stand firm on Charles fee

Southampton risk pricing Shea Charles out of a move to the Premier League as they push for over £30million for the Northern Ireland international.

Fulham are the latest club to be rebuffed after they offered in the region of £24million for the 22-year-old.

The Cottagers believed they could strike a deal on the understanding Saints would accept £25m plus add-ons. However, the Championship side are demanding more.

Charles, who they bought from Manchester City in 2023, made 38 appearances last season and scored what looked to be the winning goal in the play-off semi-final against Middlesbrough only for the club to be excluded from the showpiece Wembley final as a consequence of 'Spygate', as exclusively revealed by Daily Mail Sport.

Leeds United had made the early running for Charles.

They also made three offers to Southampton which were subsequently rejected and are likely to consider other options.

Manchester City also hold a 15percent sell-on.

Saints are trying to build for the new season against the backdrop of head coach Tonda Eckert facing a suspension after he was charged with misconduct by the Football Association for his role in the Spygate scandal. He had until Tuesday to respond to the charges.

West Brom are also keen on Saints forward Cameron Archer.

Leeds in talks with City over Trafford move

Leeds United are in talks to sign England international goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City.

Trafford, who went to the World Cup this summer, only rejoined Manchester City from Burnley last summer but managed just four Premier League outings.

Leeds are on the hunt for a new No 1 goalkeeper after Karl Darlow left for Manchester United.

Trafford came through City's academy but, after making no first-team appearances, left for Burnley in 2023 after a series of loans.

He rejoined last summer in a £31million deal - a record sum for a British goalkeeper.

As Daily Mail Sport reported in April, Trafford was back on Newcastle United's agenda to be their number one but they were aware it as becoming increasingly difficult amid competition and valuation last week.

Leeds are acting are losing Darlow. Illan Meslier has also joined Arsenal while Torino want Lucas Perri.

They have asked about Zion Suzuki at Parma but are hopeful Trafford will join as he looks to cement his place as Jordan Pickford's main rival to the England number one jersey.

Aston Villa and Spurs have also shown interest in Trafford but he sees an opportunity at Leeds to build his future.

Newcastle have also met Brighton goalkeeper Carl Rushworth’s representatives who remains subject of offers from Coventry City and was also on Leeds’ radar.

Leeds United are in talks to sign England international goalkeeper James Trafford (right)

Young Reds stopper leaves on loan

Liverpool goalkeeper Armin Pecsi has joined TSV Hartberg in Austria on a season-loan.

The 21-year-old, who made his senior international debut for Hungary last month, arrived at Anfield a year ago m.

He has been a regular for Liverpool's U21s and was also included in the senior side's matchday squad on five occasions.

Blues ramp up pursuit of Leverkusen teenager

Chelsea are stepping up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen winger Kerim Alajbegovic after offloading Alejandro Garnacho to Aston Villa and Nicolas Jackson expected to follow.

The exciting Bosnia international has had interest from Leeds United, Arsenal, Aston Villa and Atalanta.

Leverkusen sold the 18-year-old to Red Bull Salzburg last year but, after an impressive season, took up their option to buy him back this summer for £7million.

However, the winger made such an impression in Austria, and on World Cup duty with Bosnia, where he scored a spectacular long-range goal in their group-stage win over Qatar that his valuation is now closer to £30m.

Atalanta were considered to be in pole position earlier this month but Chelsea and Xabi Alonso were made aware of the opportunity and are now looking to strike a deal.

They have recognised the youngster's potential to add another pacy dimension to the first team set-up alongside new signing Morgan Rogers with Garnacho going and Nicolas Jackson expected to follow the Argentine to Villa.

Chelsea are stepping up their interest in Bayer Leverkusen winger Kerim Alajbegovic

Harrison poised for MLS return

Leeds United are finalising terms with New England Revolution for the sale of Jack Harrison.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this month the Revolution have been pursuing the 29-year-old this summer but were trying to navigate the required personal terms and fee.

The winger, who started his senior career with New York City, spent last season on loan at Fiorentina and has two years left on his contract at Elland Road.

Leeds are continuing negotiations with Manchester City over a fee for James Trafford.

The England goalkeeper is also expected to have a release clause in any contract he signs at Leeds.

City are also looking for a replacement should they agree terms.

Bettoni heads to Stamford Bridge

Chelsea have confirmed Harrison Bettoni has joined from Wigan Athletic on a four-year contract 2030.

The 18-year-old attacking midfielder was part of Wigan’s first team last season and appeared 27 times during a breakthrough campaign.

Chelsea beat off stern competition for his signature from Manchester City and AC Milan.

Sports.title: Elliot Anderson aims dig at Man United after sealing £116m move to Man City as he declares: 'I've joined the kings of Manchester'
Sports.content:
Elliot Anderson aims dig at Man United after sealing £116m move to Man City as he declares: 'I've joined the kings of Manchester'

Follow all of today's transfer developments with Window Watch HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester City have announced the £116million signing of England international Elliot Anderson from Nottingham Forest.

Anderson, 23, joins City on a five-year deal, signing a contract until the summer of 2031, and becomes the second most expensive British transfer.

His move to the Etihad, agreed on July 2, was expected to make him the most expensive British player of all time - topping the £115m Real Madrid paid for Jude Bellingham in June 2023.

However, the switch was put on hold until after the World Cup, where Anderson won a bronze medal with England.

During that time, Chelsea completed a £117m deal for fellow England international Morgan Rogers from Aston Villa, making Anderson the British record transfer that never was.

City's new arrival wasted no time winding up local rivals Manchester United, declaring his new club the 'Kings of Manchester'. In Anderson's lifetime, City have indeed won more trophies than United - claiming 26 compared to United's 24 since 2002 (including the Community Shield).

'It's one of the biggest derbies in the world and for as long as I've known Manchester, City have been the Kings of Manchester,' Anderson said. 'It'll be a great fixture, and I can't wait to be involved in something like that.'

Newcastle, who sold Anderson to Forest for £35m in 2024 for PSR purposes, do not have a sell-on clause in the deal - meaning Forest stand to make £81m profit on the midfielder.

Elliot Anderson puts pen to paper on five-year deal at Manchester City

Anderson will take some time to rest after a marathon seven-week World Cup before joining Manchester City training in three weeks

Anderson won bronze with England at the World Cup

The deal contains no add-ons, with £117m representing the full transfer fee.

Anderson won the Under-21 European Championship with England last June before leaping up to Thomas Tuchel's senior side for the first international break of last season.

He is now an established England international with 17 caps and featured in all of the Three Lions' games at this summer's World Cup.

Anderson turned out 50 times in all competitions for Forest last season, helping them secure Premier League safety and reach the last four of the Europa League.

Anderson said: 'City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen.

'As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity. From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. I'm over the moon. I can't wait to play for this club. I'm really looking forward to it.

'The success they have had and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It's a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that.

'I think they're winners, they're relentless, and that's the sort of team I want to be a part of - champions and people who win trophies. Over the last 10, 12 years, they've dominated, so that's why I wanted to join. As soon as I arrive in Manchester after a break, I will be doing everything I can to establish myself in the City team.

'It's a club built to win trophies and compete at the very top of the game. That is exciting for any footballer. I am so happy to have been given this opportunity, and I am determined to repay the faith City have shown in me.'

Everywhere on the pitch 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/iNouzyZJJp — Manchester City (@ManCity) July 23, 2026

Manchester City director of football Hugo Viana labelled Anderson 'one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football right now'

Anderson had the most touches (3,300), won the most duels (297) and won the most possession (306) across the Premier League last term.

City say Anderson has experience far beyond his age with 174 senior appearances in club football

Anderson added that Enzo Maresca's intense style of football suits his game and noted that there is plenty of room for improvement.

'I always believed that I could get to this point and this is where I want to be. Now that I'm here, I'll keep pushing and try to take this Club forward. I'm only twenty-three, so I've got plenty of time to get to my best levels, and I'm not there yet - there's more to come from me.

'I'm really looking forward to that (working with Enzo Maresca). I've watched his teams over the past couple of years and spoke to a few of the lads from Chelsea and they all rate him very highly.

'I'm really looking forward to getting to work with him. I like to be intense when I play and use lots of energy around the pitch and get the fans going. So, I think that'll be good.'

Manchester City's director of football Hugo Viana said: 'Elliot is one of the outstanding young midfield talents in world football right now. He offers energy, outstanding work rate and an exceptional range of passing.

'His improvement in recent years has been really impressive and underlines his desire to be the best player he can be. At just 23, there is plenty of opportunity for development over the coming years and we feel he can become a complete midfielder.

'Manchester City is the best place for him to develop his game and keep improving, we are glad that he sees things the same way as we do. I look forward to seeing Elliot working with us ahead of the new season. I'm sure every City fan is excited to see what he can do.'

Anderson is set for three weeks off before joining up with Maresca's side at the end of pre-season.

Sports.title: Leeds in advanced talks with Man City over £35m deal for England goalkeeper James Trafford - just a year after he joined for record £31m
Sports.content:
Leeds United are in advanced negotiations with Manchester City for goalkeeper James Trafford in a deal worth in excess of £35million.

Newcastle United, who have spoken to City in recent weeks about Trafford and tried previously to sign him, are now exploring other options.

The 23-year-old's representatives wish to insert a release clause in any new deal with the expectation that higher placed clubs will be in the market for the England goalkeeper's services further down the line.

Personal terms will not be an issue with Leeds' owners paying competitive salaries.

Trafford joined City last summer in a £27million move from Burnley, just two years after City sold him for £14m, and they expect a substantial profit plus sell-on.

Trafford was expecting to take the No 1 jersey when he signed for Pep Guardiola but was sidelined when City seized an opportunity to sign Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris St Germain.

Leeds are in talks to sign Manchester City goalkeeper James Trafford, a year after he joined

Trafford ended up playing just four times under Guardiola in the league, but a further 13 cup games as they won the FA Cup and Carabao Cup.

City are now looking to add another goalkeeper as cover for Donnarumma as they negotiate the fee they want for Trafford.

They are continuing discussions with Lille also over a prospective £85million deal for Morocco international midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi.

The 18-year-old's arrival, alongside that of £116m signing Elliot Anderson, would be timely with Rodri due to miss the start of the season with back surgery.

The Spain captain has also yet to agree on a new contract and has one year remaining.

City announced Anderson's arrival from Nottingham Forest yesterday in a deal that made him the second-most expensive British player ever, behind Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea for £117m.

The 23-year-old Anderson signed a six year contract and said: 'City are one of the biggest clubs in the world and the squad they have is amazing - so strong in every position. As soon as I knew they wanted me, I was absolutely determined to make this move happen.

'As a footballer, you want to test yourself at the highest level. Being at City means I have that opportunity.

'From the outside looking in, City are a club that treats its players well and provides the perfect environment to excel. The success they have had and the way they have played the game in the last 10 to 15 years has been extraordinary. It's a privilege to be given the chance to be part of that.'

City also want to add a winger and a right-back.

Can Trafford relaunch his career?

​How did it go so wrong for Trafford at his boyhood club? It's only been a year since he re-joined City, but the goalkeeper already seems set to leave the club in search of more playing time.

​It could have been so different. Trafford came through the academy at City, and after impressing in a loan spell at Bolton Wanderers and then subsequently at Burnley in both the Premier League and Championship, he returned believing he was going to be the No1 at the club.

​But that's not how it panned out. Trafford only made three Premier League appearances for the Citizens before he was demoted to No2 after the arrival of Gianluigi Donnarumma from Paris Saint-Germain, and only four in total.

​'It wasn't what I expected coming into the season, and I tried to guard against the situation happening, but it's the reality,' Trafford said following a rare appearance against Salford City in the FA Cup last season.

​Now, if the move goes through, Trafford has the chance to relaunch his career at Leeds. The statistics show that before his disappointing spell back in Manchester, he was on the road to being a top goalkeeper. Hence, City bought him back.

​His performances on loan at both Bolton and Accrington Stanley, where he also spent a season on loan, earned the now England international a move to Burnley for £19m.

Trafford was initially brought back to City as No1 but only made three Premier League appearances before he was replaced by Gianluigi Donnarumma

Trafford showed his true potential when at Burnley in the Championship in the 2024-25 season

​After a bumpy start at the Clarets, in which he conceded 62 goals in 28 starts - and kept only two clean sheets - as they were relegated from the Premier League, Trafford showed his true potential between the sticks.

​As Burnley secured promotion from the Championship in the 2024-25 campaign, earning 100 points, Trafford broke John Ruddy and Paddy Kenny's clean sheet record with a remarkable 29 shutouts in 45 games. He only shipped a record-breaking 16 goals in those matches.

​In that season, Trafford remarkably managed to avoid conceding a single goal between December 22, 2024 and March 4, 2025. In that time, he managed 12 consecutive clean sheets, beating the previous record of nine.

​While Burnley ended up being pipped to the title by Leeds United that season, losing out on goal difference, Trafford was awarded the EFL Championship Player's Player of the season for his heroics in goal.

​Trafford's record-breaking season for the Clarets led to City triggering the buy-back clause they initially included in his sale, wrestling off competition from Newcastle.

While he may not have featured much in the top flight following Donnarumma's arrival, Trafford played every game on City's path to securing their ninth Carabao Cup.

​Trafford saved 88 per cent of the shots he faced during the competition, only conceding two goals and keeping four clean sheets, including one in the final against Arsenal.

​His 14 appearances in all competitions for City have shown he can still cut it at the top level, and he will be looking to relaunch his career in full if he completes the move to Yorkshire.

Sports.title: Man United considering £35m move for Bournemouth star Tyler Adams to add to £85m midfield overhaul
Sports.content:
Man United considering £35m move for Bournemouth star Tyler Adams to add to £85m midfield overhaul

Follow all of today's transfer developments with Window Watch HERE

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tyler Adams is among a number of options being considered by Manchester United as the club weigh up signing a third midfielder this summer.

Andrey Santos, of Chelsea, and Aston Villa’s Youri Tielemans have already moved to Old Trafford as part of the midfield rebuild for a combined total of £85million.

United would like to further strengthen that area of the squad following Casemiro’s departure as a free agent and the long-term knee injury that Manuel Ugarte sustained at the World Cup, but it will be determined by the transfer budget and the players signed in other positions.

United have been interested in Adams for some time, and it’s understood that the Bournemouth midfielder is still on a list of potential targets this summer. Unlike some of the other options, he would be more affordable at around £35m.

Whereas Bournemouth have steadfastly refused to consider offers for his teammate Alex Scott – another player on United’s radar – it’s believed that a deal could be done at the right price.

Both players have two years left on their contracts at the Vitality Stadium, and Scott is refusing to sign a new one. Not having two key men entering the final year of their deals in 11 months’ time is another factor that could persuade Bournemouth to do business this summer.

Tyler Adams is among a number of options being considered by Manchester United

Statistics have become an increasingly important factor in United’s approach to recruitment under new director of data Mike Sansoni, and the club have been impressed by Adams’ figures when compared to other defensive midfielders in the Premier League.

The 27-year-old USA international scored highly on running stats last season, ranking in the top-four of 85 players in five of the 10 categories. Adams also posted good stats in terms of tackles, interceptions and winning headers, surprisingly for a player who stands 5ft 9in.

The former Leeds and RB Leipzig man, who was linked with a move to United in January before suffering a knee injury just a few minutes into Bournemouth’s 4-4 draw at Old Trafford in mid-December, has just returned from a strong performance for the US at the World Cup.

While he is one of a number of midfielders on United’s radar, a combination of the low price and impressive stats could make him an attractive option as the club continue to pursue targets in different positions.

Sports.title: Charlie Woods snaps at fan in fiery on-course moment... a day after he was caught swearing on hot mic
Sports.content:
Charlie Woods, the 17-year-old son of golf legend Tiger Woods, had a fiery clash with a fan on Wednesday, moments after being caught in an X-rated hot mic moment.

The teenager endured a frustrating morning that saw his bid to win the 2026 U.S. Junior Championship at Saucon Valley Country Club come to an abrupt end.

After bogeying the first hole of a 14-for-2 playoff for the final pair of match-play berths, Charlie's dreams were crushed after carding a +5 over two days of action.

During that par-five first hole, after two competitors had secured birdies, the 17-year-old went for the green in two from 270 yards out - but fell 25 yards short.

As he attempted to hit his third shot, a fan took a photo during his backswing - with the shutter sound clearly heard as Charlie was going through the motions.

A video of the incident has since gone viral and captured the moment that the teenager turned around to the fan, asking: 'Really, dude?'

Charlie Woods, the 17-year-old son of golf legend Tiger Woods, had a fiery clash with a fan

Another person behind the camera could be heard saying: 'Right in his swing'.

Following the awkward moment, Woods was unable to convert his chip for birdie.

Tiger's son finished with a bogey - meaning that Eli Wessel of Indianapolis and Hudson Kutchma of Westfield, Indiana made it to the 64-person match-play bracket.

The unfortunate, viral moment came just one day after Woods dropped an X-rated hot mic moment, as he teed off on the par-three eleventh hole.

In another viral video, posted by Michael Schmittinger Jr., Charlie was seen screaming out: 'Oh, f*** you' following his tee shot.

In the end, this particular instance didn't have a major impact on the 17-year-old, who went on to make par on the hole.

The viral moments came just days after he failed to qualify for this year's US Amateur Championship - the leading annual tournament for amateur golfers in the United States.

He teed it up at Ohio State University's Scarlet Course last week in an attempt to secure his place in the tournament field.

It marks the latest blow for Charlie, who has struggled to string together a series of results

However, Charlie, who has committed to Florida State University when he finishes high school next year, struggled in the qualifying event.

He shot a five-over 76 to miss out on qualifying by six shots, according to Golf Digest. A total of 13 qualifiers and two alternates emerged from the Scarlet Course site.

It marks the latest blow for Charlie, who has struggled recently to string together a series of promising results in his young career.

Charlie has participated in seven ranked events this season, where his best finish was 19th place at the Junior Orange Bowl International back in January.

Aside from that event, Charlie is yet to secure another top-25 finish this season.

Sports.title: Donald Trump urges Atlanta Braves fans to continue doing 'racist' gesture at games despite huge backlash
Sports.content:
President Donald Trump made a hard push with Atlanta Braves fans while stumping for Republican congressman Mike Collins' campaign for US Senate on Wednesday.

Not only did he invite former Braves manager Brian Snitker on stage at a Cobb County high school, but the 80-year-old Trump also snuck in a dig at the rival New York Mets and their league-high $328 million payroll: 'The Mets have the highest salary in baseball, and they lose all the time.'

But it was Trump's performance of the Braves' controversial tomahawk chop that may have gotten the biggest reaction.

'They say you're not allowed to do that,' Trump told the chanting crowd. 'Do it.'

Trump was stretching the truth, of course. Braves fans continue to do the chop at Truist Park, where the team stills sells foam tomahawks despite the controversy.

Snitker laughed and clapped in response to the chants that Native American groups have condemned as 'racist,' 'harmful' and just plain 'hokey.'

Trump encourages the audience to continue doing the controversial tomahawk chop

Trump gives the tomahawk chop next to Braves executive Mike Plant, center, and Brian Snitker

Georgia was one of the settings for the infamous Trail of Tears, which was the forced displacement and ethnic cleansing of about 60,000 Native Americans between 1830 and 1850. But Trump has never shied away from the chop controversy in Atlanta, where he famously performed the ritual alongside First Lady Melania five years ago.

But unlike 2021, when Trump's chop was widely celebrated on the right, the President didn't seem to get as much mileage out of it on Wednesday.

Many still embraced his antics, including one Trump supporter who wrote on X: 'This is what I voted for.'

But while many Trump loyalists like Fox News sports pundit Clay Travis posted glowing tributes, responses to the chant were largely negative.

'I don't care whether it's non-woke or whatever, it's just the most annoying and grating chant in sports,' one fan wrote on X in response to Travis.

'Imagine actually doing something because you believe it, instead of doing it to just annoy people,' another added.

Many critics referenced surging gas prices and the ongoing war with Iran that Trump claimed to have won four months earlier.

'When's he going to put a tomahawk chop to gas prices?' asked sportswriter Robert Lusetich.

Another critic added: 'This will help lower the cost of living.'

Trump brought First Lady Melania to Atlanta in 2021 so they could both perform the chop

Although it's not as prevalent as it once was, Braves fans still do the tomahawk chop. Also, the club continues to sell foam tomahawks despite criticism from Native American groups

The chants aside, Braves fans appeared to be more concerned about the dreaded Trump curse.

The President recently intervened on behalf of the US men's soccer team over Folarin Balogun's controversial red card, and famously jumped on the bandwagons of several professional sports teams only to see them lose their following game. As a result, many Braves supporters were concerned about any Presidential hangover in Atlanta.

'The Braves players had better burn some sage in the dugout tonight to try and ward off the Trump curse,' one fan said of his first-place team. 'This isn't a joke. I'm very serious.'

'Thank you Trump for cursing the Braves,' one delighted Philadelphia fan added. 'Now my Phillies will overtake them.'

One gambler offered some advice on the subject: 'If you can still get action on win totals, empty the clip on the Braves under.'

Sports.title: BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid
Sports.content:
BHA freezes activity of leading syndicate after members complain they’ve not been paid

No entries or declarations will be allowed for Deva Racing whose flagship horse Imperial Emperor has won nearly £1.5 million in prize-money

View 4 Images Imperial Emperor is a star for Deva Racing run by Ryan Tongue (inset)

The BHA has put a stop to entries and declarations for horses owned by a popular racing syndicate after members complained they had not been paid.

‌



The Deva Racing Syndicate has a dozen horses in training in stables in Britain, the US and Dubai, managed by Ryan Tongue, who as a teenager served tea to 20-champion jockey Sir AP McCoy when he worked in the Worcester weighing room.

‌



Tongue, 30, has worked in a number of roles in racing, briefly as a jockey and then as a racing manager when he was involved in the purchase of dual Grand National winner I Am Maximus for the late owner Michael Grech.

‌



Seven years ago he took over Deva Racing, whose flagship horse Imperial Emperor brought the syndicate to national attention through his exploits in Dubai.

Trawlerman vs Scandinavia Goodwood Cup rematch set after Gold Cup thriller READ MORE :

The gelding, who was bought from Godolphin for £63,000 and put into training with local champion trainer Bhupat Seemar, has been transformed into a dirt performer.

He has won five of his eight starts for Seemar and earned a start in the last two runnings of the Dubai World Cup, one of the world’s richest races.

‌



View 4 Images Deva Racing members on the podium in Dubai (Image: Dubai Racing Club)

After two victories, including at Group 1 level during the latest carnival and a fourth place in the World Cup, his winnings have risen to nearly £1.5 million.

However attempts by syndicate members to secure their share of the prize-money from his latest campaign have been unsuccessful and as a result the problems have been brought to the attention of the BHA.

‌



One of the members, Tom Walton from Leeds, who works for a Manchester law firm, told Mirror Racing: “We have uncovered the overselling of shares and ultimately Ryan has kept prize-money.

View 4 Images Imperial Emperor has won nearly £1.5 million (Image: Dubai Racing Club)

“I got paid roughly £7,000 last year but I do know of one syndicate member who got nothing. We’ve not received any prize-money from this season when the horse won £760,000.

‌



“The last response I had from Ryan was on June 19 which said he wouldn’t be speaking to me, only to another member Mark. Ryan then blocked me and Mark is getting no response too.

“The BHA gave him a deadline and he told them he would endeavour to pay within 60 days but he was currently experiencing ill-health.”

In April, Walton discovered that Imperial Emperor had been entered in an online auction in Dubai without his knowledge. The gelding was withdrawn from the sale and the 20 original owning members subsequently completed a deal to buy the horse.

‌



View 4 Images Bhupat Seemar, the trainer of Imperial Emperor (Image: YouTube)

Walton said: “I wouldn’t want this experience to put anyone off getting involved in racing. Ryan and Deva are certainly outliers. The shining light is we’ve still got the horse and we can run him next season.

“I’ve kind of written the money off but what I want is to make sure that Ryan and Deva don’t have any involvement in racing again.

Article continues below

“I am presently a part owner in a syndicate run by My Future Champion. They’re a great outfit and I don’t want this experience to stain the whole syndicate world when there’s one like them around.”

A spokesperson for the BHA said “We can confirm that the BHA has put a stop on entries and declarations being made for Deva Racing Syndicate horses trained in Britain. We encourage any concerned syndicate members to contact the BHA on intel@britishhorseracing.com. We will be making no further comment regarding this matter at this time.”

Ryan Tongue has been approached for comment.
