World.title: Costa Rica Betting Operation Lands California Man in Federal Prison
World.content:
A California man who survived an assassination attempt outside an Escazú café more than a decade ago has been sentenced to federal prison for running an illegal gambling and money laundering operation out of Costa Rica. Jason Noah Feinman, 52, of Calabasas, received 27 months on June 9 in federal court in Los Angeles after pleading guilty in January to one count each of tax evasion, operating an illegal gambling business, and money laundering. A federal judge also ordered him to pay more than $1.3 million (about ₡589 million) in restitution and a $150,000 (₡68 million) fine, plus interest.

According to the Justice Department, Feinman operated a Costa Rica–based business that ran a website unlicensed bookmakers used to take wagers, including from bettors living in California, in violation of both state and federal law. The platform was a service layer for other operators rather than a consumer-facing sportsbook, and court filings do not name the business. Prosecutors say Feinman then laundered the cash the operation generated by converting it into checks made out to himself or his companies.

The mechanics were straightforward and repetitive. Between May 18, 2018 and January 2, 2024, the Justice Department says, Feinman handed a single customer more than $1.5 million (₡680 million) in cash and received 18 checks payable to him or his businesses for the equivalent amount, one of them for $200,000. Court filings identify that customer only by the initials C.K. and describe checks whose memo lines frequently referenced loans. Across the life of the operation, prosecutors say Feinman exchanged between $1.5 million and $3.5 million (₡680 million to ₡1.59 billion) in cash for checks.

The tax case ran alongside it. Feinman reported no taxable income to the Internal Revenue Service on his 2020 return and paid nothing that year, despite earning roughly $1.8 million (₡815 million), according to the Justice Department. Between 2018 and 2022 he evaded taxes on approximately $4.2 million (₡1.9 billion) in income, a loss to the United States that prosecutors put at about $1.52 million (₡689 million).

Assistant Attorney General Colin McDonald of the Justice Department’s National Fraud Enforcement Division and First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bilal A. Essayli for the Central District of California announced the sentence. IRS Criminal Investigation and Homeland Security Investigations conducted the investigation, and Trial Attorneys John C. Gerardi and Charles A. O’Reilly of the Criminal Division’s Tax Section prosecuted the case. The Fraud Division was created on April 7 and counts the case among its early results.

Feinman’s history in Costa Rica predates the gambling charges and includes a considerably more violent episode. In 2015 he was ambushed by gunmen on a motorcycle as he left a parking lot in Escazú, struck by nine rounds, and survived. Two men, Ricardo Francisco Solís Méndez and Steven Javier Calvo Sánchez, were tried at the Pavas courts for attempted homicide in a case that rested heavily on Feinman’s own identification of his attackers, which his attorney Miguel Jiménez Cerros said the American made on three separate occasions.

During the trial, two parking attendants who witnessed the shooting testified they had heard gunfire but could offer nothing further, with one telling the court he had a family. Jiménez Cerros said at the time that his client’s next objective was helping investigators identify whoever ordered the attack, a question the proceedings never resolved.

The case is not an outlier. In October 2025, Christopher Scott King, 51, of Santa Monica was sentenced to 21 months after admitting he ran an unlicensed bookmaking operation from Los Angeles County using a Costa Rica–based sports betting website to take wagers from California bettors. Prosecutors said King concealed $13.6 million (₡6.16 billion) in income from the IRS between 2019 and 2022 and laundered proceeds through real estate development and gold purchases.

He was ordered to forfeit $10 million (₡4.53 billion) and pay $3.8 million (₡1.72 billion) in restitution. A year earlier, Matthew Bowyer of Orange County pleaded guilty to running a betting ring that moved wagers through Costa Rican websites and casino agents, an operation whose clients included Ippei Mizuhara, the former interpreter for Los Angeles Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani, who placed roughly 19,000 bets through it.

The pattern that emerges from these prosecutions is consistent enough to be a template. American operators establish the technical and administrative side of a bookmaking business in Costa Rica, where offering online betting services to customers abroad occupies a permissive regulatory space and has supported a substantial data-processing sector for years, then use that infrastructure to reach bettors in states where the activity is plainly illegal.

What repeatedly ends these operations is not the betting itself but what happens to the cash afterward. In Feinman’s case it was checks. In King’s it was property and gold. In each, the proceeds eventually had to enter a banking system, and that is where IRS Criminal Investigation found them.

For the thousands of foreign residents working in or around Costa Rica’s online gaming and call center industry, the distinction that matters is jurisdictional rather than technical. Costa Rica does not license offshore sportsbooks in the way Curaçao or Malta do, and companies here have historically operated under ordinary commercial registration on the understanding that no bets are accepted from within the country.

That arrangement offers no protection whatsoever from United States law when American customers are on the other end of the transaction, and the last three years of federal sentencings suggest prosecutors have become considerably more systematic about following the money back to its source.

World.title: Costa Rica 911 App Can Locate Users Who Cannot Speak During Emergencies
World.content:
Costa Rica’s emergency services are urging residents and visitors to download the official 911 application before the August 2 Romería, highlighting features that can locate people in real time and allow them to request help without speaking. The Emergencias 9-1-1 CR app connects users with emergency operators through a standard voice call or an interactive text chat. When either option is activated, the application automatically sends the user’s location to the 911 system.

The location feature can be especially useful during the Romería, when hundreds of thousands of pilgrims travel on foot toward the Basílica de Nuestra Señora de los Ángeles in Cartago. Someone suffering an injury, medical problem or security threat may not know the name of the road or community where they are located.

Instead of requiring the caller to describe an unfamiliar location, the application allows emergency operators to receive that information directly from the phone. The location continues to update when a user communicates through the chat. Each new message sends updated location information, allowing operators to follow the person’s movement if they are walking, riding in a vehicle or attempting to leave a dangerous situation.

The chat was designed for emergencies in which speaking could place someone at greater risk. A person facing a threat can write that they need assistance and cannot safely talk. Operators can then continue communicating through text while monitoring the person’s changing location.

Users who choose the voice-call option should speak with the operator whenever possible. When speaking is not possible, authorities recommend keeping the call connected so the operator can listen to what is happening and determine whether the contact was accidental or involves a genuine emergency.

The application also includes a section for reporting events that do not require an immediate emergency response, including planned fumigations and drills that could otherwise generate calls from concerned members of the public. The Emergencias 9-1-1 CR app is available through Google Play and Apple’s App Store. Registration requires a full name, telephone number, email address and password. A verification code is then sent to the registered phone.

Users can complete a profile containing their home address, emergency contacts and relevant medical information. Gerardo García, a spokesperson for Costa Rica’s 911 system, said information stored through the app is confidential and receives the same protection as information provided during an emergency call.

The app currently handles about 40 reports per day, according to the emergency system. Officials hope greater awareness of its location and chat tools will encourage more people to install it before they face an emergency.

Authorities are particularly promoting the app before the Romería because pilgrims may be traveling through crowded or unfamiliar areas, sometimes at night or in changing weather conditions. Having the app in advance could prevent delays when emergency assistance is needed.

World.title: Argentina Leads Latin American Charge at Cincinnati Open
World.content:
Latin American tennis will field one of its deepest contingents of the season at the 2026 Cincinnati Open, with 14 players from six countries currently listed across the ATP and WTA singles fields. The group includes 12 men and two women, led by Argentina’s Francisco Cerúndolo, Brazil’s João Fonseca, Peru’s Ignacio Buse, Chile’s Alejandro Tabilo, and — in the women’s draw — Colombia’s Camila Osorio and Brazil’s Beatriz Haddad Maia.

Argentina accounts for eight of the entrants, giving the country by far the largest Latin American delegation at the combined ATP and WTA 1000 tournament. The published lists remain subject to withdrawals and other changes before the draws are completed. Rankings attached to the entries are entry-list positions, not finalized tournament seeds.

Cerúndolo arrives as Latin America’s highest-ranked entrant, listed at No. 22 after producing one of the strongest seasons of his career. The 27-year-old won the Buenos Aires title in February before capturing his first ATP 500 trophy at Queen’s Club in June. That victory made him the first Argentine man to win the historic grass-court tournament and moved him back toward the world’s top 20.

Fonseca will be another major attraction. The 19-year-old Brazilian is listed at No. 28 after reaching his first ATP Masters 1000 quarterfinal in Monte Carlo and making a breakthrough run to the Roland Garros quarterfinals.

Fonseca’s Paris run included a third-round, five-set comeback from two sets down against Novak Djokovic — a result that made him the first teenager in three decades to win back-to-back Grand Slam matches from two sets down, and the first to oust a former Roland Garros champion from that deficit since Michael Chang. He followed it by beating Casper Ruud to reach the last eight before falling to Jakub Mensik in the quarterfinals.

Cerúndolo and Fonseca are joined inside the tournament’s published top 32 by Tabilo at No. 30 and Argentina’s Tomás Martín Etcheverry at No. 31. Those four players would be positioned to receive seeds if the rankings and field remain similar when the draw is made. Final seedings, however, will be determined closer to the tournament and could shift because of ranking changes or withdrawals.

Etcheverry won his first ATP Tour title at the Rio Open in February, defeating Tabilo in the final after completing two matches on the tournament’s final day. The result gave Argentina another established contender beyond Cerúndolo. Tabilo has also been showing improved form. In addition to reaching the Rio final, the Chilean advanced to the semifinals in Båstad in July before losing a close three-set match to Andrey Rublev.

Buse may be the most important player sitting just outside the projected seed line. The 22-year-old Peruvian is listed at No. 35 following a remarkable rise that included winning the ATP 500 tournament in Hamburg as a qualifier. His victory over Tommy Paul in the Hamburg final made Buse the first Peruvian to win an ATP singles title since Luis Horna in 2007. He later became the first Peruvian man in more than three decades to win a Wimbledon main-draw singles match.

Argentina’s full group also includes Sebastián Báez at No. 56, Román Andrés Burruchaga at No. 60, Juan Manuel Cerúndolo at No. 50, Mariano Navone at No. 47, Thiago Agustín Tirante at No. 57 and Camilo Ugo Carabelli at No. 69. Navone has already collected a significant result this season, winning his first ATP Tour title in Bucharest in April.

Paraguay will be represented by Adolfo Daniel Vallejo, listed at No. 63. Vallejo recently reached the Båstad semifinals, where he pushed defending champion Luciano Darderi to three sets and became the first Paraguayan to reach an ATP Tour semifinal since Ramón Delgado in 2002.

Two women from the region appear in the published WTA field. Osorio, Colombia’s long-time No. 1, is joined by Haddad Maia, a former world No. 10 and 2023 Roland Garros semifinalist who is the most decorated Latin American woman in the draw. The regional representation still tilts heavily toward the men’s tournament, where Argentina alone accounts for eight entrants.

The Cincinnati Open will begin with qualifying on August 11, followed by main-draw competition and the men’s and women’s singles finals on August 23.

The tournament features 96-player singles fields and is one of five events that stage ATP and WTA 1000 competitions at the same location. Its expanded format followed a $260 million redevelopment of the Lindner Family Tennis Center in Mason, Ohio. For Latin American players, Cincinnati represents both an opportunity to collect valuable ranking points and a final major test against elite competition before the US Open.

World.title: Police seeking to arrest Stoney Ferguson on direction from Police Minister: ‘No-one above the law’
World.content:
Police seeking to arrest Stoney Ferguson on direction from Police Minister: ‘No-one above the law’

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Interim Minister of Home Affairs Julius Espat has reportedly directed police to arrest the son of a government minister following allegations that he assaulted a police officer and damaged a police mobile in Placencia.

The man has been identified to Breaking Belize News as Stoney Ferguson, the son of Stann Creek West Area Representative and Minister of Agriculture, Food Security and New Growth Industries Rodwell Ferguson. Previous public reporting has also identified Stoney as Minister Ferguson’s son.

Channel 7 News reported that the incident unfolded at around 5:15 p.m. on Saturday, July 18, while police officers were conducting a vehicle checkpoint at Mile 22 on the Placencia Main Road, near Mariposa Resort.

According to the report, a white cargo truck approached the checkpoint without licence plates, and the driver was allegedly not wearing a seatbelt. When a police corporal instructed the driver to pull over so that he could be issued with traffic tickets, the driver reportedly became verbally abusive and drove away.

Police pursued the vehicle to Crimson Two Drive, where the driver was reportedly found standing beside the truck. He was informed of the alleged traffic violations and cautioned, but police claim he continued behaving aggressively, refused to cooperate and pushed a corporal. Officers subsequently informed him that he was under arrest for allegedly assaulting a police officer and resisting lawful arrest.

The man was subdued and taken to the Placencia Police Station. Channel 7 reported that after his handcuffs were removed, he allegedly picked up a large stone and threw it at the corporal.

The stone reportedly missed the officer but struck a police patrol vehicle, damaging its front and rear windshields. The suspect allegedly attempted to throw another stone before officers subdued him again.

Despite the allegations, Channel 7 reported that the suspect was subsequently released without being charged after telephone calls were made. Police in Placencia were reportedly searching for him on Thursday.

Information obtained by BBN indicates that Espat has now directed that Ferguson be arrested and that the matter be handled strictly according to law. Espat reportedly instructed that police officers “must always act lawfully and be guided by the law, not by political considerations.”

Espat has been serving as acting Minister of Home Affairs since June 22, following the decision to place Minister Oscar Mira on leave.

At the time of publication, the Belize Police Department had not issued a public statement confirming Ferguson’s arrest or detailing the charges he may face.

The allegations against Ferguson have not yet been tested before a court, and he is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

World.title: Belize’s Garifuna Collective celebrates 20 years with European tour and major magazine cover
World.content:
Belize’s Garifuna Collective celebrates 20 years with European tour and major magazine cover

Minister of Culture Francis Fonseca, alongside the National Institute of Culture and History (NICH), proudly congratulated The Garifuna Collective reaching a monumental 20-year milestone.

To mark two decades of sharing Belizean culture with the world, the legendary group has landed a historic cover feature on Songlines Magazine-the world’s premier guide to global music-with cover photography shot right at home Jeremy Lewis of Hopkins Village.

The band is embarking on a 14-day tour spanning the UK, Ireland, and Germany.

“The complex rhythms demand attention, and quickly resolve themselves into a completely irresistible groove. When the melodies kick in on top of them, the lushness is overwhelming.” – The Wall Street Journal

The current touring line-up features Desiree Diego, Kenrick Lewis, Mohobub Flores, Al Ovando, Denmark Flores, Emilio Thomas, Sam Harris, and Austin Aranda.

The Garifuna Collective extended a heartfelt thank you to NICH, as well as their dedicated fans and friends worldwide, for decades of support in keeping Belizean music thriving on the international stage.

World.title: Zarah Castillo rises above the odds!
World.content:
Zarah Castillo rises above the odds!

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Port Authority has welcomed employee Zarah Castillo back to work, celebrating her return as a powerful example of resilience and determination.

Castillo, a wheelchair user, entrepreneur, legal clerk and advocate for persons with disabilities, has overcome significant challenges since an accident in September 2023 left her facing the prospect of paralysis from the waist down.

Castillo endured months of physical, emotional and mental struggles but refused to allow her circumstances to define her future.

Through faith, perseverance and the support of her loved ones, she rebuilt her life and gained a deeper appreciation for patience, gratitude and life’s small victories.

Most importantly, she said her disability does not limit her abilities or potential.

Her return to work marks more than a return to employment, representing independence, confidence and purpose.

Among her accomplishments since the accident are graduating with honors, launching her own business and resuming her professional career. Castillo also hopes to continue expanding her business and advocating for greater opportunities for persons with disabilities.

Reflecting on her journey, Castillo described herself as “resilient” and encouraged others facing difficult circumstances not to give up. She said it is important to take life one day at a time, celebrate even the smallest victories and believe that brighter days are ahead.

The Belize Port Authority said her story is a reminder that with faith and perseverance, even the toughest odds can be overcome.

World.title: University of Belize host Electric Vehicles and Battery Technology Workshop
World.content:
University of Belize host Electric Vehicles and Battery Technology Workshop

By Zoila Palma: The University of Belize (UB), through its Energy Office, is hosting a 3-day Electric Vehicles and Battery Technology Workshop, facilitated by The University of the West Indies and funded by The Federal Republic of Germany.

UB explained that the hands-on workshop provides participants with practical exposure to electric vehicle systems, battery technology, maintenance, safety, and emerging innovations. It is designed to bridge the gap between academic learning and real-world application while fostering interdisciplinary collaboration among students, professionals, and stakeholders in engineering, environmental science, business, and public policy.

“As Belize advances toward cleaner energy solutions and greater climate resilience, initiatives like this position the University of Belize at the forefront of the technologies shaping the future of transportation and sustainable development,” UB said.

UB says that this initiative reflects UB’s commitment to innovation, research, and workforce development while supporting national priorities in renewable energy, environmental sustainability, and technological advancement.

World.title: International News: Wildfires in Southern Europe claim lives of 3 firefighters, force thousands to evacuate
World.content:
International News: Wildfires in Southern Europe claim lives of 3 firefighters, force thousands to evacuate

By Zoila Palma: Wildfires raging across southern Europe have killed three firefighters and forced about 12,000 people to evacuate as flames continue to spread through parts of France, Italy and Spain.

Two firefighters died while battling a blaze near Bordeaux, France, while a third was killed and another injured while fighting a major fire in Sicily, Italy, Yahoo reports.

In southwestern France, nearly 6,000 acres have burned west of Bordeaux, prompting authorities to order about 10,000 people to leave their homes.

Around 500 firefighters were deployed to tackle the blaze, which began near the town of Saumos and was moving southwest. Several roads were closed, while firefighting aircraft were being sent to assist crews on the ground.

The French department of Var, along the Côte d’Azur between Marseille and Nice, has also been heavily affected, with thousands of acres destroyed.

Some evacuated residents were allowed to return home Thursday, but authorities warned them to limit movement because strong winds could cause the flames to flare up again. In Sicily, thousands were also evacuated as about 6,000 firefighters, forestry officers and civil protection personnel worked to contain several major fires.

Spain has also been battling dangerous wildfires, with footage showing Civil Guard officers going door-to-door to evacuate residents near Madrid.

The latest fires follow a massive blaze in Guadalajara province that burned nearly 80,000 acres and a deadly wildfire in Almería that killed at least 11 people.

World.title: Nearly a kilo of suspected cannabis found under old fridge in San Pedro
World.content:
Nearly a kilo of suspected cannabis found under old fridge in San Pedro

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Police intelligence has led officers to a substantial drug stash on Ambergris Caye, with nearly a kilogram of suspected cannabis found hidden beneath an old refrigerator in an empty lot in San Pedro Town, and no one around to answer for it.

According to the Belize Police Department, at 7:00 p.m., acting on Special Branch intelligence, police conducted a search at an empty lot in the DFC area of San Pedro Town for illegal drugs and ammunition.

During the search, an officer’s attention was drawn to an old refrigerator sitting on the lot. Further checks underneath it led to the discovery of a black plastic bag. When retrieved and opened, the bag was found to contain transparent plastic bags wrapped in white tape, holding a green leafy substance suspected to be cannabis.

No one was in the immediate area at the time of the discovery, and the suspected drugs were retrieved and transported to the San Pedro Police Station.

At the station, the suspected cannabis was weighed, registering 991 grams, just shy of a full kilogram. The drugs were placed in an envelope, properly labelled and sealed, and handed over to the exhibit keeper as found property.

No arrests have been made in connection with the find, and the matter remains under police attention.

The near-kilo seizure ranks among the more significant recent finds on the island, and the intelligence-driven nature of the operation suggests police had the location marked. Whoever stashed the package under that refrigerator now knows it is gone.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the San Pedro police or Crime Stoppers anonymously at 922.

World.title: Teen slashed across the throat in Guinea Grass
World.content:
Teen slashed across the throat in Guinea Grass

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): An 18-year-old fisherman is nursing grievous harm injuries after his throat was slashed during a night out at a Guinea Grass Village restaurant, an attack he says came from a man with whom he never had a problem, and police are investigating with video footage in hand.

According to the Belize Police Department, the young fisherman of Guinea Grass Village, Orange Walk District, reported that on Sunday, July 19, 2026, at about 11:00 p.m., he was socializing with a friend at a restaurant in the village when a man he has known for about three years arrived with his family.

The teen told police the man walked to where they were seated and spoke to him in an aggressive manner, though he cannot recall exactly what was said. He got up holding a beer bottle, and then, he reported, he was suddenly attacked. The next thing he realized, he was cut and bleeding from his throat area, gripping his throat with both hands to stem the bleeding. He told police that fear took over when he realized he had been sliced, and he thought he was going to die.

The backstory he offered police only deepens the puzzle. Earlier that same evening, the teen said, he had given the man’s cousin a ride on his motorcycle to a mechanic shop, where he encountered the man, who told him he had a problem with the teen’s friend. The teen relayed the message, and the friend replied that he had no problem with the man. Hours later, it was the young fisherman himself bleeding from the throat.

The complainant said the restaurant’s lighting allowed him to clearly see his attacker, that he had no quarrel with the man, and that he does not know why anyone would want to hurt him. He requested court action.

A doctor certified his injuries as grievous harm. Police recorded statements from the complainant and a witness, and video footage of the incident has been obtained.

No one has been detained or charged at this time, and the identity of the man reported is being withheld pending charges.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the Orange Walk police or Crime Stoppers anonymously at 922.

World.title: Taxi driver punched into the sea by stranger at San Pedro pier
World.content:
Taxi driver punched into the sea by stranger at San Pedro pier

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A San Pedro taxi driver waiting for a fare ended up in the sea, knocked off his feet by a blow from a man he says he had never seen in his life, and a suspect has now been formally charged with harm.

According to the Belize Police Department, the 27-year-old taxi driver of the San Pedrito Area reported that on Saturday, July 18, 2026, at about 3:15 p.m., he was waiting for an arrival at the entrance of a pier on the beachfront of San Pedro Town when a man approached him from behind and said, “Don’t touch none of my family.”

The taxi driver told police he replied, “I don’t know you,” and continued standing with his back turned. Moments later, he reported, he felt a hard blow to the right side of his head, causing him to lose his balance and fall into the sea.

The ordeal did not end in the water. After getting back to his feet, the man stated, the same attacker approached again and punched him once to the upper chest, causing pain. Bystanders in the area then restrained the attacker, who, according to the report, appeared to be searching for an object to strike him with again.

The complainant told police it was broad daylight with clear weather and an unobstructed view, and that although he had never seen the man before, he could positively identify him after the roughly ten minutes the incident lasted. He was observed with scratches and bruising to his upper chest and complained of head pain, and a doctor certified his injuries as harm.

Police detained a man in connection with the report, and on Tuesday, July 21, formally arrested and charged 27-year-old Ian Earson Young Sr. of the DFC Area, San Pedro Town, with the crime of harm. Cautioned after the charge, he chose to remain silent.

World.title: WATCH: Troy residents protest amid man’s arrest following fatal mobbing over slain 10-year-old
World.content:
Placard-bearing residents protesting in Troy, Trelawny on Thursday morning.

TRELAWNY, Jamaica — Placard-bearing residents of Troy, Trelawny on Thursday morning mounted a roadblock as they demanded the release of a man who they say was arrested in relation to a fatal mobbing two days ago following the gruesome murder of 10-year-old Shani Coke.

The residents also protested over Coke’s death. The child’s partially nude body was found with her throat slashed in bushes on Tuesday.

Police said following the discovery of the child’s body, there was a mob attack on a father and son in the community.

READ: Family grieves bright 10-year-old killed in Troy, as man accused of her murder beaten to death by mob

Residents told the Jamaica Observer that the two men are Shani’s relatives. They accused the son of raping and killing the child. He was beaten, chopped and stoned to death, while his father, who was also attacked by the mob, was admitted to hospital.

Subsequently, police arrested a man in connection with the mob attack. However, residents are demanding his release as they claim he is innocent.

“We blocked the road this morning, and police came and clear most of it. The police came and lockup [a man] and he is innocent, because the guy never went to the mobbing with any machete,” a resident who requested anonymity told Observer Online.

“The whole Troy is in mourning. We can’t stop thinking about the little girl and how she died so awful,” added the resident.

— Kasey Williams

World.title: A light extinguished
World.content:
Shawna Williams-Stevens (left) shows off trophies her niece, 10-year-old Shani Coke, received from Troy Primary School. Looking on is Shani’s mother, Ackeem “Kim” Williams. Kasey Williams

TROY, Trelawny — Huddled on the verandah of their family home, relatives of 10-year-old Shani “Kaidra” Coke, whose partially nude body was found with her throat slashed on Tuesday, remembered the child for her brilliance and radiant smile.

“Shani was born here and lived [with her grandparents], because her [mother] has to work. When Shani goes to school she doesn’t play around. She took her education seriously. From Shani a go basic school she was always first [in her class]. She was always putting out her best. She is from an educated background. Her father is educated and so is her mother,” the child’s aunt Shawna Williams-Stevens told journalists on Wednesday as she stood beside her grieving sister, Shani’s mother Ackeem “Kim” Williams.

The aunt’s hands could not hold the many academic trophies and certificates earned by Shani during her tenure at Troy Primary School.

“From grade one her teachers rewarded her, whether with a stamp in her book or sweets, or you know the teachers always try to elevate her for her to know that she does good. Her mother would always buy her gifts to encourage her,” said Williams-Stevens.

“Right now she was [among] the top students at Troy Primary. If school was keeping it would have to lock today, because of Shani,” added the aunt, while pointing out that up to last Friday Shani was recognised for her participation in summer school.

“All last week she got her certificate to show her brilliance. When you look at her you see the next doctor, lawyer, and they just took her life, just cut her off. Right now we are devastated. Right now we don’t know our head from our feet. Last night we nuh sleep. This is traumatising. Maybe Kaidra was going to come and take her mother out of poverty and they cut her life short and kill her,” Williams-Stevens said before breaking down in tears.

According to a police report, as well as the account of residents, mid-afternoon Tuesday Shani was walking home from a shop along a roadway near her home when she was abducted.

Later, a farmer, who had gone in search of his cow after hearing strange sounds from bushes, made the grisly discovery and raised an alarm.

Police said following the discovery of the child’s body, there was a mob attack on a father and son in the community.

Residents told the Jamaica Observer that the two men are Shani’s relatives. Angry residents accused the son of raping and killing the child. He was beaten, chopped and stoned to death, while his father, who was also attacked by the mob, was admitted to hospital.

Police identified the dead man as Delroy Coke, but did not provide any other information.

Shani’s father, Aston Coke, otherwise called Junior, told journalists that his daughter was well-loved and admired by many in her community.

“Her grandmother sent her to the shop and she did not make it back home. Someone stopped her on the street and disturbed her somehow and slashed her throat… She was loving and caring in the community growing up. Everybody knows her. She knows everyone. She can see you and call you by your full name. She had a sense of humour. She was doing well in school and she got a lot of academic awards,” said the heartbroken father.

“She decided that she wanted to make something out of herself growing up, because we were driving that into her head, but things just happened overnight,” added Coke as he alleged that the man believed to have killed his daughter was a habitual offender.

“It is an act that should never have happened in this neighbourhood,” declared Coke, who is battling his own health problems.

He recounted the last encounter with his daughter over the weekend.

“She came by Saturday afternoon and my uncle was putting on a back-to-school treat up by the community centre and she went there to get bags and food. She was very polite. She stopped by and I said to Kaidra, ‘What you doing here? Aren’t you supposed to be up by the treat?’ She said, ‘Yes, Daddy’ and she walked off and said, ‘Daddy, later when I am coming back I will show you what I get.’ I called her back and went in my wallet to give her money to buy juice,” Coke said.

“That was the first time my uncle and some of my aunts met her. I didn’t get to see her Sunday morning when she went to church and I didn’t get to see her yesterday (Tuesday), because she didn’t come all the way out here to the store,” he said as he reflected on the precious memories and proud moments he spent with his daughter.

“She was always smiling and you never saw her sad. You always saw her happy. Those are the things I remember about her at all times. When it comes to the academics you go by her grandmother’s house, trust me you will see a lot of achievements — trophies — that she got at school. Even sometimes when her mother and grandmother are not around I go by the church to collect them,” he said.

“It is a very sad story to know that this neighbourhood of Troy, Trelawny, has come to this. I don’t know if it is because it reached my doorstep [why] I feel it so pressuring, but things have been happening around here a long time and nobody gets justice,” charged Coke.

World.title: Too late to explain?
World.content:
Chairman of Parliament’s Public Accounts Committee Julian Robinson speaks during Wednesday’s sitting of the parliamentary oversight committee.

PERMANENT secretary in the Office of the Prime Minister Ambassador Rocky Meade has defended the Government’s decision to preserve Hurricane Melissa cash donations for longer-term recovery, insisting the auditor general’s finding that only 1.8 per cent of the funds had been spent did not reflect the Government’s full recovery strategy.

However, after hearing the detailed explanation from Meade during Wednesday’s sitting of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), Chairman Julian Robinson argued that the explanation should have been communicated much earlier and clearer to prevent the public alarm and loss of confidence that followed the audit report.

The discussion emerged as the committee reviewed the auditor general’s compliance audit into governance and procurement under the Hurricane Melissa relief programme, which found that the National Disaster Fund Committee had been non-functional for more than two years.

As members questioned officials about how the committee now operates, the conversation shifted to the controversy sparked by a separate auditor general’s report showing that only 1.8 per cent of the roughly $1.44 billion in Hurricane Melissa cash donations had been spent by February 23, prompting Meade to again defend the Government’s recovery strategy.

Seeking to place those findings in context, Meade told the committee that the Government deliberately prioritised distributing food, medical supplies, building materials and other items donated in kind during the immediate aftermath of the hurricane, while preserving cash donations to support the country’s transition from emergency relief to long-term recovery.

“The point about the percentage of donations that were deployed needs to be put into context. We were getting donations in kind and we got cash donations. The decision that was taken was in the immediate aftermath of the hurricane, while persons were in need of physical items, giving them money would not help them at that time necessarily. They were interested in getting physical items. The funds that we had, the idea was to reserve those funds to acquire and provide for these [modular] units that would give people the recovery,” he explained.

He argued that focusing solely on the amount of cash spent failed to capture the extensive use of donated goods, which he said formed the backbone of the initial relief effort.

“The bottom line to the point is that the totality of the donations we got included cash and kind, and the priority was to use up the resources in kind first. So by reporting that at a certain point, only a small percentage of the donated funds were used, it doesn’t capture the fuller picture that of all the donations, including the kind… we did substantially use up the donations in kind to provide for the immediate need, and it was a part of the plan that most of the funds that were donated would be used for the more medium-term sustainable recovery, including the housing solutions, [and] that’s the context,” he said.

While acknowledging that approach, Robinson said the public had not been given sufficient information to understand why the money remained largely untouched months after the hurricane.

“It’s important to note because people did fundraisers, people went out of their way, and so if you hear eight months post a hurricane that only two per cent of the money has been used, come next hurricane, people aren’t going to be inclined to run and support a fund of this nature… So the communication on that particular issue, I believe, should have been done earlier, probably immediately after the report came out so that there was some greater understanding of what the plan was,” said Robinson.

Meade accepted that the Government could have done more to communicate its strategy, although he maintained that information had been shared through several channels.

“I certainly accept the point that if you saw a gap in communication, it means we didn’t do enough. I can assure you that communication was done, but clearly if there are persons who didn’t hear it, we didn’t do enough… I accept your point in principle, and we will do even more than we did,” said Meade.

Updating the committee on the recovery programme, Meade said the cash donations are now being used to support the modular housing initiative, including the construction of foundations and installation of utilities.

He disclosed that the Government had initially targeted the procurement of 2,500 modular units, with about 1,200 already in Jamaica for families who suffered total or near-total loss of their homes during Hurricane Melissa.

World.title: For the love of music
World.content:
Veteran dancehall selector Supa Twitch has credited his enduring passion for music, discipline, and unwavering respect for sound system culture as the keys to a career that has remained relevant for nearly four decades.

Fresh from a standout performance at the recent Joyride event, Supa Twitch said the atmosphere was a reminder of why the music of the 1990s and early 2000s continues to resonate with fans across generations.

“Joyride was special. The crowd came to feel the music, not just hear it. You could feel the nostalgia in the air, with people singing every lyric from my 90s set like it dropped yesterday. When I touched the stage the energy was electric. It was pure love, which is the magic of a real dancehall crowd,” he said.

Born in Hartford, Connecticut, and raised in east Kingston, Supa Twitch attended St Aloysius Primary School before moving on to St. George’s College. He relocated to New York in 1991 and is now based in Miami, although he describes the road as his true office.

“I was in love with dancehall from the age of 10 and used to sneak out just to listen to sound systems,” he recalled.

His professional journey began in 1988 with the east Kingston-based Supersonic sound system before moving to Black Stone the following year.

Inspired by legendary selectors Rory of Stone Love and Webba of Black Stone, Supa Twitch said he quickly realised that selecting was about much more than playing records.

“A selector doesn’t just play tunes; a selector moves people. I wanted to move people,” he told the Jamaica Observer.

After migrating to New York, he joined Afrique Soundstation, where he worked alongside respected figures including Jagga B, Crazy Richie, and the late Supa Claude.

“That was school for me. They taught me versatility and showed me how to take dancehall global without losing my roots,” he shared.

Reflecting on his longevity in one of the world’s most competitive music cultures, Supa Twitch said staying true to the music has always come first.

“You have to respect the music, evolve without selling out, and bring 100 per cent every time you perform. Most importantly, you have to keep loving the music. Once that love disappears, it starts feeling like a job,” the selector charged.

While acknowledging that today’s dancehall industry offers artistes unprecedented global opportunities through digital platforms, he believes something valuable has been lost.

“The talent is definitely there today, but the golden era had more artiste development and stronger connections between artists and sound systems. Back then, a tune had to pass the dance test before it hit radio. Now a song can trend and disappear in two weeks,” the veteran reasoned.

For Supa Twitch, events like Joyride play a vital role in preserving Jamaica’s rich sound system heritage.

“Joyride acts as both an archive and an amplifier. It reminds the new generation where the music comes from and reminds my generation why we fell in love with it in the first place. Sound system culture is Jamaica’s original social media,” he said.

One of the biggest highlights of his Joyride performance came when he playfully convinced female patrons he was about to play only hard-core dancehall selections before surprising them with classic soul and R&B favourites.

“I had them singing every single word. That created the biggest vibe of the entire night,” he told the Observer.

Among his proudest achievements are founding Supa Sound in 2005, winning the 2014 International Reggae and World Music Awards (IRAWMA) for Florida’s Most Popular Dance DJ, and successfully touring Japan annually between 2013 and 2019.

Looking ahead, Supa Twitch revealed plans for an extensive international touring schedule, including Europe, Canada, and a return to Japan later this year, with Australia targeted for 2027. He is also expanding his acting career following his appearance in the 2025 film Unbelievable.

World.title: Final push to get PEP students high school-ready
World.content:
Permanent secretary in the Ministry of Education Dr Kasan Troupe delivers her remarks at the handover ceremony of nine CIBC Caribbean prepaid cards to principals affected by last October’s Hurricane Melissa at the bank’s corporate office in New Kingston.Garfield Robinson

THE Ministry of Education is expecting at least 80 per cent of the 1,341 students enrolled in its special summer numeracy and literacy programme, for those who did not attain mastery scores in their Primary Exit Profile (PEP) examinations, to meet that benchmark before they enter high school in September.

After PEP results were released in June, the education ministry reported that of the 31,677 students who sat the exam, 75 per cent achieved mastery in numeracy assessments, while 79 per cent demonstrated mastery in literacy.

At the time, portfolio minister Senator Dr Dana Morris Dixon indicated that those students who performed at near mastery and non-mastery levels would be sought out by the ministry to ensure that no child is left behind.

On Tuesday, permanent secretary in the ministry Dr Kasan Troupe told the Jamaica Observer that those students are now being engaged in an intense three-week, Government-funded, summer programme that runs until the end of July and which will target their weak areas and reassess their level of competence upon its completion.

“Right now, as indicated by our minister, the plan is for us to have a majority of our students, if not all, go to high school literate. As you know, we have been working on that as an education system,” said Troupe at the handover ceremony of CIBC Caribbean prepaid cards to nine principals affected by last October’s Hurricane Melissa, at the bank’s corporate office in New Kingston.

“We saw a 10 per cent improvement in the level of mastery for literacy this year. The same students who we assessed this year, when they got their mastery scores in grade four it was 69 per cent, and this year it is 79 per cent, and we identified some students who are on the cusp. If it was a little bit more we would have got them there. So, the thrust now is to run them through an intensive literacy and numeracy initiative,” said Troupe.

The permanent secretary explained that the first week of the programme was used to conduct assessments that identified where students were on their journey of becoming numerate and literate. She noted that the information garnered from those tests was then used to form their learning plan for the next two weeks.

While acknowledging that attempting to achieve mastery in three weeks would be a challenge, she argued that the ministry is well equipped to provide students with the material needed to help them along the way.

“Some persons would say what we didn’t do in six years we’re going to try to do in a summer. That’s not absolutely true; it is like an intensive programme. And we are deploying literacy software and licenses that we have procured, [so] we are using that as well, and we have our Jamaica Learning Passport that is built around literacy and numeracy support, so we are pulling in the ICT [information and communications technology], we are pulling in the readers, and we have equipped the regions,” she said.

Troupe told the Observer that students are being thoroughly monitored throughout the programme, and those who are still unable to secure mastery will undergo a Government-funded psychoeducational assessment which will then help to shape their curriculum at the high schools they attend in September.

“We are now working with those receiving schools to ensure that the learning programmes are developed in response to the gaps identified in those learners. We are restructuring some of those learning programmes in some of those high schools to limit the number of subjects the students are exposed to; to increase the amount of time that they will need in literacy, numeracy, language arts, mathematics, ICT, physical education, and I think social studies and personal development,” she said, explaining that students will matriculate to other subject areas once they improve.

She added that students were grouped in selected nearby schools or other institutions closest to them so that they have ease in accessing the summer programme. Troupe added that the initiative was designed to minimise spending for parents.

“We have also looked at providing nutritional support through Nutrition Products Limited for the students, we provided the teachers or the tutors — and that is something that the Government is fully funding — so the parents are not contributing to summer school in any way — we are paying. It’s fully funded by the Government. We have our principals who are coordinating, we have our literacy coaches and specialists who have been deployed into the field,” she said.

Troupe also called on parents to make the extra effort to send their children to summer school, charging that persistent commitment to their child’s improvement is what will eventually make the difference.

“We are asking our parents to make the sacrifice. And if they can’t afford whatever it is, let us know because we will make the sacrifice and put the resources in place — because the end game is for all of our students to be literate before they go to high school,” declared Troupe.

World.title: Back the Girlz!
World.content:
Members of the Reggae Girlz team celebrate their fourth goal against Antigua and Barduda during their Group B match in the Concacaf Women’s qualifiers at the National Stadium on April 10, 2026. (Photo: Naphtali Junior)

FIFA Consultant and Women’s Football Division Advisor Jose Andres Portabella believes the long-term growth of women’s football in Jamaica hinges on meaningful support for the Reggae Girlz in their bid to reach a third successive FIFA Women’s World Cup.

In less than four months, the national senior women’s team will take on Costa Rica in the quarter-finals of the Concacaf W Championship in Texas, USA, with victory securing a place in next year’s World Cup in Brazil.

It would continue a historic run for the team, which stunned the world at the 2019 tournament in France and the 2023 tournament in Australia and New Zealand.

Despite their impressive performances over the past decade, the Reggae Girlz have struggled to attract consistent, lucrative sponsorship and sustained fan support, although more than 6,500 supporters turned out at the National Stadium for their 2-0 win over Guyana in April.

Portabella told the Jamaica Observer that stronger backing for the Reggae Girlz would not only boost the team’s success but also help drive the long-term development of the sport locally.

“I would love to see the whole country rally behind the Reggae Girlz. They have a beautiful opportunity to go three times in a row to a World Cup – that is special, it’s not every country that can say that. So I would love to see the Jamaican people come together and get behind the Reggae Girlz in a way that no one has ever seen before,” he said.

“If we see that, I think the Girlz will respond to the country in an amazing way, and it will inspire a completely new generation to really see the pathway to play football, to enjoy football and to one day excel in football at the global stage.”

Portabella was a key figure in helping the Jamaica Football Federation (JFF) to develop and launch its Women’s Strategic Plan, which outlines several key objectives to be achieved in the sport by 2031.

The world governing body is prepared to provide more than $41 million in funding to support JFF programmes focused on national teams, league and club development, as well as governance and leadership.

Portabella believes Jamaica has the potential to build one of the best women’s football programmes, provided all stakeholders play their part.

“FIFA definitely sees Jamaica (with) huge potential in women’s football. Not only potential, but already a proven track record,” he said. “Your national teams have been spectacular at youth and senior level so we’re looking forward to seeing what the future holds for Jamaica, for the players here, the clubs. Your women’s Premier League is continuing to grow in a fantastic way. The future is truly bright for them and at national team level as well.”

“It’s not only the success that you see from the players, but coaches, we want to see more women coaches out there. We want to see young kids participate in the sport at a grassroots level so I think the future is quite bright for Jamaica as a whole. The JFF and the Women’s Premier League need to continue to work together with their clubs, all stakeholders, to really take things to the next level.”

JFF Projects Committee Chairperson for Women’s Programmes Carlene Edwards, who also serves on FIFA’s Women’s National Competitions Committee, says improving the club system will also prove crucial in improving the sport.

“My greatest wish for women’s football is that we get it really to a professional level,” she told the Jamaica Observer. “I think based on the strategy, we are aiming to at least get to some sort of professionalism by 2031. With what Concacaf is now doing around club licensing, I think later this year we’re supposed to be seeing the rolling out of the women’s club licence and I believe that is one element to actually get our clubs at least to a level of professionalisation.”

“I believe as we transition in 2031, I’m hoping as well that our players can be paid some sorts, I think that would be the greatest wish.”

World.title: Enter The DoughJo Ja
World.content:
The DoughJo Ja principal Kimberly Clarke. (Photo: Instagram/@thedoughjo.ja)

Sourdough lovers, celebrate! The DoughJo Ja has officially landed on the shelves of Loshusan Supermarket bringing a freshly baked line-up of handcrafted sourdough treats to locals.

Officially launched in April 2026 by principal Kimberly Clarke, the brand was born out of a personal search for gluten-friendly options using wild fermination techniques.

“It started from my search for healtheir bread that wouldn’t necessarily trigger my gluten sensitivity,” Clarke said. “I used to post TikTok videos of me making the bread and then persons eventually showed interested in them,” shared Clarke.

Within a matter of months, she has transitioned seamlessly from social media posts to online orders and, ultimately, supermarket shelves. Shoppers can now pick up handcrafted sourdough loaves in original, 100 per cent whole wheat, and sharp cheddar ranging from $1,800 to $2,200, as well as sourdough blueberry crumble muffins for $2,400.

Delighted by the enthusiastic response and the shift towards healthier choices, Clarke ensures every creation is made with meticulous care and patience.

World.title: Schools under scrutiny
World.content:
Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth & Information’s Region One Director Ottis Brown addressing the region’s One Back-to-School Conference held at Grand Palladium Hotel and Spa in Point, Hanover, on Tuesday.Anthony Lewis

POINT, Hanover — The Ministry of Education, Skills, Youth & Information’s Region One Director Ottis Brown has sounded the alarm over what he alleges are numerous accounting breaches in primary schools within Kingston and St Andrew.

“The breaches are too many. Here is what is happening now, colleagues. We are getting documents from the Integrity Commission (IC) for principals to be investigated… Accountability is stepping up,” he said.

Brown made the revelation, Tuesday, during the second of a three-day back-to-school conference for Region One that was held at Grand Palladium Hotel and Spa in Point, Hanover.

“Stakeholders in the communities are writing to the ministry. They talk about what they observe in schools. They go to a school and they get no receipt for the money they pay. They call you and ask if they should get a receipt and what it should look like,” he told an audience of educators.

The regional director said primary schools are the main offenders.

“Do you know where we tend to find the bulk of the breaches now? The primary schools. It’s a serious problem,” said Brown.

While he conceded that there may be administrative issues such as inadequate staff that impact how money is handled, he said there can be no excuse for some of the behaviour seen.

“Some simple things. Why would you keep money in excess of a million dollars locked up in a room for two, three weeks, months, and so forth? The bursar not being there caused that? So what I’m saying: I know you need those people, and we are working on that, but don’t do things to set up yourselves in the process,” added the senior officer.

Brown used the opportunity to explain proper administrative procedures when handling school funds.

“I beg you, lodge the money in a reasonable time frame. Money must be lodged intact. Can somebody please explain what the FAA (Financial Administration and Audit) Act means when it says ‘money must be lodged intact’? ‘[It means as soon] as collected,” he emphasised.

He explained that if five $100-notes are collected, that exact configuration must be deposited into the account.

“Don’t use it to make any change for anybody who wants to pay somebody something. That is what they mean [by] to lodge the money intact. If you are guilty, don’t say anything. Just sit like nothing is wrong but pray a prayer in your heart. I’m giving you 30 seconds to ask God to forgive you,” stated Brown to an outburst of laughter.

“You saved the money, but the law says treat it a particular way,” added the senior officer.

During his address Brown also expressed gratitude to the Ministry of Education for providing the region with additional professionals to conduct audits of schools within the region.

“We want to publicly say thanks to the members of the central ministry team, our CEO, [and] the permanent secretary. We spoke and they have given us a large number of people to build out the finance unit in the region. I have about five or six additional staff members now so we can do more audits. Clap the central team for that,” he said magnanimously.

World.title: EU’s Google fine risks triggering Trump as he gears up for more tariffs
World.content:
European officials insist that the two-part fine on Google that includes €460 million for favoring its own search services and €430 million for the unfair way the Play Store is installed on smartphones, has nothing to do with trade policy. Brussels says the penalties reflect normal enforcement of EU law, like a similar fine against China’s Alibaba earlier this week. They also note that the total penalty is relatively modest, amounting to around 0.22 percent of the global annual turnover of Google’s parent company, Alphabet.

“We'd rather have a very friendly relationship with all our partners but we are not going to refrain from acting because one of our partners doesn't like our law,” said Teresa Ribera, the European Commission's executive vice president for competition policy.

But that European attempt to keep the Google case separate from trade policy is unlikely to count for much in Washington as Trump gears up for his new tariff round.

U.S. trade czar Jamieson Greer said the “EU’s recent actions ... pose a real risk to the continuation of transatlantic stability with respect to trade” while Andrew Puzder, the U.S. ambassador to the EU, called the Google fine “the latest example of Brussels using regulation as a blunt instrument against American innovation.”

U.S. lawmakers this week also called on Trump to push back against the EU’s “discriminatory” digital policies and keep up the pressure on Brussels in order to defend American interests. The Republican legislators thanked the president for his “recent threat to impose tariffs” on countries imposing a digital service tax. The appeal underscored how the EU’s regulation of U.S. tech firms has become intertwined with domestic politics, particularly ahead of the U.S. midterm elections in November.

The expiration of the temporary 10 percent tariffs on Friday opens the way for the administration to rebuild its tariffs against Europe using other legal mechanisms.

World.title: L’UE inflige à Google une amende de 890 millions d’euros pour son moteur de recherche et son app store
World.content:
Ces sanctions sont prononcées plus de deux ans après l’ouverture des procédures par la Commission en mars 2024, parallèlement à des enquêtes visant Apple et Meta, qui se sont soldées par des amendes en avril 2025.

La Commission avait pris une décision en interne dès le mois de mars, ce qui avait suscité des critiques de la part d’organisations professionnelles et de la société civile, qui reprochaient à Bruxelles de freiner l’application de la réglementation pour éviter de s'attirer les foudres de Washington.

L’amende la plus élevée, d’un montant de 460 millions d’euros, concerne la pratique dite de “self-preferencing” ou autopréférence : la Commission a en effet constaté que le moteur de recherche affichait de façon plus visible les propres services de Google en matière d’e-commerce, d’hôtellerie, de transports et de sport que ceux de ses concurrents.

La seconde, d’un montant de 430 millions d’euros, concerne le Play Store installé sur les smartphones fonctionnant sous le système d’exploitation Android. La Commission a constaté que Google empêchait les développeurs d’applications d’informer les utilisateurs de l’existence d’offres moins chères disponibles en dehors de l’app store, et que, par ailleurs, elle facturait des frais liés aux redirections des utilisateurs vers les applications dépassant les limites autorisées par la loi.

Ces amendes, bien que substantielles, sont nettement inférieures à celles infligées par Bruxelles à Google pour pratiques anticoncurrentielles : la Cour de justice de l’UE a récemment confirmé une amende de plus de 4 milliards d’euros, décidée en 2018 par la Commission européenne, après avoir conclu que Google avait abusé de sa position dominante via Android.

Cela vient du fait que le DMA cherche d’abord à lutter contre les positions dominantes sur le marché en collaborant avec les entreprises pour qu’elles modifient leur mode de fonctionnement.

World.title: Linnemann wird offenbar neuer Gesundheitsminister
World.content:
Linnemann war bereits zu Beginn der Legislatur im Gespräch für ein Ministeramt. Der 48-Jährige sollte ursprünglich Wirtschaftsminister werden, lehnte die Position aber ab. Er wäre lieber Arbeitsminister geworden, wie er der „Welt“ sagte (hier). Das Ressort ging aber an die SPD. Am Ende blieb Linnemann Generalsekretär seiner Partei. Er ist seit 2009 Mitglied des Deutschen Bundestags für den Wahlkreis Paderborn.

Warken hinterlässt ihrem Nachfolger eine abgeschlossene Finanzreform der Gesetzlichen Krankenversicherung und eine angestoßene Pflegereform, die nach der Sommerpause ins Kabinett kommen soll. Auch hier muss ein Milliardendefizit ausgeglichen werden. Warken hat zudem eine Strukturreform für das deutsche Gesundheitswesen angestoßen. Hierzu soll die Finanzkommission Gesundheit erste Vorschläge gegen Jahresende machen.

Die Nominierung Warkens zur Gesundheitsministerin im vergangenen Jahr galt als Überraschung. Die Juristin kam als Quereinsteigerin in das Ressort. Durch die noch kurz vor der Sommerpause verabschiedeten GKV-Reform hatte sie sich dann zwar Respekt innerhalb der Union verschafft. Warken gilt als ideal für den Posten der Kanzleramtschefin, bei dem sie im Hintergrund agieren wird.

Das zeigen die Worte von Kanzler Friedrich Merz nach dem Kabinettsbeschluss des GKV-Beitragssatzstabilisierungsgesetzes (hier). „Sie hat mit sehr viel Mut, mit Augenmaß, mit Ehrlichkeit, mit Empathie eine Reform vorgelegt, die beispielhaft ist für all die großen Reformen, die wir in der Koalition noch leisten wollen“, so Merz über Warken. Ihrer Entschlossenheit und dem Tempo gebühre „allergrößte Anerkennung“.

World.title: You won’t see the back of me before year-end, says ECB’s Lagarde
World.content:
“You are not going to see the back of me before 2027, OK?” Lagarde, who served as minister under conservative Presidents Jacques Chirac and Nicolas Sarkozy, said during a press conference Thursday afternoon following the ECB’s decision to keep interest rates at 2.25 percent.

The ECB president has issued several messages, not always consistent, on whether she will stay in office until the end of her term.

She today repeated that she would not leave the Bank in times of economic turbulence, returning to the same nautical metaphor she used earlier this month and arguing that speculations about her future are "not particularly important."

“When there are clouds on the horizon, the captain stays on the ship. This captain is staying on the ship.”

Lagarde warned that "the flaring up of the conflict" in the Middle East could further raise inflation.

"The risks to the inflation outlook are to the upside. The energy shock could intensify further and its effects on other prices and wages could be stronger than currently expected," she said.

World.title: Germany rebukes Trump over South Africa’s G20 ban
World.content:
The U.S. president announced in a social media post last November that South Africa would not be invited to the next G20 meeting.

South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola also slammed Trump's decision during a joint press conference with Wadephul. "No country can decide on its own to disinvite a founding member of the G20", he said. Other members attending the summit in Miami should put this member on the table: "There must be a discussion … Can you still call it a G20, when a founding member is excluded?", Lamola said.

Wadephul also emphasized his interest in fostering closer relations with South Africa, despite disagreements on key geopolitical questions like Russia's war in Ukraine, the Gaza conflict or China. As a BRICS member, South Africa holds traditionally close relations to Moscow and Beijing.

"In some disputed matters we can agree to disagree", he said. "And at the same time keep on working together. What matters is that we are committed to the same international principles."

Wadephul said at that press conference that he was "confident that this hiatus will not be permanent, but that South Africa will be able to participate again as a full member of the G20 next year."

Wadephul also argued that Russia "continues to pose an existential security threat to us," which was made evident by Russia's Iskander ballistic missiles in Kaliningrad, which "would take only a matter of minutes to reach Berlin."

On China, he said that both countries should work more closely together as they were both "too dependent on supply chains coming from one country. We’re too dependent on one country as being the most important market."

This article has been updated.

World.title: France’s far left faces accusations of antisemitism from Olympics DJ
World.content:
On Saturday, Butch was forced to interrupt a show in the southeastern town of Grenoble amid heckling and reports that objects had been thrown at the stage.

“I was extremely scared, so much so. And the shock was such that I couldn’t move for days,” Butch said on Thursday. “And now there are new calls to boycott that have been made by the France Unbowed [locally].”

Critics, including former prime minister and presidential hopeful Gabriel Attal, have accused the far left of targeting Butch because she is Jewish. France Unbowed and Mélenchon, who has been gaining ground against centrist candidates in recent polls ahead of next year’s presidential election, have previously faced accusations of antisemitism.

Ahead of Butch’s show in Grenoble, local branches of France Unbowed and pro-Palestinian activists called for a boycott and protest, accusing her of supporting Israel. In a leaflet, they said she had “censored Palestinian voices” by signing a petition backing controversial French draft legislation against antisemitism in 2024. The bill was later dropped.

France Unbowed has been on the defensive over the incident. Mathilde Panot, the leader of its parliamentary group, said Wednesday that the leaflet targeting Butch was “bad.”

World.title: Russia chokes Ukraine’s lifeline Black Sea export corridor
World.content:
The attacks forced shipping giant Maersk to stop operations at the Chornomorsk Fishing Port in the Odesa region this week, redirecting cargo to Romania’s Constanta Port. Ukraine says it would still provide security, but the vessel owners decided to halt traffic due to heightened security threats.

“Previously, there had also been many hits on ships, but most of them concerned ships already docked in ports,” Andrii Klymenko, head of the Black Sea and Baltic Strategic Research Monitoring Group, told POLITICO. Vessel owners have halted operations, wanting to see how the situation unfolds and what new solution Ukraine can find, Klymenko added.

Russia's actions prompted Ukraine to request an urgent U.N. Security Council meeting for July 27, urging all states to immediately demand that Moscow stop its attacks on freedom of navigation in the Black Sea.

The attacks intensified after Ukraine conducted a series of successful strikes against Russian shadow fleet oil tankers in the Azov and Black Seas, forcing Russia to halt exports earlier this month.

But it would be wrong to say that’s a response, because Russia never paused the attacks on Ukraine’s ports and cargo, Klymenko said. “This narrative would only help Russia to force a maritime ceasefire on us, which would benefit only the Kremlin, as it has to sell oil,” the expert added.

Ukraine’s Navy spokesman Dmytro Pletenchuk said there is a big difference, as while Russia shells vessels operating in a completely legal way, Ukraine targets cargo vessels breaking maritime law by illegally transporting sanctioned oil or entering ports of Ukraine’s occupied territories.

“The war in the sea never stopped. We have already been in a similar situation. Yes, pressure increased, and yes, shipping companies see risks and reduce operations. But we will keep working to restore maximum capacity of our maritime corridor," Pletenchuk added.

Russia’s blockade of Ukrainian ports in 2022 strangled vital agricultural exports and helped drive global food prices more than 60 percent higher by March. But after Ukraine’s navy established a protected maritime corridor in the Black Sea, the country exported more than 168.9 million tons of cargo through it, including over 100 million tons of grain, much of it bound for countries in the Global South, despite repeated Russian attacks on Odesa’s ports.

World.title: Countdown to the ballot: Zambia gears up for August elections
World.content:
This week on Spotlight on Africa, we're heading to Zambia, where general elections are set to take place on the 13th August. Voters will go to the polls to elect a president, members of the National Assembly, councillors and council chairs. Incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema has already picked up endorsements from within his own camp, the UPND Alliance, the coalition that's held power since 2021. So what's at stake, and who's in the running?

Advertising

This week on the podcast, we're heading to Zambia, which is gearing up for elections next month and is now in full campaign mode. Two of our RFI colleagues, Yang Mei and Igor Strauss, travelled to Zambia recently for in-depth reporting on four years of Hakainde Hichilema's rule, and his chances of re-election.

In power since August 2021, "HH", as he's most often called, is a businessman, farmer and politician, and the seventh president of Zambia.

General elections are due to be held in the country on 13 August 2026 to elect a president, members of the National Assembly, councillors and council chairs.

The year ahead for African democracy: who is going to the polls in 2026?

Hichilema has received endorsements from some members of the UPND Alliance, including from the leaders of the Party of National Unity and Progress and the Movement for Multi-Party Democracy.

According to an opinion poll conducted by a University of Zambia demographer, Hichilema is set to be re-elected, leading with 60 percent of the vote, while the combined opposition would take 35 percent.

Zambia's Hichilema sworn in, becoming rare opposition president in southern Africa

Our colleagues Yang Mei and Igor Strauss bring us some of the interviews they gathered on the ground, so join us as we hear from ordinary Zambians, as well as from leading journalist Joseph Mwenda, editor-in-chief at News Diggers, who has led multiple investigations into the current government's relations with China; and from Robert Mwale, an economist and Lead Public Finance and Economic Governance Researcher at the Centre for Trade Policy and Development (CTPD).

Among the issues at stake are a lack of freedom of expression, but also a legacy of economic growth, driven in no small part by China's heavy involvement in the economy.

Thanks to our reporters, Igor Strauss and Yang Mei, for their work and insight, and thank you for listening.

This is the last episode of the 2025–26 season. We'll be back in September with another one.

Spotlight on Africa is produced by RFI's English language service. This episode was mixed by Erwan Rome.
