World.title: Garcia Confident as Hajduk Face Pafos in Europa League Qualifying
World.content:
Hajduk take on Cyprus’s Pafos tomorrow at Poljud in the second qualifying round of the Europa League, with kick-off set for 9 pm. Coach Gonzalo Garcia and player Dario Melnjak previewed the tie on Wednesday.

Garcia outlined what he expects from Pafos.

“They’re a side that competed in the Champions League last season. They have quality and experience, so we’ll be up against a tough opponent. We saw how they played in pre-season, but we’ll see what tomorrow brings. I expect them to be competitive and to push us to give our absolute best,” he said.

Hajduk went into the Žilina tie as favorites, but the situation is different this time around.

“I don’t think we were favorites against Žilina either. Pafos aren’t bigger favorites than us. If we play as a team, we have a chance. That’s how it was against Žilina, and that’s how it will be against other sides,” said the Hajduk coach.

“There are two legs to be played. When we play at home, we have the advantage of our supporters, and this is a chance to use that to our benefit. We’ll go for the win. If we get a good result, we’ll be in a better position — and if not, we’ll have another 90 minutes away from home,” he added.

Can we expect to see Marko Livaja in the starting line-up?

“We never discuss the starting lineup. Livaja is fighting to earn his place back in the first 11, and I support that, because we need the real Livaja — motivated, competitive and full of drive. We’ll see, but I think you already know the answer,” Garcia said.

Melnjak revealed the mood in the dressing room.

“The atmosphere is good. We got through to the next round, and our goal is to keep progressing. Compared to Žilina, Pafos are a different kind of side, but we need to stay true to ourselves,” he said.

In the games against Žilina, Melnjak played on the left wing rather than at left-back.

“It’s all ‘left’ in the end, and I believe that with experience you need to be ready for any position,” he said.

Hajduk have had a slightly lighter schedule, with just one match a week before the domestic season gets underway.

“Since our pre-season was shorter, we’re building match by match. I hope our form keeps improving and that we get better and sharper as we go,” said the Hajduk player.

Legendary Brazilian center-back David Luiz also previewed the tie.

“This is a new chapter in my career and a big test at the start of the season. We have a squad that can fight for titles, and I’ve been lucky in my career to have played for clubs like this,” Luiz said.

The Brazilian icon has had the chance to play alongside several Croatian players during his career.

“It’s always been a pleasure to play with Croatians. Kovačić is one of the best I’ve played with, but I’ve played with plenty of others too. Hajduk have a lot of brilliant young players. It’ll be tough, but it’s a privilege. We’re in for a great football atmosphere,” said David Luiz.

The Brazilian is 39 years old but is still performing at the highest level.

“I rest, I watch what I eat, and I’m privileged to be healthy — that’s the most important thing. I want to help the team. God gave me the chance to play football and I have no complaints. Go to a hospital and see sick children there, and then you’ll see what a real problem looks like,” David Luiz said.

World.title: Dinamo Draw at the Start of Champions League Qualifying
World.content:
Dinamo Zagreb played out a 1-1 draw against Thun in Switzerland in the first leg of the Champions League second qualifying round. The hosts took the lead through a Brighton Labeau goal in the 20th minute, before Miha Zajc set the final score in the 86th minute. The tie will be decided in the return leg in Zagreb in a week.

Thun are the first of three potential opponents Dinamo must overcome to secure a place in the Champions League group stage. The second round is followed by the third round and then the play-off. Dinamo’s possible third-round opponent will be the winner of the tie between KÍ Klaksvík of the Faroe Islands and Lithuania’s Kauno Žalgiris. Should they fall to Thun, Dinamo would continue their European campaign in the Europa League third qualifying round against the loser of the tie between Hapoel Be’er Sheva and Vikingur.

After a quiet start, the Swiss side took the lead in the 20th minute. Fabio Fehr’s cross from the right caught goalkeeper Ivan Filipović out, and Brighton Labeau headed home to make it 1-0. Just a minute earlier, Filipović had misjudged a free-kick delivery but redeemed himself by saving two efforts from the home side.

Dinamo almost leveled quickly, but Dion Drena Beljo’s effort in the 22nd minute went straight into the hands of goalkeeper Niklas Steffen. The Thun keeper also did well to save a fine long-range attempt from Moris Valinčić in the 28th minute. Thun’s best chance to extend their lead came in the 30th minute, when Furkan Dursun found himself unmarked five metres out but headed wide of the post.

Dinamo created a few more openings before halftime, but efforts from Miha Zajc and Gabriel Vidović fell short, and Thun led 1-0.

Dinamo continued to press after the restart. In the 53rd minute, Beljo’s header from a corner was cleared off the line by a home defender, and in the 65th minute a Mislav Oršić effort was again blocked on its way towards goal. Thun threatened on the counter, coming closest in the 73rd minute when Valmir Matoshi’s shot went narrowly wide.

Dinamo’s persistence paid off in the 86th minute. Fran Topić, on since the 79th minute, supplied the assist from the right for Miha Zajc, and the Slovenian midfielder finished first-time from 17 meters to make it 1-1. The score remained unchanged until the final whistle, leaving the tie to be settled in Zagreb.

World.title: Will Smith Visits Rimac Campus Near Zagreb
World.content:
July the 22nd, 2026 – Hollywood star Will Smith paid a visit to Rimac Campus near Zagreb this week, where he was treated to something special indeed.

The well known actor was given a behind-the-scenes look at one of Croatia’s most celebrated technology companies, and judging by his reaction, he was thoroughly impressed! Poslovni reports that the Oscar-winning actor toured the state-of-the-art headquarters of Rimac Technology, meeting founder and CEO Mate Rimac while exploring the cutting-edge engineering and production facilities that have helped place Croatia firmly on the global automotive map.

During the visit, Smith experienced several of Rimac’s innovations firsthand, including the company’s world-renowned electric hypercars. Videos shared from the visit captured the actor reacting with visible excitement, laughing, shouting in amazement and expressing disbelief at the performance and technology on display. According to those present, Smith was particularly impressed by the speed, engineering and innovation that have become synonymous with the Rimac name.

putting croatian innovation on stage

Founded by Mate Rimac back in 2009, the company has grown from a small garage startup into one of the world’s leading developers of high-performance electric vehicle technology. Today, Rimac supplies advanced battery systems, electric powertrains and software to some of the biggest names in the automotive industry, while its Nevera hypercar has repeatedly broken global performance records. The Rimac Campus, located in Kerestinec on the outskirts of Zagreb, has become a symbol of Croatia’s growing reputation as a centre for advanced engineering and innovation.

Smith’s visit shines another international spotlight on one of Croatia’s biggest business success stories. Over the past few years, the company has welcomed politicians, investors, automotive executives and celebrities eager to see firsthand how a Croatian startup evolved into a global technology powerhouse. The visit also serves as another reminder that Croatia’s international reputation is increasingly being shaped not only by tourism, but also by world-class innovation and high-tech manufacturing.

more than just fast cars…

While Rimac’s electric hypercars often capture the headlines, the company has become equally important as a technology partner for the wider automotive industry. Its expertise in battery systems, electric drivetrains and vehicle software is helping shape the next generation of electric mobility, with technologies developed in Croatia finding their way into vehicles produced around the world. For Will Smith, the visit offered a glimpse into the future of transportation. For Croatia, it was another high-profile endorsement of a company that continues to demonstrate the country’s ability to compete at the highest possible levels of global technology.

World.title: Largest Croatian Cave System Was Discovered by Chance
World.content:
July the 22nd, 2026 – The largest Croatian cave system was discovered entirely by chance, and it revealed fascinating evidence of a 20,000 year old hunter…

The largest Croatian cave, located in beautiful Ogulin, is widely considered to be the country’s most remarkable archaeological and natural treasure. More interestingly still, it owes its entire discovery to pure chance.

The Đula-Medvedica Cave System, the largest cave complex in all of Croatia, was uncovered unexpectedly during railway construction back during the early 20th century. Putni kofer writes that what initially began as an ambitious but otherwise normal engineering project soon turned into one of the country’s most significant archaeological discoveries in history, revealing evidence of human life dating back tens of thousands of years.

the best discoveries usually happen by accident…

What eventually turned out to be the largest Croatian cave system ever discovered came to light while workers were building the railway through Ogulin, exposing a vast underground network hidden deep beneath the landscape. Subsequent exploration revealed kilometres upon kilometres of interconnected passages, underground chambers and various waterways, making it the largest known cave complex in Croatia and an important site for both speleologists and scientists.

a present-day window into prehistoric croatia

Among the cave’s most extraordinary discoveries was the bone of a prehistoric hunter estimated to be around 20,000 years old. Archaeologists also uncovered numerous traces of Ice Age human activity, confirming that the cave provided shelter to people living in the region during the last Ice Age. The finds have helped researchers better understand how prehistoric communities survived in what is now Croatia during one of Europe’s harshest climatic periods.

Beyond its archaeological importance, the deep Đula-Medvedica Cave System is renowned for its geological features. The labyrinth of passages includes underground rivers, enormous chambers, dramatic rock formations and unique ecosystems that support species specially adapted to life in complete darkness. Because of its scientific value and fragile environment, much of the cave remains protected and is accessible only to researchers and experienced cavers.

ogulin’s subterranean attraction

While many visitors know Ogulin as the hometown of Croatian fairy-tale writer Ivana Brlić-Mažuranić, this picturesque but often bypassed area is also home to one of Croatia’s most fascinating karst landscapes. The rich cave system lies beneath a region shaped by many sinking rivers and limestone formations that have been carved over millions of years, creating an extraordinary underground world hidden in depths, far beneath the town.

the discovery was a turning point for croatian archaeology

Over a century has now passed since its accidental discovery, and yet the Đula-Medvedica Cave System continues to provide valuable insights into Croatia’s natural and human history. From prehistoric hunter-gatherer human remains to utterly spectacular geological formations, this incredible cave stands as an eternal reminder that some of the country’s greatest discoveries have happened entirely by accident, lying patiently in wait, deep beneath the surface, until the right moment revealed them to the world.

World.title: Iraq, Iran ink four key bilateral agreements
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq and Iran inked four agreements on Thursday focusing on transportation, rail connection, and municipal support, as well as government administration and human resource training.

The agreements were signed during meetings in Tehran between Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, with an emphasis on improving regional networks and collaborative work across borders, according to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Representatives from the transportation ministries of both countries signed a bilateral agreement designed to establish a structure for the international road transit of goods.

To improve rail network connectivity, the two sides signed an agreement to extend a railway connecting the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, to the Iranian city of Kermanshah. This railway will traverse the border city of Khosravi in Iran and Iraq’s Khanaqin.

Additionally, Tehran and Baghdad became sister cities after signing municipal twinning agreements and cooperative public administration training efforts.

The two countries also inked an agreement on administrative training, education, and human resource development.

The geopolitical achievement takes place as Iraq promotes an expansive economic strategy. Al-Zaidi’s visit to Tehran comes after a notable trip to the United States, where Iraq inked 48 business agreements worth over $60 billion with US corporations.

Through these diplomatic moves, Baghdad apparently aims to establish itself as a regional gateway.

World.title: Iraqi PM meets Iranian president in Tehran
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi met on Thursday with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian in Tehran, marking his first official visit to Iran since taking office.

Al-Zaidi’s reception in the Iranian capital was followed by a bilateral meeting with Pezeshkian and a joint session attended by a high-level Iraqi delegation, according to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The Iraqi prime minister proposed a diplomatic initiative focused on stabilizing the region in light of recent escalations in military operations between the United States and Iran.

Al-Zaidi said in a statement on X that he will address matters of shared interest, bilateral cooperation, regional concerns, and measures to consolidate regional security and stability.

According to al-Zaidi, Iraq and Iran have a deep connection rooted in their shared history, culture, geographic closeness, and mutual interests. This relationship highlights the importance of dialogue and collaboration in achieving sustainable development for both countries and fostering stability in the region.

The discussions reportedly centered on economic agreements, especially concerning essential shared resources like gas supplies and the declining water flows in the Tigris and Euphrates rivers.

The Iraqi delegation underscored that Iraq will stay unbiased and neutral in any foreign tensions between Tehran and Washington.

This visit takes place after al-Zaidi met with US President Donald Trump in Washington, where they inked several trade and economic deals worth billions of dollars.

Following his visit to Tehran, al-Zaidi is expected to continue his regional tour, stopping in Turkey and Saudi Arabia to discuss bilateral cooperation.

World.title: Iraq’s public debt stands at 47% of its GDP
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi prime minister’s financial advisor Mazhar Saleh told Rudaw News on Wednesday that Iraq’s total public debt is approximately 47 percent of the country’s gross domestic product (GDP).

Although Baghdad can easily handle its debt burden, the country’s dependency on revenues generated from oil exports leaves its economy exposed to various external factors.

The major issues in the Iraqi economy, according to Saleh, are its reliance on oil income, the poor performance of other productive sectors, and the growing administrative costs.

To guarantee that the Iraqi economy can survive foreign shocks, the Iraqi government is working to diversify income sources, notably in the industrial, agricultural, and service sectors, as well as reforming the tax, customs, and banking systems, according to Saleh.

In late June, the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) revealed that the country’s domestic debt rose to 95.7 trillion Iraqi dinars ($73 billion) by the end of April 2026 compared to 90.51 trillion dinars ($69.1 billion) recorded at the end of 2025, representing an increase of 5.16 trillion dinars ($3.9 billion).

In 2024, the domestic debt in Iraq stood at 83.05 trillion Iraqi dinars (approximately $63.4 billion).

According to the statistics, domestic debt increased during the first four months of 2026, while external debt dropped in comparison to prior years.

Iraq’s external debt stood at $54.101 billion in 2025, compared to $54.601 billion in 2024 and $56.207 billion in 2023, marking a total drop of $2.106 billion over two years, according to the CBI.

Senior officials in the Iraqi financial sector and representatives from Oliver Wyman, a renowned firm specializing in financial audits, emphasized the significance of developing medium-term plans customized to the nature of the debt, Iraq’s credit rating, and key global indicators.

The officials also called for drawing up budgets based on realistic evaluations of the country’s available finances and execution capabilities.

World.title: Iraqi security seizes 40 gold bars, large sums of cash in corruption case
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council revealed on Wednesday that investigations into the case of Adnan al-Jumaili, a deputy oil minister accused of corruption, have resulted in the seizure of 13 billion Iraqi dinars (nearly $10 million), $400,000, and 40 gold bars hidden in different locations in the northern province of Salah al-Din.

The step is part of the Iraqi government’s ongoing nationwide anti-corruption campaign launched last month.

The Iraqi judiciary said in a statement that each of the gold bars weighs one kilogram. It added that security forces also seized five kilograms of gold jewelry, according to the state-run news agency (INA).

The seizures resulted from ongoing investigations into the suspect, according to the statement.

Al-Jumaili’s case is one of the most prominent corruption cases that emerged in the past few months, as the government’s campaign targets people suspected of theft and wasting public funds.

Iraqi authorities had already announced al-Jumaili’s arrest on allegations of financial and administrative corruption before the judiciary opened a broad investigation into the issue, including a review of his accounts, assets, and finances.

The Supreme Judicial Council did not provide any information on the locations where the money and gold were discovered and mentioned that search and recovery efforts are ongoing.

The Iraqi cabinet affirmed that recovering public funds is one of the priorities of its agenda, while the Federal Commission of Integrity and the judiciary are working to pursue those accused both inside and outside Iraq.

World.title: Air defenses intercept 4 drones in northern Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The international coalition’s air defense systems intercepted on Wednesday evening four drones over Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The systems were activated when flying objects approached the US consulate and its associated logistics base, according to Al-Arabiya News.

Four explosions were reportedly heard in the skies over Erbil following the activation of the international coalition’s air defense systems.

A security source confirmed that air defenses successfully intercepted and destroyed the drones before reaching their targets, adding that the attack caused no casualties or material damage.

On Tuesday, Iraqi security sources said that air defenses intercepted three explosive-laden drones near the US consulate in Erbil with two drones targeting a camp of the Kurdistan Freedom Party (PAK), an Iranian Kurdish opposition group.

The state-run news agency (INA) reported that Erbil International Airport temporarily suspended flights but later announced their resumption.

Iraqi air defenses shot down an explosive-laden drone on Monday near Harir Air Base in Iraq, which houses US and international coalition forces. There were no reports of casualties or damages.

No group has claimed responsibility for the attacks. Neither Iraqi officials nor the Kurdistan Regional Government (KRG) has issued a statement identifying the attackers or the types of drones involved.

The recent escalation in Iraqi Kurdistan, which largely included drone assaults over Erbil, comes amid rising tensions between the United States and Iran, the most serious since a cease-fire deal was reached in mid-June.

World.title: US dollar rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar compared to the Iraqi dinar rose on Wednesday in the Iraqi capital, Baghdad, and the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq, Erbil.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,504 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,502.5 Iraqi dinars on Wednesday’s morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,510 Iraqi dinars and 1,500 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also rose, fluctuating between 1,508.5 and 1,507.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi proposes joint fund in call with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi held high-level telephone discussions with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Wednesday, July 22, 2026, focusing on expanding economic cooperation, trade, and industrial investment between the two nations.

According to an official statement released by the Prime Minister’s Media Office, the talks covered bilateral ties across multiple sectors, with particular emphasis on economic partnerships, trade volume expansion, direct investment, and joint migration management frameworks.

Key Discussion Pillars

Joint Iraqi-German Fund: Prime Minister Al-Zaidi proposed establishing a dedicated joint fund to finance industrial development projects in Iraq with German technical and capital backing.

Economic Reforms & Anti-Corruption: Al-Zaidi reiterated Baghdad’s commitment to eradicating administrative corruption and creating an open, transparent environment for foreign capital to diversify Iraq’s national economy.

Official Invitation to Berlin: Chancellor Merz extended a formal invitation to Prime Minister Al-Zaidi to visit Germany for an official state visit to deepen economic and political coordination.

Support for Fiscal Reform: Germany reaffirmed its support for the Iraqi government’s ongoing economic and financial reforms, expressing strong readiness from German corporations to expand investment footprints across Iraq.

The discussions highlight Baghdad’s broader diplomatic strategy of leveraging European economic integration to modernize domestic industrial infrastructure and broaden trade partnerships beyond energy exports.

World.title: Lebanon PM says Beirut working for ‘complete Israeli withdrawal’
World.content:
Zawtar al-Gharbiyah – Lebanon is working towards a “complete Israeli withdrawal” from areas it occupies, Prime Minister Nawaf Salam said on Wednesday on a visit to a village where Lebanon’s army recently deployed.

“We will continue mobilising our political and diplomatic efforts to secure a complete Israeli withdrawal from the south,” he said in Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

Israeli forces were previously present on the outskirts of the village following the war with Iran-backed Hezbollah.

Salam visited the town a day after Lebanese President Joseph Aoun met with his US counterpart Donald Trump at the White House, where he “stressed the urgent need for a full Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory”.

Under a US-sponsored agreement signed last month, Lebanon’s army is meant to disarm Hezbollah and the Israeli military is to withdraw from “pilot zones” where Lebanese forces will subsequently deploy.

Hezbollah has repeatedly rejected the agreement and refuses to lay down its weapons.

The military said on Tuesday that Israeli forces “opened fire” near troops deploying at Zawtar al-Gharbiya.

The Israeli military said it had only fired “warning shots into the air” after Lebanese soldiers entered an area that was “not part of the pilot area”.

Hezbollah drew Lebanon into the Middle East war by attacking Israel in support of Tehran on March 2, prompting major Israeli airstrikes and a ground invasion.

After planting a Lebanese flag in Zawtar al-Gharbiya on Wednesday, Salam said “in parallel with the army’s deployment, we will continue opening roads, removing rubble, and securing essential services, enabling our people to return safely and with dignity to their homes and villages”.

– ‘Heads held high’ –

The war caused widespread destruction, mainly in the south, though violence has declined since the signing of a framework agreement between the United States and Iran last month and the Lebanon-Israel deal.

According to the United Nations, more than 700,000 people have returned to their homes over the past few weeks.

In Zawtar al-Gharbiya, dozens of residents waited at the village’s entrance for permission to go check on their homes.

“We will enter the town with our heads held high, thanks to the presence of the Lebanese army,” Abbas Yaghi, 73, told AFP.

The military had told residents on Tuesday to avoid entering the village “until the security situation stabilises”.

The army is conducting a sweep of the town, which is geographically contiguous with its Israeli-occupied neighbour, Zawtar al-Shariqya.

Israeli troops still launch intermittent strikes in surrounding towns, the latest on Nabatieh al-Fawqa.

“We will follow the army if it gives us permission to enter,” Mostapha Ammar, a 60-year-old resident of Zawtar al-Sharqiya said, hoping that Israel would withdraw from other areas.

Wafaa Ismail, 64, also from Zawtar al-Sharqiya, was not granted permission to enter the neighbouring village as Salam visited.

She expressed frustration at seeing the prime minister enter on his own, escorted by the army, saying: “He should have brought the people in with him so he could claim victory.”

World.title: 'More strict actions to come against paper leaks': PM Modi announces new Bill push in video message
World.content:
Prime Minister assures students that strict action will be taken against paper leaks on Friday

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday announced that government will bring in more strict actions against paper leaks. In a late night video message, PM Modi said that the Union Cabinet will discuss these stringent measures on Friday and the government will try to get the Bill passed in Parliament next week.He assured that the Centre will bring in stricter measures to curb examination paper leaks, including provisions for fast-track courts and harsher punishments for offenders.His message comes amid massive nationwide protests against alleged irregularities in the NEET UG examination. "I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakh of students and their guardians.""Numerous effective measures have been taken in the past two and a half months since the paper leak incident. The culprits have been caught and are in jail. Our most important responsibility was to ensure that students' year is not wasted. The government used all its might to ensure that 22 lakh students could take their exams in the shortest possible time," he added.Further talking about the bill on fast track courts he added, "On the 19th July, the results were declared. I directed the departments today to establish a fast-track court. The departments presented me with the resolution late at night. This resolution, along with the provision for a fast-track court and harsh punishment, will be discussed in the cabinet tomorrow. After the suggestions of cabinet colleagues, it will be finalised, and since the second week of Parliament is starting from Monday, efforts will be made to get that bill passed in the House as soon as possible. "

World.title: CJP delegation to meet government ministers on Friday as Centre renews outreach: Report
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A delegation of the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) will meet government ministers at 12.30 pm on Friday, PTI reported, citing sources, marking the first formal engagement after days of deadlock between the Centre and the student-led outfit over the alleged NEET paper leak.

The meeting comes after repeated efforts by the government to initiate dialogue with the protesters. On Thursday, Union minister J P Nadda invited the CJP leadership for talks, but the offer was declined as the outfit insisted that any discussion should take place at a neutral venue near the protest site, according to PTI sources.

Government sources had earlier told ANI that an offer to continue talks with the CJP leadership had also been rejected, prolonging the stalemate.

CJP spokesperson Saurav Das had maintained that the group was willing to hold talks but not at a minister's residence or office. "We refused to go to anyone's house or office. The people's court is here. Ministers should come among the people. If they want to talk, it should be held at the Jantar Mantar," he had said.

Das, however, said the CJP remained open to dialogue at a neutral venue if there were security concerns.

The protests, centred at Jantar Mantar, have continued for nearly a month, with demonstrators demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, compensation for families of students who allegedly died by suicide over the NEET paper leak, and withdrawal of cases filed against peaceful protesters.

Earlier this week, representatives of the CJP met J P Nadda and submitted their demands. According to the CJP, the Union minister assured them that the issues would be discussed at the appropriate level, ANI reported.

World.title: Govt reshuffles top bureaucrats in ministries: Education secretary shifted out
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday carried out a major reshuffle in the education ministry, appointing senior

officer Naresh Pal Gangwar as secretary of the department of higher education and T K Anil Kumar as secretary of the department of school education and literacy, amid continuing protests over the alleged NEET paper leak.

According to an order issued by the Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC), Gangwar, a 1994-batch IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre, will replace Vineet Joshi as secretary of the department of higher education. Joshi, a 1992-batch IAS officer of the Manipur cadre, has been appointed secretary in the ministry of panchayati raj.

Gangwar was serving as secretary in the department of animal husbandry and dairying under the ministry of fisheries, animal husbandry and dairying.

An engineer by training, he holds a BTech in Electronics and Communication from the University of Roorkee, an MTech in Communication from IIT Delhi, and an MA in Economics from the University of Rajasthan. He has previously served in several senior positions in the Rajasthan government and the Centre, including principal secretary in Rajasthan and joint secretary in the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.





The ACC also appointed T K Anil Kumar, a 1996-batch IAS officer of the Karnataka cadre and additional secretary in the Ministry of Rural Development, as secretary of the Department of School Education and Literacy.

The government order did not cite any reason for the appointments. The reshuffle comes amid continuing protests by the

and students over the alleged irregularities in the NEET examination, with demonstrators demanding accountability and reforms in the examination system.

World.title: 400 Pakistani handles revived from Op Sindoor target NEET protests, being blocked: Delhi Police
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

on Thursday said it had identified and blocked more than 400 Pakistani social media handles allegedly spreading misinformation and rumours amid the ongoing protests, urging people not to fall for fake content circulating online.

Addressing the media, deputy commissioner of Police (DCP) Sumit Jha said the same social media accounts had also been active during Operation Sindoor and were now attempting to exploit the current situation to provoke people and distract students.

"We have noticed that some attempts are being made to spread misinformation on social media. So far, more than 400 Pakistani social media handles have been identified, which are taking advantage of this situation and spreading fake content and rumors.

They are being blocked. These are the same social media handles which were active during Operation Sindoor as well. Their only aim is to provoke people and especially divert the attention of students.

"

Jha appealed to the public, particularly students and parents, not to be influenced by unverified posts, edited videos or content shared by anonymous accounts.

"I appeal to you that for the safety of children, do not get provoked by any fake post, edited videos or any post made by anonymous handle. Fact check any post before sharing it. Do not spread rumors and do not let any anti-social elements control your emotions."

He also reiterated that the police respected citizens' right to peaceful protest.

"Remember that it is your right to hold a peaceful protest and Delhi Police respects this right."

World.title: Centre monitoring 2,485 Himalayan glacial lakes; 56 classified as 'very high risk'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday said it is monitoring 2,485 glacial lakes spread across the Himalayan river basins using remote sensing techniques. It also informed Parliament that 56 glacial lakes have been classified as 'very high risk' following a scientific assessment conducted in 2025 due to their potential to trigger Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs).

In a written reply in the Lok Sabha, jal shakti state minister Raj Bhushan Choudhary said the Central Water Commission (CWC) monitors glacial lakes larger than 10 hectares across four states and two Union Territories from June to October every year using remote sensing.

The minister said the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), in collaboration with national scientific agencies, carried out a scientific assessment of 189 high-risk glacial lakes across the Indian Himalayan Region in 2025.

"Based on the assessment, 56 glacial lakes were classified as very high risk considering their potential to trigger Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOFs) and the exposure of downstream habitations and infrastructure," Choudhary said.

He said the government has started establishing Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) Early Warning Systems (EWS) at selected high-risk glacial lakes based on hazard assessments and continuous monitoring.





However, the minister clarified that no end-to-end GLOF Early Warning System has been commissioned so far under the National GLOF Risk Mitigation Programme (NGRMP).

Choudhary said the NDMA is implementing the NGRMP, which was approved in 2024 for Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh at a cost of Rs 150 crore.

"The programme envisages Hazard and Risk Assessment, Monitoring and Early Warning Systems, site-specific structural and non-structural mitigation of measures, and community awareness and capacity building," he said.

The minister added that Rs 52.50 crore has been allocated under the Monitoring and Early Warning System component of the programme.

He also said the NDMA, along with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) and the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority (SSDMA), carried out multi-agency expeditions to the high-risk South Lhonak and Shako Cho glacial lakes in Sikkim during 2023 and 2024. The expeditions were aimed at supporting scientific studies and developing monitoring systems, early warning mechanisms and mitigation measures.

(with inputs from PTI)

World.title: 'UP ke ladke' to take on BJP again, but who will show 'bigger heart'? Seat-sharing test awaits Rahul, Akhilesh
World.content:
NEW DELHI: What does the size of oneâs heart have to do with political alliances? Perhaps quite a lot when the allies are the

and the Samajwadi Party, and at stake is the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly election.

The âUP ke ladkeâ delivered in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. The partnership between

and

helped the INDIA bloc win 43 of Uttar Pradeshâs 80 seats, handing the

BJP

its biggest electoral setback in the state in a decade.

Now, as the two parties prepare for seat-sharing negotiations for next yearâs assembly election, leaders on both sides want the other to show a âbig heartâ and be more accommodating.

The 'UP ke ladke' proved to be a winning combination in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

Akhilesh made the first appeal. At the INDIA blocâs crisis meeting on June 9, held after Mamata Banerjeeâs shock defeat in West Bengal, the SP chief had a word of advice for the Congress: âShow a large heart and be accommodative.â

The message was clear: the Congress should avoid competing with regional allies and recognise their dominance in states where they remain the principal opposition force.

With the Congress facing criticism from allies over its aggressive approach during elections, Rahul responded with an emphatic assurance: âI will bear every single humiliation that I have to bear to knit this group together and make it succeed.





What is the main issue here? I have no interest in fighting you. I would have to be a madman to suddenly get up and say I am going to fight you because you are our allies, you are our friends, you are the people we love.

â

Rahulâs conciliatory message, however, has not stopped Congress leaders in Uttar Pradesh from staking an ambitious claim. They have turned the âbig heartâ argument around, asking the SP to offer the Congress equal status, a respectable deal and, according to some leaders, 50:50 parity.

Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has argued that the SP benefited more from the alliance in 2024.

Saharanpur MP Imran Masood has claimed that the SP gained more than the Congress from their alliance in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

Congress co-incharge for Uttar Pradesh Rajesh Tiwari made a similar argument: âThe SP is keen to head the next government in the state. Hence, it should have a big heart.â

The pitch grew louder on July 2 when newly appointed Uttar Pradesh Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam said the party would enter the assembly election on the principles of âequality and respectâ.

These remarks appear far removed from Rahulâs conciliatory intervention at the INDIA bloc meeting in June. But the posturing by Congress leaders is hardly surprising. Seat-sharing has repeatedly emerged as a point of friction between the party and its regional allies.

The same tension has surfaced in several states where the Congress has attempted to balance its national ambitions with the political dominance of regional partners.

Bihar

In Bihar, the Congress and the RJD failed to finalise a seat-sharing agreement even after nominations opened for the first phase of the assembly elections. The lack of coordination was evident when Tejashwi Yadav filed his nomination papers without any senior Congress leader by his side.

The two parties eventually reached an agreement, but the delay had already exposed divisions within the Mahagathbandhan and disrupted its preparations.

Little wonder, their Mahagathbandhan was decimated by the BJP and its allies.

Haryana

In Haryana, several rounds of negotiations between the Congress and Arvind Kejriwalâs AAP failed to produce a seat-sharing agreement. The two parties could not agree on the number and choice of constituencies, while the bitterness of their rivalry in Delhi made a compromise even more difficult.

They eventually contested separately, splitting the opposition space in several constituencies.

The Congress fell short of dislodging the BJP, which returned to power for a third consecutive term.

Madhya Pradesh

But when it comes to seat sharing with Samajwadi Party, there is already a history of bitterness between the two allies. There was an open war of words between Akhilesh Yadav and the then CM face of Congress Kamal Nath, who refused to cede any ground to the Samajwadi Party in the state. This was immediately after the opposition had joined hands at the national level under the INDIA bloc banner to fight the BJP.

Despite that the Congress high command remained a mute spectator as Kamal Nath refused to budge. Kamal Nath, who was confident of victory then, announced that the INDIA bloc was only for national elections. The bitterness complicated negotiations for the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, before an intervention by senior leaders, including Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, helped rescue the partnership.

What's happening now?

Now, as the assembly elections approach, both sides have begun posturing to keep up the pressure.

Congress leaders have been more vocal, citing the partyâs national status, as they often do when dealing with regional allies.

In fact, newly appointed Congress in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam, who is supposed to oversee the partyâs campaign in UP, has gone on to claim that the SPâs success in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections was because the Congress was projected as the senior partner.

Gautam credited INDIA blocâs 2024 gains to Congressâs leadership, arguing that only Rahul Gandhi had national stature to take on BJP.

The Congress leader has also claimed that if the party is not given its due respect within the alliance, it would amount to giving the BJP a âwalkoverâ.

Interestingly, both parties are citing past results to justify their claims. The Congress points to the Samajwadi Partyâs performance in the 2014 and 2019 Lok Sabha elections to argue that its spectacular showing in 2024 was the result of its alliance with the grand old party.

The SP won five seats in 2014 when it contested alone and five in 2019 when it was allied with Mayawatiâs BSP. However, when the SP and Congress contested together in 2024, the SPâs tally rose to 37.

Congress leaders claim that this sharp increase was due to the influence of the grand old party.

Now, let us analyse the Congressâs performance in Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

The Congress has been out of power in UP since 1989. Over the last four decades, its presence in the state assembly has dwindled continuously, and the party has largely been confined to the Gandhi family bastions of Rae Bareli and Amethi. In the Lok Sabha elections, the Congress won only two seats in 2014 and one in 2019, before increasing its tally to six in 2024.

The Congress and SP contested the 2017 assembly elections in alliance but were decimated by the BJP. While the SP won 47 seats, the Congress managed only seven.

In the 2022 elections, the Congress went solo. Led by AICC general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, the party contested 399 seats, with women accounting for 40% of its candidates. Despite this, the party performed poorly and its vote share fell to 2.33%.

How the SP and Congress fared when they fought separately

The Congress managed to win only two seatsâAradhana Mishra âMonaâ from Rampur Khas in Pratapgarh district and Virendra Chaudhary from Pharenda in Maharajganj district.

It marked the partyâs worst-ever assembly election performance in Uttar Pradesh.

So, will the âUP ke do ladkeâ unite again in 2027, as they did in 2024, to stun the BJP-led NDA in Uttar Pradesh? There has been considerable bonhomie on display between Rahul Gandhi and Akhilesh Yadav. The two used their birthdays, 12 days apart, to reinforce their shared commitment to fighting the BJP. But to ensure that this bonhomie translates into electoral gains for both parties, they will have to rein in their leaders, especially those in the Congress.

When the Congress surprised everyone with a sit-in protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs residence in the national capital over the NEET issue, Akhilesh was by Rahul Gandhiâs side. The two leaders have also held a closed-door meeting in Parliament, along with Priyanka Gandhi, perhaps to work out the contours of a practical seat-sharing formula acceptable to both parties.

The stakes are higher for the SP, which is in contention to form the next government in UP and knows that support from its allies could be crucial to achieving that objective.

The Congress, with just two seats in the assembly, has little to lose in the state. However, the grand old party would do well to realise that another botched alliance experiment could isolate it further within the INDIA bloc, which it leads.

The BJP in Uttar Pradesh is going through a challenging phase amid recent controversies. But chief minister

Yogi Adityanath

is leading the fight himself and has been quick to capitalise on the reported differences between the two allies.

While Congress leaders may be making strong remarks to build pressure on Akhilesh, they should realise that this ploy carries the risk of creating a perception among voters that the two allies are fighting. And if the Congress and SP lose this perception battle, winning the election could become difficult.

Bihar has already shown how damaging such an impression can be.

The SP and Congress have already shown that they can hurt the BJP when they fight together. The challenge in 2027 will be to ensure that the fight over seats does not begin before the fight for Uttar Pradesh. Whether they can set aside competing ambitions and agree on who must show the 'bigger heart' will determine if the 'UP ke ladke' can deliver again.

World.title: Watch: Gujarat rains trigger waist-deep flooding, vehicles go under
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Around 1,200 people have been rescued and hundreds more relocated as heavy rains battered south Gujarat, with Umbergaon taluka in Valsad district receiving over 1,100 mm of rainfall in just 16 hours, officials said on Thursday.

One rain-related death was reported in Tapi district. The Indian Air Force and Coast Guard have been put on alert for rescue efforts, while NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected areas.

Valsad district was the worst hit, with many talukas receiving over 600 mm of rain during the same period. A red alert for heavy to extremely heavy rainfall was in effect for Valsad, Navsari, Surat and Tapi districts.

Floodwaters submerge vehicles, roads in Vapi

Large parts of Vapi in Valsad district were inundated, with floodwaters submerging parked vehicles and disrupting normal life.

Videos from the area showed waist-deep water in residential colonies and commercial areas, with people wading through the deluge.

The Kaveri river in Navsari rose sharply, stranding 200 people across 11 villages. They were rescued and relocated to safety. In Surat, 1,500 residents were moved from low-lying areas and waterlogged localities.

Relief operations underway, CM reviews situation

Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel visited the State Emergency Operation Centre and reviewed the situation, speaking to district collectors and instructing them to move people from vulnerable areas to safer places.





He also spoke to Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who assured all necessary assistance.

Over 300 roads were temporarily closed, more than 200 state-run bus trips were affected, and power outages were reported in many areas.

Red alert continues, rescue teams on standby

The IMD has issued a red alert for Valsad, Navsari, Dangs, Surat and Tapi for Thursday and Friday. NDRF and SDRF teams are deployed across the affected districts, with additional teams on standby in Amreli, Junagadh and Bhavnagar.

Several trains to Mumbai were cancelled or short-terminated due to rising water levels along rail routes in south Gujarat.

The state has received around 36 per cent of its annual average rainfall so far, with south Gujarat recording over 62 per cent of its seasonal average.

World.title: ‘Must be handled with empathy’: BJP veteran Murli Manohar Joshi breaks ranks, backs NEET protesters
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Veteran

leader and former Union minister Murli Manohar Joshi on Thursday extended support to students protesting over the alleged NEET paper leak, saying their concerns about the examination system are "genuine" and should be addressed with empathy rather than force.

In a rare intervention from a senior BJP figure, Joshi also criticised the police action against protesting students in Delhi earlier this week, describing it as "merciless" and warning that such use of force could alienate large sections of society from the government's vision of a Viksit Bharat.

"It is painful to see young students from different parts of the country assembled for days on the streets of New Delhi.

Their anxieties and concerns regarding the examination system are genuine and must be handled with empathy and a desire to find a lasting solution," Joshi said in a post on X.

"It is very painful to see that even young girls were brutally mishandled," he added.

Calling for a more humane approach, Joshi said, "I fervently hope that this is not treated merely as a law-and-order issue to be tackled through the use of force."





He further warned that such action "shall alienate large sections of Indian society from the national goal of Viksit Bharat."

BJP, opposition continue war of words

Joshi's remarks came amid an intensifying political confrontation over the alleged NEET paper leak and the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.

The BJP accused the

of avoiding a discussion on the issue in Parliament despite the government expressing readiness for a debate. BJP president Nitin Nabin said the opposition was "running away" from a discussion because its "double standards" would be exposed.

"The NDA government is fully prepared to hold discussions at every level on the future of students and youngsters," Nabin said, while challenging the opposition to participate in a debate on NEET and other issues concerning students.

Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman also asserted that the Centre had already taken action against those accused in the alleged paper leak and remained committed to ensuring justice for students.

She accused the Congress of pursuing "disruptive politics" instead of participating in a parliamentary discussion.

Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal appealed to the opposition not to politicise the issue, saying the government would take the "strictest possible action" against those found guilty in paper leak cases.

Earlier in the day, Prime Minister Modi issued his first public response to the ongoing agitation, announcing that the government would set up fast-track courts to ensure swift punishment for those involved in paper leak cases.

"Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared," PM Modi wrote on X.

Opposition backs students, Parliament remains deadlocked

Meanwhile, opposition parties have continued to press for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and have linked the issue to the alleged assault on student protesters.

Leader of opposition

said INDIA bloc leaders were heading to Gandhi Smriti to express solidarity with students affected by the alleged paper leak and those injured during police action.

"India's students are not alone. The entire Opposition stands with them and their demands," Gandhi wrote on X.

The Opposition has made Pradhan's resignation and a discussion under Rule 267 in the Rajya Sabha key demands before agreeing to a debate, while the government has maintained that it is willing to discuss the issue without preconditions.

The deadlock has repeatedly disrupted proceedings in both Houses of Parliament.

World.title: No evidence against Sanjeev Mukhiya in NEET-UG 2024 case: CBI
World.content:
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) on Thursday (July 23, 2026) said it did not find any evidence establishing the complicity of Sanjeev Kumar alias Sanjeev Mukhiya in the NEET-UG 2024 case. He is an accused in certain other cases being investigated by the Bihar police.

In 2024, the State police had detected the paper theft and registered a case. Prima facie suspicion had emerged at that stage against Sanjeev Mukhiya, suggesting his role, as he was found involved in certain other examination paper theft/leak cases, said the agency.

“He was accordingly named as an accused in the said FIR by the Bihar police. The case was subsequently transferred to the CBI for investigation,” it said.

The CBI said that during its investigation, each person involved in the theft and onward distribution of the stolen NEET-UG 2024 question paper were identified, as also each candidate who benefited from its use. “Multiple chargesheets have accordingly been filed by the CBI against 45 persons before the jurisdictional court in Patna,” said the agency.

“Sanjeev Mukhiya had remained absconding during the relevant time. He was subsequently arrested by the Bihar police in connection with those other cases. Since he was a named accused in the FIR in the NEET-UG 2024 case as well, the CBI took his police custody for the purpose of examination...,” it said.

As no evidence of his involvement in the NEET-UG case emerged, the CBI did not file any chargesheet against him. He accordingly availed bail in that case. “Sanjeev Mukhiya remained in judicial custody after his bail in the CBI’s case, he being an accused in certain other cases being investigated by the Bihar police,” said the CBI.

“This issue was clarified in the year 2024 itself adequately. The narrative going around now about his deliberate omission is factually incorrect,” it added.

World.title: Jantar Mantar protest LIVE: Government and CJP delegation have likely agreed to meet tomorrow, a government source says
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (July 23, 2026) took to social media to address students’ concerns on NEET paper leaks. He assured students that stricter actions against paper leaks will come in tomorrow’s Cabinet.

A delegation of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will meet with government Ministers on Friday (July 24), sources said. The meeting will take place at 12.30 pm, but its venue has not been disclosed. This comes after intense backroom negotiations to end the deadlock over the NEET paper leak, the sources said. Delhi High Court designates Judge Anu Grover Baliga as Special Judge of the fast-track court to deal with criminal cases arising out of paper leaks and the use of unfair means in public examinations.

Also read: The cockroach dilemma facing India’s political parties

Union Minister Jitendra Singh on Thursday (July 23, 2026) said that the Centre is ready for talks with the Cockroach Janta Party amid the latter’s protest in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar over paper leaks and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. However, CJP has declined the invitation and said that the talks need to happen at Jantar Mantar or at another neutral venue.

Also Read: 16 metro stations, including Rajiv Chowk, Patel Chowk, Delhi Gate and Central Secretariat, closed, says DMRC

Earlier today, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in a social media post, said that his government will set up fast-track courts for action against those involved in paper leaks. “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard. This continues our series of steps for safeguarding the interests of students. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared,” Mr. Modi said.

The CJP reacted to the announcement and said that while fast-track courts will address what happens after the paper leak, why there are paper leaks is a larger issue that the government must address.

World.title: Chairperson of Palani Municipality moves HC seeking CBI probe into fraudulent registration of Palani Math land
World.content:
Chairperson of Palani Municipality R. Uma Maheshwari Pradeep on Thursday filed a petition before the Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court, seeking a CBI probe into the case pertaining to fraudulent registration of Palani math land.

Describing herself as a devotee who had a genuine interest in the protection and preservation of the math’s properties, she said the land had been subjected to encroachment and unauthorised occupation by private individuals over the course of several decades.

Though departmental action, including suspension, was initiated against some Registration Department officials, the role of the supervisory officers and other public servants involved in the processing and registration of the document had not been effectively examined in the criminal investigation, she said.

Besides, the Division Bench of the High Court, which declared the sale deed null and void, had recorded that fraud was evident at every stage of the transaction, from preparation and presentation of the instrument to registration. “The criminal investigation must consequently extend to the complete chain of persons who prepared, financed, presented, processed, facilitated and completed the fraudulent registration. The enormous disparity between the true value of the property and the consideration recorded in the instrument raises a serious question as to whether the document reflects a genuine transaction between the parties,” she said.

She said the probe must trace the complete financial trail, including the source of ₹2 crore, banking transactions, cash withdrawals and deposits, undisclosed considerations, intermediaries, accomm- odation entries, beneficial ownership, and persons who may have funded or directed the transaction. The possibility of cash dealings, benami arrangement, informal transfer of funds or hawala transactions must be examined, she said.

“The Ministers in charge of the HR and CE and Registration departments publicly described the occurrence as a mistake, lapse or inadvertent act before completion of the investigation into the larger conspiracy. No material, preliminary report, electronic audit, financial inquiry or department finding forming the basis of such conclusion was disclosed,” she said.

The matter came up for hearing before Justice L. Victoria Gowri on Thursday under the caption ‘Numbered subject to maintainability’. The judge directed the Registry to place the matter before the appropriate bench after getting necessary orders from the Administrative Judge.

World.title: Use of force against student protesters in Tamil Nadu flayed
World.content:
Human Rights Defenders’ Alert - India (HRDA) has strongly condemned the use of force by the Tamil Nadu police against students and youth who have staged peaceful protests, demanding accountability with regard to NEET paper leak. The HRDA also demanded accountability over the paper leak.

In a press statement, national working secretary of the HRDA Henri Tiphagne said protests in Tamil Nadu must be understood in their national context. They were a reaction to attacks on protesters affiliated to the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and allied student organisations in New Delhi, where the young demonstrators raising the same demands were met with force.

At the heart of these protests, in Tamil Nadu and nationally, was one central demand: accountability. Students were calling on Union Minister for Education Dharmendra Pradhan to take responsibility for the NEET paper leak and the broader failures in the conduct of the examination, and to answer for the institutional lapses that have affected the future of lakhs of young aspirants, he said.

Students across the country, including in Tamil Nadu, had responded in solidarity, refusing to stay silent while their peers elsewhere were subjected to police action for making the same legitimate demands.

Students who organised, mobilised, and spoke up for accountability and reform in education system were, in every meaningful sense, human rights defenders. Under the 1998 UN Declaration on Human Rights Defenders, anyone who peacefully worked to promote and protect human rights, including the right to education and the right to a fair and transparent examination process, was entitled to recognition and protection, not suppression, he said.

Mr. Henri said to treat these students as law and order problems rather than as rights-holders and defenders was to fundamentally misread the moment. The right to protest peacefully was a right guaranteed to every citizen, and it did not diminish because the protester was young or a student. The Tamil Nadu Police, like every police force in the country, had a constitutional obligation to facilitate peaceful assembly, and not to suppress it.

He urged the State government to instruct the police to immediately cease all use of force, intimidation, and detention against the student protesters, to treat them as rights-holders exercising a constitutionally protected freedom, and to ensure that the legitimate demand for accountability over the NEET paper leak was heard rather than suppressed.

World.title: Muttil tree-felling case: Kerala High Court upholds cheating charges against Augustine brothers
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has refused to interfere with the order of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Chottanikkara, dismissing the discharge petition of Jose Kutty Augustine and Anto Augustine, the accused in a cheating case connected to the Muttil tree-felling case.

The cheating case had alleged that the accused deceived M.M. Aliyar of Ernakulam by selling timber which reportedly was illegally cut and transported from Meppadi Forest Range in Wayanad. Mr. Aliyar was allegedly led to believe that the timber had the requisite permits issued by the Forest department.

Mr. Augustine argued that the permit referred to by Mr. Aliyar was not required for the transportation of the timber sold and that the charges were unsustainable. Mr. Aliyar contended that he was convinced by the accused that the timber sold to him was not in any offence or violation of the procedures prescribed by law.

The court held that there was no merit in Mr. Augustine’s contentions since it was revealed during an investigation by the Forest department that the accused did not possess the right or authority to transport and sell the timber.

Justice G. Girish observed that the offence of cheating could be found prima facie from the facts of the case.

Jose Kutty Augustine and Anto Augustine, along with their brother Roji Augustine, were arrayed as key accused in the massive illegal smuggling of protected rosewood and teak trees worth ₹8 crore from the assigned lands in Muttil South in Wayanad without the permission of the Revenue department.

World.title: Kejriwal targets PM; AAP to join CJP protest today
World.content:
Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convener Arvind Kejriwal on Thursday criticised the Centre’s response to the alleged examination paper leak issue, saying Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s announcement of fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in such leaks does not address students’ concerns. The party also announced its support for a nationwide protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) on Friday demanding Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.

Addressing a press conference, Mr. Kejriwal said the government’s announcement of fast-track courts would not solve the problem or restore confidence in the examination system. “The students did not demand fast-track courts. They demanded Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation,” he said, alleging that the Centre was trying to divert attention from the issue and protect the Education Minister.

Questioning the effectiveness of fast-track courts, he said many such courts already exist but either do not function properly or take longer than regular courts to dispose of cases. He also claimed that the government had not announced any reforms to prevent future paper leaks. “There has been no announcement that gives students confidence that next year’s NEET or any other examination will not see another paper leak,” he said.

The AAP chief also criticised the government’s handling of the student protests, alleging that protesters were subjected to lathi charge and tear gas. Claiming he had met injured students at Jantar Mantar, he rued that the Prime Minister “did not express even a single word of sympathy for them”. He also questioned Mr. Modi’s silence on the alleged police action, saying, “The Prime Minister’s statement appears to be that of a defeated, directionless and arrogant person.”

Separately, AAP said it would support a nationwide protest called by the CJP on Friday over the alleged police action against students and to demand Mr. Pradhan’s resignation.

Party leader Gopal Rai said AAP workers and office-bearers across the country would join the protest without carrying party flags or banners. He appealed to party members to participate under the leadership of students and continue supporting the movement until the Education Minister resigns.

Delhi AAP president Saurabh Bharadwaj also said the party would back the nationwide protest in support of students.

World.title: Kerala High Court quashes sexual harassment case against Boby Chemmanur
World.content:
The Kerala High Court has quashed the criminal proceedings against businessman Boby Chemmanur in a sexual harassment complaint registered by a female actor.

Justice Jobin Sebastian, who was was apprised of the settlement that had been reached between the actor and Mr. Chemmanur, allowed Mr. Chemmanur’s plea to set aside the proceedings pending before the Additional District and Sessions Court, Ernakulam.

The woman actor had earlier informed the court that she was inclined to reach a settlement with Mr. Chemmanur after he made an apology through social media.

The crime was registered against Mr. Chemmanur in January 2025, after he had made sexually loaded remarks against the actor during an inaugural function. A special investigation team then arrested Mr. Chemmannur on the charges of sexual harassment, making sexually coloured remarks, and publishing or transmitting obscene material in electronic form.

World.title: Three killed in accident near Tirupachethi
World.content:
In a tragic incident, three persons, including a young advocate, who were riding a two-wheeler were killed when a speeding car hit the bike from behind near Tirupachethi toll plaza in Sivaganga district on Thursday.

Police said advocate Pandiarajan, 32, of Vadakarai in Tiruppuvanam was travelling on a two-wheeler with two of his friends — Sibi Chakravarthi, 28, and Venkatesan, 27 — riding pilion. The trio were returning home from Kaanur.

When they were approaching the toll plaza, a speeding car, proceeding from Salaigramam towards Madurai, hit the two-wheeler from behind. In the impact, all the three riders were thrown off the bike, and died on the spot.

The bodies were sent to Government Rajaji Hospital in Madurai. Preliminary inquiries revealed that the car was heading to Nagamalai Pudukottai in Madurai. The driver, Arvind Kumar, was detained for interrogation. A case has been registered.

World.title: In midnight video message, PM promises more steps to stop exam paper leaks
World.content:
Hours after he announced fast-track courts to punish those behind exam paper leaks, Prime Minister Narendra Modi broadcast a video Thursday night that a tough new law was on its way. He said he had received its draft and it would be discussed at a meeting of the Cabinet Friday.

In the video, Modi said, “Friends, I am well aware that the issue of paper leaks is not a small matter. It causes immense distress to lakhs of students and their parents. Consequently, numerous measures have been taken over the past two-and-a-half months following these incidents, and the culprits have been apprehended and are currently in jail.”

“Our primary responsibility was to ensure that the students did not lose an academic year; conducting the examinations promptly was crucial. The government mobilised all its resources to arrange for the exams of 22 lakh students to be held in the shortest possible time, and the results were declared just five or six days ago, on the 19th (of July). While news of the success and happiness of students across the country is coming in, we are not the kind of people to simply rest content with that. That is why I instructed the departments concerned today regarding the establishment of fast-track courts,” he said.



“Working tirelessly, late into the night, the departments have already submitted a draft proposal to me. This draft, which includes provisions for fast-track courts and stricter penalties, will be discussed in the Cabinet tomorrow. It will be finalised after incorporating suggestions from Cabinet colleagues, and efforts will be made to pass the Bill in the House as soon as possible, starting with the second week of the Parliament’s session this coming Monday,” he said.

More strict actions against paper leaks to come in tomorrow’s Cabinet! pic.twitter.com/NRysBukk5U — Narendra Modi (@narendramodi) July 23, 2026

Earlier in the day, the Prime Minister, in a post on X – his first public remarks on the row over examination paper leaks that have triggered protests in the heart of the Capital – said, “Nothing is more important than the welfare and future of our youth! We have decided to set up fast-track courts to ensure swift and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leaks. Have directed the concerned authorities and officials to take all necessary steps in this regard. This continues our series of steps for safeguarding the interests of students. Those who try to harm the future of our youth will not be spared.”

His remarks came amid his government’s efforts to defuse the situation arising out of the Cockroach Janta Party-led protests, now backed by the Opposition which has joined the chorus for the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.



The CJP and Opposition leaders criticised the announcement, saying it did not address their key demands for accountability and the resignation of Pradhan.

Law and Justice Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal said the government would set up fast-track courts to conduct trials of examination paper leak cases.

Speaking to The Indian Express, Meghwal said, “We have taken note of the NEET exam leak cases ongoing at the Bombay, Delhi, Calcutta, and Madhya Pradesh High Courts. We are setting up fast-track courts at these four courts for speedy trials. In the future, we will do so if any such case arises.”

He said the fast-track courts could be set up as early as this week. “There will be day-to-day hearings in the NEET cases so that the youth are given justice soon,” he said.



BJP leaders and senior ministers welcomed the decision to form fast-track courts.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah said, “The decision to expedite hearings and take stringent action against the guilty in paper leak cases through the establishment of fast-track courts by the Prime Minister is a reflection of this very commitment. This important step… against those who toy with the future of the youth due to paper leaks will prove to be a milestone.”

BJP president Nitin Nabin said the Prime Minister had said earlier and reiterated that the NDA government was “ready for any investigation” and would bring fast-track courts to ensure that those involved would not be spared.

“When Narendra Modi ji takes a sankalp (commitment), both the nation as well as the world know that it means taking this towards siddhi (completion/conclusion),” he said.



Nabin said the entire Opposition, including the Congress, was “running away from discussion, because they know that as soon as they come to the floor of the House, their double standards will be completely exposed before the people of the country and the youth”.

Health and Family Welfare Minister J P Nadda said, “To tackle a serious challenge like paper leaks, Prime Minister Modi ji’s resolve to establish fast-track courts and take the strictest action against the guilty is a clear testament to our government’s sensitivity and commitment towards the youth.”

World.title: Commonwealth Games 2026 Opening Ceremony Live Updates: Event begins, Mirabai and Lovlina India’s flag bearers
World.content:
Commonwealth Games 2026 Opening Ceremony Live: Watered down Games' to kick off on Thursday. (PTI)

All eyes will be on the Indian contingent as the watered down Commonwealth Games kicks off with the Opening Ceremony at OVO Hydro on Wednesday night. India has sent a contingent of 126 athletes, significantly lesser than the one that was sent to Birmingham for 2022. This was the result of the sport count has dropped from 17 to 10 with badminton, hockey, wrestling, table tennis, squash and cricket all excluded which might hurt India’s medal tally this time around.

With the Opening Ceremony scheduled for 12.30 AM, India have already kicked off their campaign with wins in Lawn Bowls. Putul Sonowal defeated 2023 world champion Ryan Bester of Canada in tie-break in Lawn Bowls Men’s Singles while Rupa Rani Tirkey and Pinki Singh won their Women’s Pairs opening match against Malta in tie-break.
